operations.description:
Lists every portal area (`area` is the portal key used in scopes and event names, `label` its name) with whether it needs manual approval (`sensitive`) and where your client stands (`status`). Some areas, by default Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work, are sensitive: their API calls, and the webhook events of the same area, are refused until Hub staff approve a request made by a user of your client in the Hub under API access. Use this call to show a clear message before you call such an area, instead of waiting for a `403`.

`status` is `not_required` (the area is open), `not_requested` (nothing asked yet), `pending` (a request is waiting for review), `approved` (calls and events work), `rejected` (the last request was not approved) or `revoked` (staff withdrew an earlier approval). `decided_at` is when the current state was decided and is null for `not_required`, `not_requested` and `pending`. The reason staff gave for a rejection or a withdrawal is shown to your users in the Hub and in the email, never in the API. The states match the error codes a refused call returns: `api_access_not_approved`, `api_access_pending`, `api_access_rejected` and `api_access_revoked`.

Works with any valid key, whatever its scopes, and counts against the key's hourly limit. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.summary: Show the key behind the token
operations.description:
Tells you which key a token belongs to: the Hub client id, and the key's `name`, `prefix` (its first eight characters, to recognise it), `scopes` and `expires_at`. Use it as the first call of a deployment to check that the key carries the scopes your integration needs, to show which key is configured without revealing it, or as a cheap test that a token still works (Zapier and similar tools use it as the connection test). The secret part of the key and the token's own expiry are never returned; `expires_at` is when the key expires (null if it does not), not the token.

Send the access token in the `Authorization` header. A missing header is `401 unauthenticated`; an unknown, revoked or expired token is `401 invalid_token`; the usual `403 key_inactive` and `403 ip_not_allowed` checks of the key apply. The answer is the object itself and is not wrapped in `data` (like the other authentication answers). It counts against the key's hourly limit and carries the `X-RateLimit-*` headers. No scope is needed. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.summary: Get a new token pair with a refresh token
operations.description:
Trades a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token, without sending the API key again. Use it when a call answers `401 invalid_token` because the access token expired (after one hour), or ahead of that. If the refresh token is no longer good, fall back to `POST /auth/token` with the key. Send only `refresh_token` in a JSON body; there is no `Authorization` header.

A refresh token works once. The call revokes the whole pair you used (the old access token stops working at once too) and answers with a new pair of the same lifetimes as at the exchange (3600 and 604800 seconds, so a client that keeps refreshing stays signed in without limit while its key stays valid). Store the new refresh token before you use the new access token. Two processes that refresh with the same token at the same moment cannot both win: the second gets `401 invalid_token` and must exchange the key again, so keep one refresher per pair.

Errors, in the order they are checked: `422 validation_failed` when `refresh_token` is missing, not text or longer than 100 characters; `401 invalid_token` when the token is unknown, already used, revoked or past its seven days (the answer does not say which); `403 key_inactive` when the key behind it is switched off or expired; `403 ip_not_allowed` when the key has an allowlist and the caller's address is not on it. Who may call it: anyone who holds a refresh token; no scope is needed. Not idempotent and not counted against the hourly limit of the key.

Rate limit: 10 calls a minute for each caller address (the limit is not keyed to the token, so every refresh from one address shares it), then `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

refresh_token.description: The `refresh_token` of the pair you hold (up to 100 characters). It works once: this call revokes it together with its access token, so store the new refresh token from the answer. An unknown, used, revoked or expired token is `401 invalid_token`.

operations.description:
Ends the session of the token you send: the access token in the `Authorization` header and the refresh token that came with it both stop working at once. Use it when a token may have leaked, when a worker that held it is retired, or when a session ends. Nothing is sent in the body. The answer is `{ "status": "revoked" }` and is not wrapped in `data`.

Only this pair is revoked. The API key is untouched, so you can exchange it again with `POST /auth/token`, and other pairs made from the same key keep working. To stop a key altogether, switch it off, delete it or regenerate it on the Developer page. Calling revoke twice with the same token answers `401 invalid_token` the second time, because a revoked token is no longer accepted anywhere. A missing header is `401 unauthenticated`. The call counts against the key's hourly limit, needs no scope and is not idempotent in the `Idempotency-Key` sense (repeating it simply fails as above).

operations.summary: Exchange an API key for a token pair
operations.description:
Trades your API key for a short-lived access token and a longer-lived refresh token. It is the first call of every integration and the only sign-in call there is: one exchange serves every portal the key has scopes for (there are no token routes under the portals), and the portals themselves are chosen by the scopes of the key, not by anything you send here. Send only `api_key` in a JSON body (the `hbk_` key from the Developer page of Hub, 52 characters). There is no `Authorization` header and no client id.

The answer is a `token_type` of `Bearer`, an `access_token` valid for `expires_in` seconds (3600, one hour) and a `refresh_token` valid for `refresh_expires_in` seconds (604800, seven days) that can be used once. Both are opaque random strings of 80 characters; Hub keeps only a hash of each, so a lost token cannot be shown again. Send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every other call. Each exchange makes a new, independent pair: earlier pairs stay valid until they expire or are revoked, and there is no limit on how many are live. Keep one pair per process and renew it with `POST /auth/refresh` rather than exchanging the key on every call.

Who may call it: anyone who holds a key; no scope is needed, and the scopes of the key are not checked here (they are checked on every call that uses the token). The checks run in this order: `422 validation_failed` when `api_key` is missing, not text or longer than 100 characters; `401 invalid_credentials` when no key matches (a revoked or regenerated key is unknown too); `403 key_inactive` when the key is switched off or past its expiry; `403 ip_not_allowed` when the key has an IP allowlist and the caller's address is not on it. A successful exchange records the key's last-used time. The call is not idempotent (it never takes `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat just makes another pair) and it does not count against the key's hourly limit.

Rate limit: 10 calls a minute for each caller address and key value together, then `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`; this limit is separate from, and much tighter than, the hourly limit of the key.

api_key.description: Your API key: `hbk_` followed by 48 random characters (52 in all), shown once when the key was created or regenerated on the Developer page of Hub. Up to 100 characters are accepted. Exchange it once, keep the tokens, and renew with the refresh token. An unknown, revoked or regenerated key is `401 invalid_credentials`.

operations.description:
Lists the appraisal types that can be booked, each with its id, name, description, list price including VAT and the price your account pays. The `id` is the `appraisal_type_id` of `POST /bookings`. Only active types are listed. The list is short and fixed, so one page holds every type; `page`, `per_page` and `sort` (`name`) work as on every list. Prices are integer pence with a `currency` field.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description:
Books an appraisal for a Hub candidate. Send the `appraisal_type_id` (from `GET /appraisal-types`), the `candidate_ref`, who pays and how (`pay_option`), the agency contact and your confirmation that the candidate knows about the video call and the photo ID requirement. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, so create the person first with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates`; a candidate with no name, email or phone number in Hub is a `422` on `candidate_ref` unless you send `phone`. There is no slot to hold or choose: the booking starts at `appraisal_status` `pending_docs`, the candidate completes the documentation and then books a slot themselves, and `start_date` stays null until they do.

With `credits`, `balance` or `invoice` the booking is confirmed and paid at once (`booking_status` `booked`): one credit of the type is taken, or the appraisal's price is taken from the booking money balance, or nothing is taken now and the appraisal is invoiced by Healthier Business. The candidate is emailed a request to complete the documentation, the agency contact is told the booking is awaiting the candidate, and Healthier Business's bookings mailbox is notified. With `candidate_pays` the booking stays `pending` and `paid_by` is `candidate`: the candidate is emailed a payment link, the answer carries the same link as `payment_url`, and nothing is taken from your account. In every case the webhook event `clinical-appraisals.booking.created` is sent when the booking is made, and `clinical-appraisals.booking.confirmed` follows when a card payment is received later. A login on the appraisals portal is created for the candidate's email and for the agency's email when they do not have one, with a random password nobody knows; the person gets in through the signed links in the booking emails or the portal's password reset.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original booking with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books and charges nothing twice; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key a retry books again, and charges again.

Refusals. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details` (for example `candidate_ref`, `agency_contact_email`, or `video_call_awareness`). `422 booking_refused` is a business refusal with a message: the appraisal type cannot be found or is not active, or the way of paying is not available to your account (no credit for the type, a balance that does not cover the price, no invoice terms). A short balance is therefore refused, never answered with `402`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:write`; because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give it `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read` to read the booking afterwards. The booking holds the candidate's personal data (name, email and phone), which later answers return.

credits.description: With pay_option `credits` one credit of the appraisal type is taken by this call; with `balance` the appraisal price is taken from the booking money balance; with `invoice` nothing is taken now; with `candidate_pays` nothing is taken from the account. A way of paying the account cannot afford is refused with `422 booking_refused`, never `402`, and nothing is charged.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /bookings`: books an appraisal for a Hub candidate. There is no slot to hold or choose: the candidate completes
the documentation and books a slot afterwards. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, not
from this body (`phone` can fill a missing phone number). The service that creates the booking validates the details
again after these rules.

appraisal_type_id.description:
The appraisal type to book: an `id` from `GET /appraisal-types`. A type that does not exist or is not active is
`422 booking_refused`.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate to book: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of
your candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref` (never a 404). The candidate needs a name, an email address
and a phone number in Hub (the phone can be sent in `phone` instead), otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref`.

phone.description:
The phone number to put on the booking. Needed only when the Hub candidate has no phone number; when it is sent it
is used instead of the number held in Hub. At most 50 characters.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role, kept on the booking. At most 255 characters. Optional.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

pay_option.description:
Who pays and how. `credits` takes one credit of the appraisal type now; `balance` takes the appraisal's price from
the booking money balance now; `invoice` (or `inv`) adds it to your invoice and takes nothing now;
`candidate_pays` leaves the payment to the candidate, who is emailed a payment link (the booking stays `pending`
until they pay, and the answer carries `payment_url`). A way of paying that is not available to your account (no
credit, balance too low, no invoice terms) is `422 booking_refused`. Card payment by the agency is not offered
through the API.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your agency who made the booking. At most 255 characters.

agency_contact_email.description:
The email address of that person. The agency's emails about the booking (it is awaiting the candidate's
documentation, and the later steps) go to this address.

agency_email.description:
The agency's own email address kept on the booking. Optional; when it is left out the account's notification email
(`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used, and when that is empty the account's main email.

video_call_awareness.description:
Your confirmation that the candidate knows the appraisal is held as a video call. It must be `true`; anything else
is a `422` on this field.

photo_id_awareness.description:
Your confirmation that the candidate knows they must show photo ID at the appraisal. It must be `true`; anything
else is a `422` on this field.

schema.title: CaStoreBookingBody

operations.description:
Returns the appraisal's evaluation report as a PDF attachment (`appraisal-evaluation-{id}.pdf`): the candidate, the past and next objectives with the appraiser's comments, the summaries, the met or not met checks and the appraiser. It is built on demand from the candidate's answers and the appraiser's evaluation, and exists from the stage `evaluation_submitted` onwards (`evaluation_report_available` is true in the booking). Before that the answer is `422 report_not_available`. There is no webhook event for it: read the booking's `appraisal_status` to find out when it is ready.

The report is a sensitive personal record of the candidate. Stream it to the person who needs it, do not log it, and keep it only as long as you have to. A booking that is not yours answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Lists the account's appraisal bookings, by default the newest first. Each row is a booking as `GET /bookings/{id}` returns it. Abandoned bookings (a card payment that was never completed) are not listed.

Filters: `status` (the booking's state, such as `pending`, `booked` or `cancelled`; send the parameter more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; a value that matches no booking returns an empty page), `appraisal_status` (one or several of `pending_docs`, `docs_submitted`, `slot_booked`, `in_progress`, `evaluation_submitted`, `report_ready`, `completed`, `cancelled`; values that are not an appraisal status are ignored), `appraisal_type_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be one of your Hub candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; a booking matches by the candidate it belongs to, or, when it has no candidate link, by the candidate's email address), `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the booking was made) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first), `start_date` and `status`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Use it to follow each appraisal through its stages and to find those whose `evaluation_report_available` is true. The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The rows carry the candidate's name, email and phone as entered on the booking: personal data.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `start_date`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters: part of the candidate's first name, last name or email address on the booking.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings in this state: `pending`, `booked` or `cancelled`. Send the parameter more than once (`status[]=booked&status[]=pending`) to match several. A value that matches no booking gives an empty page.

parameters.name: appraisal_status
parameters.description: Only bookings at this stage: `pending_docs`, `docs_submitted`, `slot_booked`, `in_progress`, `evaluation_submitted`, `report_ready`, `completed` or `cancelled`. Send the parameter more than once to match several. Values that are not a stage are ignored.

parameters.name: appraisal_type_id
parameters.description: Only bookings of this appraisal type: an `id` from `GET /appraisal-types`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A booking with no candidate link is matched by the candidate's email address.

operations.description:
Returns one booking in full: the candidate (`candidate_ref`, and the name, email and phone entered on the booking), the appraisal type, the appraiser when one has been assigned, the start and end time (null until the candidate has booked a slot), the appraisal stage and its label, the booking and payment statuses, who pays, and whether the evaluation report can be downloaded. `{booking}` is the booking id. A booking that does not exist, that is abandoned, or that belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`. The payment link of a `candidate_pays` booking is only in the answer of `POST /bookings`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns what the account can pay for appraisals with: `booking_credits` lists the credits held for one appraisal type each (credits of a type pay only for that type), and `booking_money_balance_pence` is the booking money balance in pence. A type that holds no credits is not listed. When you book with `pay_option` `credits`, one credit of the appraisal type is taken; with `balance`, the appraisal's price is taken from the money balance.

Credits and money cannot be bought through the API: the answer only reports the balances. Use it before `POST /bookings` to see whether `credits` or `balance` will be accepted; a short balance is refused with `422 booking_refused`, not charged.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the movements of the account's credit wallets and of its booking money balance, newest first by default: each deposit (credits or money added) and each withdrawal (an appraisal paid for). A credit movement has `amount` (a number of credits); a money movement has `amount_pence` and `currency` and `amount` is null. `type` says the direction.

Filters: `wallet` is an appraisal type id or `booking_balance`; `type` is `deposit` or `withdraw`; `created_from` and `created_to` bound the date of the movement. `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first) and `id`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only movements made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only movements made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: an appraisal type id (`2`) for the credits of that type, or `booking_balance` for the money balance.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only deposits (`deposit`, a wallet grew) or only withdrawals (`withdraw`, a wallet shrank).

operations.description:
Returns the Clinical Appraisals account that the API key belongs to: the Hub client id, the account name, its main contact, its email addresses and whether the account is active. Use it once after connecting to check that the key points at the account you expect, and to read `notify_email`, the address a booking uses as its `agency_email` when you do not send one.

The key needs the scope `clinical-appraisals:account:read`, and the client must have Clinical Appraisals switched on, otherwise the answer is `403 portal_unavailable`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The profile holds no candidate data and no balance; read the balance with `GET /credits`.

Cancels a confirmed interview. The answer is the booking (`booking_status` `cancelled`) plus two fields: `refund_eligible` and `late_cancellation`, which tell you what the cancellation cost. With 24 hours' notice or more the cancellation is free (`late_cancellation` false, `refund_eligible` true): a credit or booking money taken for the interview is given back, a card payment is refunded and an invoiced interview is left off the invoice. Under 24 hours before the start it is a late cancellation (`late_cancellation` true, `refund_eligible` false): nothing is given back and an invoiced interview is still invoiced.

The slot becomes free, the candidate, the agency contact and the interviewer are emailed (the candidate also gets a text message), the interview is removed from the interviewer's calendar, and the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.cancelled` is sent with `cancelled_at`. Only a booking that is paid, confirmed, not yet started and in the future can be cancelled; otherwise the answer is `422 cancel_refused` with the reason in `message`. A booking that is already `cancelled` is returned as it is with `200`, without the two extra fields and without sending anything again, so repeating the call is safe. A booking that is not yours answers `404 not_found`.

This call takes no `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Books the interview of a Hub candidate in the slot you hold with `POST /timeslots/hold`. Send the `hold_hash`, the `candidate_ref`, how you pay (`pay_option`) and the agency contact; the candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub candidate, so create the person first with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates`. A candidate with no name, email or phone number in Hub is a `422` on `candidate_ref` unless you send `phone`. The interview type and the time are those of the hold.

The booking is confirmed and paid at once (`booking_status` `booked`, `pay_status` `completed`) and the answer is `201` with the booking. With `pay_option` `credits` one credit is taken now, with `balance` the interview's price is taken from the booking money balance now, and with `invoice` nothing is taken now and the interview is invoiced by Healthier Business. The hold is used up. The candidate and the agency contact are emailed a confirmation (the candidate's text message is sent as well), Healthier Business's bookings mailbox is notified, the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.created` is sent, and an interviewer is assigned afterwards, so `interviewer` is null in the answer until then.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original booking with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books nothing twice; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key a retry would find the hold already used and answer `422 booking_refused`.

Refusals. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details` (for example `candidate_ref`, `agency_contact_email`, or `booking_fields.field_9` for an unanswered booking question). `422 booking_refused` is a business refusal with a message: the hold is unknown or has expired, the way of paying is not available to your account (no credit for the type, a balance that does not cover the price, no invoice terms), or the interview type cannot be found. A short balance is therefore refused, never answered with `402`. `403 client_restricted` means the account is restricted and cannot book.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:write`; because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give it `clinical-interviews:bookings:read` to read the booking afterwards. The booking holds the candidate's personal data (name, email and phone), which later answers return.

credits.description: With pay_option `credits` one credit is taken from this call (the credits of the interview type first, then a pool that covers it, then the all-types credits); with `balance` the interview price is taken from the booking money balance; with `invoice` nothing is taken now. A way of paying the account cannot afford is refused with `422 booking_refused`, never `402`, and nothing is charged.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /bookings`: books a held slot for a Hub candidate. The candidate's name, email and phone come from the Hub
candidate, not from this body (`phone` can fill a missing phone number). The booking questions the client or Healthier
Business has set up for the interview type are answered in `booking_fields`; the service that creates the booking
validates those answers after these rules.

hold_hash.description:
The hold to book: the `hold_hash` returned by `POST /timeslots/hold`. It must be a hold of your account that has not
run out; a hold that is unknown or expired is `422 booking_refused`. The hold is used up by the booking.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate to book: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`/api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of
your candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref` (never a 404). The candidate needs a name, an email address
and a phone number in Hub (the phone can be sent in `phone` instead), otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref`.

phone.description:
The phone number to put on the booking. Needed only when the Hub candidate has no phone number; when it is sent it
is used instead of the number held in Hub. At most 50 characters.

job_role.description: The candidate's job role, kept on the booking and shown in the report. At most 255 characters. Optional.

nmc_number.description: The candidate's NMC registration number, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

nursing_band.description: The candidate's nursing band, kept on the booking. At most 50 characters. Optional.

pay_option.description:
How you pay for the interview. `credits` takes one credit now (the credits of the interview type first, then a
pool that covers it, then the all-types credits); `balance` takes the interview's price from the booking money
balance now; `invoice` (or `inv`) adds it to your invoice and takes nothing now. A way of paying that is not
available to your account (no credit, balance too low, no invoice terms) is `422 booking_refused`. Card payment
is not offered through the API.

agency_contact_name.description:
The name of the person at your agency who made the booking. At most 255 characters. The interview emails to the
agency are addressed to this contact.

agency_contact_email.description:
The email address of that person. The agency's booking confirmation and its later emails (reschedule, cancellation,
outcome) go to this address.

agency_email.description:
The agency's own email address kept on the booking. Optional; when it is left out the account's notification email
(`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used.

agency_contact_cc.description:
Extra addresses that receive a copy of the agency's emails, separated by single commas: at most 10 distinct, valid
addresses and 500 characters. A stray comma or an invalid address is a `422` on this field. Optional.

booking_fields.description:
Answers to the booking questions set up for the interview type, as an object keyed `field_{question id}` (for
example `{"field_9": "Yes"}`). A question that is required (or required because of another answer) and is not
answered is a `422` on `booking_fields.field_{id}`. An answer to a radio or select question must be one of its
options. The questions are the ones shown on the Hub booking page; the API does not list them. Leave it out when
the interview type has no required questions.

schema.title: CiStoreBookingBody

operations.description:
Returns the interview outcome report as a PDF attachment (named `{candidate name} OUTCOME.pdf`): the candidate and photo ID details, the interviewer's questions with their answers and notes, the outcome, and the signatures. It is built on demand from the interview's data. It exists once the interview is completed (`interview_report_available` is true in the booking); before that the answer is `422 report_not_available`. When Healthier Business's data retention setting stops handing out old outcome PDFs, a report older than the retention period (counted from the interview date) answers `410 report_expired`. Listen for the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.interview_report_available` to know when the interviewer has submitted the report.

The report is a sensitive personal record of the candidate. Stream it to the person who needs it, do not log it, and keep it only as long as you have to. A booking that is not yours answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Lists the account's interview bookings, by default the latest interview first. Each row is a booking as `GET /bookings/{id}` returns it. Abandoned bookings (a card payment that was never completed) are not listed.

Filters: `status` (`pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`; send the parameter more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; a value that is not a status is ignored), `interview_status` (one or several of `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `no_show`, `incomplete`), `interview_type_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be one of your Hub candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; a booking matches by the candidate it belongs to, or, when it has no candidate link, by the candidate's email address), `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (the day of the interview), `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the booking was made; each is a UK calendar day when it is a date alone, an exact instant when it has a time with `Z` or an offset, and UTC when it has a time with no offset), `upcoming=true` (confirmed bookings that have not started yet), `past=true` (bookings whose start has passed) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `start_date` (the default, latest first), `created_at` and `status`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Use it to reconcile your own records, and use the webhook events (`clinical-interviews.booking.*`) to hear about changes as they happen. The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The rows carry the candidate's name, email and phone as entered on the booking: personal data.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `start_date`, `created_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-start_date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters: part of the candidate's first name, last name or email address on the booking.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only interviews on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset (`2026-10-01T09:00:00Z`) is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only interviews on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it, to the end of that day in UK time; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time (an hour before midnight UTC in summer); a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only bookings made on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings with this status: `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`. Send the parameter more than once (`status[]=booked&status[]=pending`) to match several. Values that are not a status are ignored.

parameters.name: interview_status
parameters.description: Only bookings whose interview is in this state: `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `no_show` or `incomplete`. Send the parameter more than once to match several.

parameters.name: interview_type_id
parameters.description: Only bookings of this interview type: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A booking with no candidate link is matched by the candidate's email address.

parameters.name: upcoming
parameters.description: `true` returns only confirmed bookings (`booked` or `rescheduled`) whose interview has not started yet.

parameters.name: past
parameters.description: `true` returns only bookings whose interview start time has passed, whatever their status.

operations.description:
Moves a confirmed interview to another free slot, given as UK local `date` and `time` (take them from `GET /timeslots` for the booking's interview type). You do not hold the new slot first: it is checked again and taken in one step, so two callers cannot get the same slot. The answer is the booking, with `booking_status` `rescheduled`.

A reschedule clears the interviewer and queues a new assignment (so `interviewer` is null until one is assigned), sets the interview back to `scheduled` and clears `attendance`. It removes the interview from the old interviewer's calendar and tells them, emails the candidate and the agency contact the new time, and sends the webhook event `clinical-interviews.booking.rescheduled` with `previous_start_date`. Only a booking that is paid, confirmed (`booked` or `rescheduled`), not yet started and in the future can be moved.

Notice and cost. With 24 hours' notice or more a move is free. Under 24 hours' notice a move counts as a late cancellation plus a new booking: a booking paid with credits has one free late reschedule (a new credit is taken now and given back when the new interview is completed within 4 weeks of the original date; a second late move stays charged), a booking paid from the money balance is charged again, and an invoiced booking is invoiced again. The charge is taken after the interview has moved and never undoes the move. A card booking (made in Hub, not through the API) cannot be moved under 24 hours' notice: the answer is `422 late_reschedule_not_allowed` and the booking has to be cancelled and booked again.

Errors. `409 slot_taken` means the new slot cannot be booked (it has just been taken, including in the moment of the move, is before the interview type's minimum notice, or no interviewer is free). `422 reschedule_refused` carries the reason in `message` when the booking cannot be moved (it is unpaid, closed, already started or finished, or in the past). `422 late_reschedule_not_allowed` is described above. `404 not_found` is a booking that is not yours. A `date` and `time` that do not exist in UK local time (the hour that is skipped when the clocks go forward) are a `422` on `time`.

Repeating the call is safe. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original answer with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and moves, charges and sends nothing again; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without a key it is safe as well: when the booking is already in the slot you ask for, the answer is `200` with the booking as it is (its status stays as it was), the interviewer is not cleared, no email or webhook event is sent, and nothing is charged. A call that is repeated at the same moment as the first is held back until the first has finished and then finds the booking in the slot.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:write`.

credits.description: Free with 24 hours' notice or more. Under 24 hours' notice a late reschedule is charged as a new booking: a credit booking has one free late reschedule (a new credit is taken now and returned when the new interview is completed within 4 weeks of the original date), later late moves keep the new credit, a balance booking is charged the interview price again and an invoice booking is invoiced again. The charge never blocks the move and never answers `402`: a balance booking is charged the interview price even when the booking money balance is short, so the balance can go below zero, and a credit booking takes a credit even when none is left (as in the Clinical Interviews portal). A repeated call that finds the booking already in the slot charges nothing.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /bookings/{id}/reschedule`: the new slot. Take `date` and `time` from a row of `GET /timeslots` for the booking's
interview type; both are UK local time. A reschedule does not take a hold: the slot is checked and taken in one step.

date.description: The new day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time: the `date` of a free slot from `GET /timeslots`.

time.description: The new start time, `HH:MM` (24 hour clock), in UK local time: the `time` of a free slot from `GET /timeslots`.

schema.title: CiRescheduleBookingBody

operations.description:
Returns one booking in full: the candidate (`candidate_ref`, and the name, email and phone entered on the booking), the interview type, the interviewer when one has been assigned, the start and end time, the booking, interview and payment statuses, whether it can still be rescheduled or cancelled, and whether the interview report can be downloaded. `{booking}` is the booking id. A booking that does not exist, that is abandoned, or that belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`.

Poll it only for a single booking you are waiting on; for the whole account use `GET /bookings` or, better, the webhook events. The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns what the account can pay for interviews with, in the order a booking spends it. `booking_credits` lists the credits held for one interview type each; `interview_type_group_credits` lists the credit pools, which are credits that pay for any of several interview types; `all_interview_types_credits` is the number of credits that pay for any type; and `booking_money_balance_pence` is the booking money balance in pence. A type or pool that holds no credits is not listed. When you book with `pay_option` `credits`, one credit is taken from the narrowest credits that have one: those of the interview type, then a pool that covers it, then the all-types credits.

An account that uses another client's credits sees that client's credit balances here. Credits and money cannot be bought through the API: the answer only reports the balances. Use it before `POST /bookings` to see whether `credits` or `balance` will be accepted; a short balance is refused with `422 booking_refused`, not charged.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the movements of the account's credit wallets and of its booking money balance, newest first by default: each deposit (credits or money added) and each withdrawal (an interview paid for, or a charge). A credit movement has `amount` (a number of credits); a money movement has `amount_pence` and `currency` and `amount` is null. `type` says the direction, and `booking_id` names the booking the movement was made for when there is one.

Filters: `wallet` is an interview type id, `all` (the credits that pay for any type), a credit pool key (see `interview_type_group_credits` in `GET /credits`) or `booking_balance`; `type` is `deposit` or `withdraw`; `created_from` and `created_to` bound the date of the movement (a date alone is a UK calendar day; a time with `Z` or an offset is an exact instant; a time with no offset is UTC). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first) and `id`; prefix it with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). An account that uses another client's credits sees that client's credit movements made for its own bookings, plus its own money movements.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only movements made on or after this date or time. A date (`2026-10-01`) is a UK calendar day and means the start of that day in UK time (an hour before midnight UTC in summer); a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only movements made on or before this date or time. A date (`2026-10-31`) is a UK calendar day and includes all of it; a date and time with a `Z` or an offset is that exact instant; a date and time with no offset is read as UTC. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: an interview type id (`3`), `all` for the credits that pay for any type, the key of a credit pool (`non_doctor`), or `booking_balance` for the money balance.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only deposits (`deposit`, a wallet grew) or only withdrawals (`withdraw`, a wallet shrank).

operations.description:
Lists the interview types that can be booked, each with its id, name, list price including VAT, the price your account pays, and how long one interview lasts. The `id` is the `interview_type_id` of `GET /timeslots` and of `POST /timeslots/hold`. Only active types are listed. The list is short and fixed, so one page holds every type; `page`, `per_page` and `sort` (`name`) work as on every list. Prices are integer pence with a `currency` field.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description:
Returns the Clinical Interviews account that the API key belongs to: the Hub client id, the account name, its main contact, its email addresses and whether the account is active. Use it once after connecting to check that the key points at the account you expect, and to read `notify_email`, the address a booking uses as its `agency_email` when you do not send one.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:account:read`, and the client must have Clinical Interviews switched on, otherwise the answer is `403 portal_unavailable`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The profile holds no candidate data and no balance; read the balance with `GET /credits`.

Keeps one free slot for your account for a few minutes (5 by default; the answer states `expires_in_seconds` and `expires_at`) so that nobody else can book it while you complete the booking. The answer is `201` with the `hold_hash`, which `POST /bookings` takes to book the slot. Nothing is booked, charged, emailed or sent as a webhook by a hold. When the hold runs out it is dropped and the slot is free again; a hold that has run out cannot be booked.

An account holds one slot at a time. While a hold is open, a second hold answers `409 hold_exists` and puts the existing hold (`hold_hash`, `expires_at`, `slot`) in `details`, so you can carry on with it or release it with `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}`. Holds are also limited per account and per internet address: too many open holds answer `429 client_limit` or `429 ip_limit`, opening slots too quickly answers `429 too_fast`, and an address that Healthier Business has blocked answers `403 blocked`. A slot that is no longer free, an interview type that is not available and any other refusal answer `422 hold_refused`. A restricted account answers `403 client_restricted`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and the same body within 24 hours returns the original hold with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of answering `409 hold_exists` against its own hold. The key and the body must match exactly; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:holds:write`. Because a `:write` scope does not include its `:read` scope, also give the key `clinical-interviews:catalogue:read` to find slots.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: `POST /timeslots/hold`: the slot to hold. Take `date` and `time` from a row of `GET /timeslots`; both are UK local time.

interview_type_id.description:
The interview type to hold a slot for: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`. An id that does not exist is a `422` on
this field.

date.description: The day of the slot, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time: the `date` of a row of `GET /timeslots`.

time.description: The start time of the slot, `HH:MM` (24 hour clock), in UK local time: the `time` of a row of `GET /timeslots`.

schema.title: CiHoldTimeslotBody

operations.description:
Lists the free start times of one interview type as UK local `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and `time` (`HH:MM`) pairs, earliest first by default (`sort` accepts `date` and `time`; prefix it with `-` for descending). `interview_type_id` is required. By default the slots of the next 2 months are returned; `months_ahead` (1 to 12) widens or narrows that, and `date` limits the answer to one day. Pass the `date` and `time` of a row to `POST /timeslots/hold` to keep the slot while you book it.

A listed slot is not reserved: another booking, or another hold, can take it before you hold it, in which case the hold answers `422 hold_refused`. A slot is listed when an interviewer is free for the whole interview, and no slot is listed that starts sooner than the interview type's minimum notice from now. The list is computed on every call and is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25); a 2 month window holds many rows, so page through it or ask for one `date`. An unknown `interview_type_id` is a `422` on that field.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is held, changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `date`, `time`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: interview_type_id
parameters.description: The interview type to list slots for: an `id` from `GET /interview-types`. Required. An id that does not exist is a `422` on this field.

parameters.name: months_ahead
parameters.description: How many months ahead to look, 1 to 12. Default 2.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Only slots on this day, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in UK local time.

operations.description:
Gives a held slot back before it runs out, for example when the candidate changes their mind. `{hash}` is the `hold_hash` of `POST /timeslots/hold`. The slot is free again at once. The answer is `{ "data": { "hold_hash", "released": true } }`. A hash that does not exist, has already been released or used by a booking, or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`, so releasing twice is safe to treat as done. A hold is also released by booking it and by running out, so you only need this call to free a slot you will not book. Nothing is charged, emailed or sent as a webhook.

The key needs the scope `clinical-interviews:holds:write`.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: The hold token returned when the place or timeslot was held.

operations.description: Marks one alert as handled: `acknowledged` becomes true and `acknowledged_at` is set to now. Nothing else happens: no email or webhook is sent and no check is run, and the worker is not changed. Acknowledging an alert that is already acknowledged is not an error and leaves its original `acknowledged_at`. The call returns the alert. An alert of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:write` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:write`.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: The alert id (integer).

operations.description: Acknowledges open alerts of the portal in one call. Send `ids` (up to 500 alert ids) to acknowledge those; send `type` to acknowledge every open alert of that type; send neither to acknowledge **every open alert of the portal**, so send an explicit `ids` or `type` unless that is what you mean. When `ids` is sent, `type` is ignored. Only open alerts of this portal and your account count: ids that do not exist, belong to another client or to the other portal, or are already acknowledged are skipped without an error. The answer is how many were acknowledged (`acknowledged_count`, possibly 0). No email or webhook is sent and nothing is checked or billed. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for more than 500 ids or an id that is not an integer. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:write` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:write`.

ids.description: The alert ids to acknowledge, up to 500, from `GET /alerts`. When present and not empty it decides which alerts are acknowledged and `type` is ignored.

type.description: An alert type: every open alert of this type in the portal is acknowledged (for example `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`). Ignored when `ids` is sent.

operations.description:
Lists the alerts of your account for this portal, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Registration Monitoring lists registration alerts (every type that does not start with `dbs_` or `rtw_`); DBS & Right To Work lists the `dbs_` and `rtw_` alerts. Acknowledged alerts are included: filter with `acknowledged=false` for the ones that still need a person, which is what a work queue should read. Further filters are `severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`), `type` (an exact alert type, see `type` of an alert), `worker_id` and `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the alert was raised). `sort` orders by `created_at`, `severity` or `type`; the default is newest first.

Where alerts come from: each completed registration check that changes a worker's status, the first check of a worker, and a change of a regulator warning or condition flag raise one; the DBS Update Service raises one when a certificate shows new information or a non-blank certificate is found; the right to work check raises one when the result is no right to work, when a passport image cannot be verified or has a low authenticity score, and when a share code is invalid; and the expiry reminders raise right to work and share code alerts as an expiry approaches. A DBS or right to work alert also sends the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. A DBS certificate number in an alert's text is always masked (only the last four characters show, for example `********7890`). The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `severity`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: acknowledged
parameters.description: `false` returns only open alerts (the ones that still need a person), `true` only acknowledged ones. Left out, both are returned. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Only alerts of this severity: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only alerts of this exact type, for example `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`. See `type` of an alert for the types of this portal. At most 100 characters; a value that is not a type returns an empty list.

parameters.name: worker_id
parameters.description: Only alerts about this worker: a worker id from `GET /workers`.

operations.description: Returns one alert of your account in this portal, with the worker it is about and, for a registration alert, the check that raised it. An alert of another client, or of the other portal (a DBS alert asked for in Registration Monitoring, for example), is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: The alert id (integer).

operations.description: Lists the account's monthly bills, newest period first, 25 to a page by default. A bill that is still a draft is never shown; every other status is (`generated`, `amended`, `ready_for_collection`, `submitted_to_gocardless`, `paid`, `failed`, `cancelled`). Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`. `period_from` and `period_to` filter by the month the bill covers, and `sort` orders by `period_start` or `id`. Bills are read only here: the invoice PDF is `GET /billing/bills/{id}/invoice`, and payment is by Direct Debit set up in Hub. Both monitoring portals list the same bills. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `period_start`, `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-period_start`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: period_from
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `period_to`.

parameters.name: period_to
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `period_from`.

operations.description: Streams the invoice of one bill as a PDF named after the bill number (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). Only bills that are shown in `GET /billing/bills` have an invoice (a draft bill, a bill of another client, or an unknown id is `404 not_found`). It is the same invoice Hub gives you. Nothing is changed, sent or billed by the download. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

parameters.name: bill
parameters.description: The bill id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns what the account's monitoring costs. There are no per check or per credit charges in Registration Monitoring and DBS & Right To Work: one monthly subscription covers registration, DBS and right to work monitoring, and every active worker (a registration, a DBS-only or a right-to-work-only worker) counts once towards it. A check you ask for through the API is not billed on its own. The answer shows the free trial (it starts when the account's first worker is created and lasts one month), whether the account may run checks (`trial.eligible`: during the trial, or with Direct Debit set up and billing allowed, or under a manual access override), the billing type chosen, this month's estimate under each billing type from today's number of active workers and the pricing tiers in force. Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`.

The billing type is chosen once in Hub and the Direct Debit is set up there; the set-up link is never returned by the API. Both portals return the same figures. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

operations.summary: Show the raw data of a DBS check
operations.description: Returns the answer the DBS Update Service gave for one DBS check, as Hub stored it: `format` is `xml` and `content` is the XML as a string. It is the technical record behind a check and holds personal data about the certificate; use the check and worker fields for decisions. `content` is null when nothing was stored. A check of another client's worker, or of a registration worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: The DBS check id (integer), from `recent_dbs_checks` of a worker or `GET /workers/{worker}/verification?track=dbs`.

operations.summary: Show the raw data of a right to work check
operations.description: Returns what the right to work check stored as its response: `format` is `json` and `content` is the decoded structure (its fields depend on the check method, share code or passport reading, and can change without notice, so do not build on them); when the stored text is not valid JSON it is returned as text. It can contain personal data. `content` is null when nothing was stored. A check of another client's worker, or of a registration worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: The right to work check id (integer), from `recent_rtw_checks` of a worker or `GET /workers/{worker}/verification?track=rtw`.

operations.description: Streams the PDF that was generated for one DBS check: the record of the status the DBS Update Service returned (`check_id` of a `dbs_certificate` row of the evidence list). The PDF is sent with `Content-Disposition: inline`, `Content-Type: application/pdf`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It contains personal data about the worker's DBS certificate: store it as carefully as you store the worker's record. A check with no PDF (the check failed, or the PDF could not be generated), a missing file, or a check of another client's worker is `404 not_found`. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: The DBS check id (integer): the `check_id` of a `dbs_certificate` row of `GET /workers/{worker}/evidence`.

operations.summary: Download a right to work screenshot
operations.description: Streams the screenshot captured by one right to work check: an image of the result page (`check_id` of an `rtw_screenshot` row of the evidence list). The image is sent with `Content-Disposition: inline`, the media type recorded for its extension (PNG or JPEG), `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It can show the worker's name and the right to work result: store it as carefully as you store the worker's record. A check with no screenshot, a missing file, or a check of another client's worker is `404 not_found`. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: The right to work check id (integer): the `check_id` of an `rtw_screenshot` row of `GET /workers/{worker}/evidence`.

operations.summary: Download an uploaded passport image or document
operations.description: Streams the file uploaded when the worker was added: `passport` is the passport image (`rtw_passport_image`), `document` the document file (`rtw_document_file`). The file is sent with `Content-Disposition: inline`, the media type recorded for its extension (PNG, JPEG or PDF), `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It is an identity document: store it with the same care as the original. A worker with no such upload, a missing file, or a worker of another client is `404 not_found`; any other `kind` than `passport` or `document` is a `404` too. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Which uploaded file: `passport` (the passport image sent as `rtw_passport_image`) or `document` (the document file sent as `rtw_document_file`). Any other value is `404 not_found`.

operations.description:
Uploads a CSV (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB) and queues it. The call answers `202` with the import row at once and the file is read by a background job: poll `GET /worker-imports/{id}`. The first row of the file is the header; get the column names from `GET /worker-imports/template` and check a file first with `POST /worker-imports/preview`, which uses the same rules and stores nothing. `column_mapping` maps an expected field to the header it is read from (without it the import reads the headers as they are, so they must be the field names, and `first_name` and `last_name` must be present or the import fails; the import never guesses a mapping, so send the `suggested_mapping` of a preview as `column_mapping` to use it). `check_frequency` (default `monthly`), `monitoring_start_date` (default today), `consent_given` (default false) and `is_active` (default true) are used for every row that does not carry its own value.

Each row is validated with the same rules as the preview: a row that fails is counted in `failed_count` with its line number and message and the others go on. A row that names a worker that already exists (the same regulator and registration number; the same DBS certificate number for a DBS-only row; the same name and share code for a right-to-work-only row) updates that worker, restoring it if it was removed; any other row creates one. Imported workers are not linked to Hub candidates. DBS & Right To Work rows can enrol a DBS certificate (12 digits, with `dbs_surname`) and a right to work check by `share_code` only: other document types need an upload and cannot be imported. **A row's `consent_given` defaults to false**: an import does not require the consent that `POST /workers` requires, so send `consent_given` true only when the workers have agreed to be monitored. No webhook is sent for an import; the checks that follow raise alerts and webhooks as usual. The imported workers count towards the monthly bill while they are active.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and file within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same import) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of importing the file twice. The import is not limited to the portal of the path: a file whose rows are of the other portal's kind is processed all the same. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a `check_frequency` that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

file.description: The CSV file, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB. The first row is the header; blank rows are skipped.

column_mapping.description: Which header of the file holds each field, as an object: the key is an expected field (see `GET /worker-imports/template`), the value the header (compared in lower case, trimmed), or null or an empty string to leave the field unmapped. Send it as `column_mapping[first_name]=First name` in a multipart form. Without it the file's headers must already be the field names.

items.description: The file header that holds one field.

check_frequency.description: The check frequency for rows that carry none: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Default `monthly`.

monitoring_start_date.description: The monitoring start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for rows that carry none. Default today.

consent_given.description: Whether the workers have agreed to be monitored, for rows that carry no `consent_given` of their own. Default false: an import does not require consent, so set this to true only when the workers have agreed.

is_active.description: Whether the workers are monitored, for rows that carry no `is_active` of their own. Default true. An inactive worker is not checked.

operations.description: Lists the CSV imports of your account, newest first, 25 to a page by default (`sort` is `id` or `-id`). Both monitoring portals list all of the account's imports, not only those started in the portal of the path, because an import enrols each row for whatever the row contains (a registration, a DBS certificate or a right to work share code). Each row shows the state and the counts as `GET /worker-imports/{id}` does. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description: A dry run of a CSV: send the same body as `POST /worker-imports` and get back the file's headers, the column mapping used (the one you sent, or a guess from the header names), the first five rows as they would be read, and how many of the rows would be imported or rejected, with the first message of each rejected row (at most 200). Only the first 1000 rows are validated (`truncated` says when the file has more); the real import handles every row. Nothing is stored, no worker is created or changed, nothing is queued, sent or billed, and the file is not kept, so a preview can be repeated freely while you fix the file. The expected columns are those of the portal of the path. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a value that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

file.description: The CSV file, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB. The first row is the header; blank rows are skipped.

column_mapping.description: Which header of the file holds each field, as an object: the key is an expected field (see `GET /worker-imports/template`), the value the header (compared in lower case, trimmed), or null or an empty string to leave the field unmapped. Send it as `column_mapping[first_name]=First name` in a multipart form. Without it the file's headers must already be the field names.

items.description: The file header that holds one field.

check_frequency.description: The check frequency for rows that carry none: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Default `monthly`.

monitoring_start_date.description: The monitoring start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for rows that carry none. Default today.

consent_given.description: Whether the workers have agreed to be monitored, for rows that carry no `consent_given` of their own. Default false: an import does not require consent, so set this to true only when the workers have agreed.

is_active.description: Whether the workers are monitored, for rows that carry no `is_active` of their own. Default true. An inactive worker is not checked.

operations.description: Returns the progress of one import: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), `progress` as a percentage, how many of the `total_rows` were turned into workers (`imported_count`) or rejected (`failed_count`), and the rejected rows in `errors` (line number and message, at most 1000). Poll it every few seconds after `POST /worker-imports` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. An import of another client is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

parameters.name: import
parameters.description: The import id (integer).

operations.description: Returns the column names a CSV import understands for the portal of the path, in the order of the Hub template: use them as the header row of your file (or as the keys of `column_mapping`). Registration Monitoring expects the registration columns (`regulator`, `registration_number`, ...), DBS & Right To Work the DBS and right to work columns (`dbs_certificate_number`, `rtw_document_type`, `rtw_share_code`, ...). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

Returns the roles a Hub team member can be given (`client-admin`, `client-manager`, `client-officer`, `client-viewer`) with the permissions each holds for your account, and the catalogue of every permission grouped by area (the Hub core, and `registration-monitoring` and `dbs-rtw` among the services). The permissions include the changes the account's Owner made on the My Team page. It is read only: team members, their roles and the role permissions are managed in Hub, and the API does not list the members. Both monitoring portals return the same answer. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:team:read` or `dbs-rtw:team:read`.

Asks for up to 200 workers to be checked now, with the same rules and side effects as `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. Send `worker_ids`, or leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (at most 200: with more active workers the call is refused with `422 too_many_workers` and you must send `worker_ids` in batches of up to 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are silently left out, not reported. One job is queued per worker and track: in DBS & Right To Work a worker enrolled for both tracks gets two jobs unless you send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) to check one track only; in Registration Monitoring the only track is `registration`.

The answer is `202` with `jobs` (`worker_id`, `track`, `job_id`) for every check that was queued and `refused` for those that were not, each with the reason (a worker may be refused for the reasons in `POST /workers/{id}/verify`, while the rest are queued). Poll each `job_id` on `GET /verify/jobs/{job}`.
