When nothing at all could be queued the call answers `422 verification_refused` with the list in `details.refused`; when there is no active worker to check it answers `422 no_active_workers`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same job ids) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing the checks again; without it every call queues new jobs. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to check, at most 200. Leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (refused with `too_many_workers` when there are more than 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are left out without an error.

track.description: Check one track only: `registration` in Registration Monitoring; `dbs` or `rtw` in DBS & Right To Work. Left out, every track each worker is enrolled for is checked, so a worker enrolled for both DBS and right to work gets two jobs.

operations.summary: Show the progress of a verification job
operations.description:
Returns the state of a job created by `POST /workers/{id}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), how many workers it handled (`processed_count` of `total_workers`), how many checks worked (`success_count`) and failed (`failed_count`), how many workers changed status (`status_changes_found`), when it started and ended, and `error_message` when it failed. Poll it every few seconds, not faster than your rate limit allows; a job stays readable after it ends. `completed` means the job ran, not that every check succeeded: look at `failed_count` and at the worker's check history.

A job belongs to the portal that created it: a registration job is only visible in Registration Monitoring, a DBS or right to work job only in DBS & Right To Work, and a job of another client is `404 not_found` (so is a job of the other portal). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The verification job id (integer) returned by `POST /workers/{worker}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`.

operations.summary: Add a worker to DBS and right to work monitoring
operations.description:
Enrols one worker for a DBS Update Service check, a right to work check, or both: send `dbs_certificate_number` with `dbs_surname` and `date_of_birth` for DBS, and `rtw_document_type` (with `rtw_share_code`, or an upload) for right to work. At least one of the two is required, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `dbs_certificate_number`. The worker is created active, with the monitoring start date you give (today when you give none), the frequencies you give for each track (the account's default for the track when you give none) and consent recorded as given at this moment. The call returns the worker with `201`. It does not link the worker to a Hub candidate: `candidate_ref` is null.

Send `multipart/form-data` when you upload a file, JSON otherwise. A passport document type (`uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`) needs `rtw_passport_image` (an image); every other document type except `share_code` needs `rtw_document_file` (`jpg`, `jpeg`, `png` or `pdf`); each upload is at most 10 MB. A passport is read from the image, a share code is checked against the Home Office service, and the other document types are stored for manual handling and are not verified automatically. For a share code worker also send `date_of_birth`: the Home Office check needs it, and a check without it ends with an error (this call does not require it for a share code worker). A share code is three groups of three letters or digits, like `ABC DEF GHI`; it is stored in upper case. A DBS certificate number is exactly 12 digits and must not already be monitored for your account.

Nothing is checked by this call and nothing is charged by it. The first checks are made by the next monitoring run, or at once when you ask for them with `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. A DBS check sets the worker's DBS status and stores a certificate PDF; a right to work check sets the right to work status and stores a screenshot. A change of status raises the `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and findings (new DBS information, a missing right to work, an expiring share code) raise an alert, an email to the account and the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Monitoring is part of the account's subscription (see `GET /billing/usage`): the worker counts towards the monthly bill while it is active, and checks stop when the free trial is over and Direct Debit is not set up.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body (uploads included) within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second worker, and the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `consent_given` when it is not true, `dbs_certificate_number` when it is not 12 digits, is already monitored, or when neither track is given, `dbs_surname` and `date_of_birth` when they are missing for a DBS enrolment, `rtw_share_code` when it is missing or malformed for a share code worker, `rtw_passport_image` or `rtw_document_file` when the upload the document type needs is missing, and the usual type and size errors. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: The worker to monitor: who they are and what to check. Send JSON, or `multipart/form-data` (`DrCreateWorkerUploadBody`) when you upload a passport image or a document. `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `consent_given` are required, and at least one of `dbs_certificate_number` and `rtw_document_type`. A field that is not listed is ignored.

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters. Required.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text, at most 255 characters.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. Required when `dbs_certificate_number` is sent (the DBS check needs it, otherwise `422` on this field). Also send it for a share code worker: the Home Office check needs it, and a check without it ends with an error.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, at most 255 characters.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person in your organisation responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Left out, it is today.

consent_given.description: Must be true: the worker has agreed to be monitored. The call is refused with `422` on this field otherwise. Hub records the moment you made the call as the time consent was given.

notes.description: Free text notes about the worker, at most 5000 characters.

dbs_certificate_number.description: The 12 digit DBS certificate number, to enrol the worker for the DBS Update Service. It must not already be monitored for your account. Send this, `rtw_document_type`, or both: sending neither is `422` on this field.

dbs_surname.description: The surname the DBS Update Service is asked about, at most 255 characters. Required when `dbs_certificate_number` is sent.

dbs_check_frequency.description: How often the DBS status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default for DBS applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

rtw_document_type.description: The document the right to work check is based on, to enrol the worker for right to work. One of: `uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`, `share_code`, `uk_birth_certificate`, `irish_birth_certificate`, `uk_adoption_certificate`, `british_citizenship_certificate`, `immigration_status_document`, `passport_with_endorsement`. A passport type (`uk_passport`, `irish_passport`, `irish_passport_card`) needs `rtw_passport_image` and is read from the image; `share_code` needs `rtw_share_code` and is checked against the Home Office service; every other type needs `rtw_document_file` and is stored for manual handling (it is not verified automatically).

rtw_share_code.description: The Home Office right to work share code: three groups of three letters or digits separated by single spaces, like `ABC DEF GHI`. Required when `rtw_document_type` is `share_code`; it is stored in upper case. A share code is assumed valid for 90 days from the day it is entered.

rtw_check_frequency.description: How often the right to work status is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default for right to work applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

operations.description: Removes the worker from your account: it is no longer listed, checked, billed or reachable on `/workers/{id}` (the id answers `404 not_found` afterwards), and its DBS and right to work tracks both stop. The worker is soft deleted, not erased: its earlier checks and evidence are kept by Hub. Nothing is sent about the removal and no refund or charge is made by this call. Repeating the call for a removed worker is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

operations.summary: List the evidence of a DBS and right to work worker
operations.description:
Lists everything Hub holds as evidence for one worker, as one list: a DBS certificate PDF for each DBS check that generated one (`type` `dbs_certificate`), a screenshot for each right to work check that captured one (`rtw_screenshot`), then the uploaded `passport` image and `document` file if the worker has them. The checks come newest first; the uploads have no check and no time. The evidence is what lets you show an auditor what the service said on the day. A worker with no evidence yet (one that has never been checked, for example) gets an empty list.

Each row carries `download_url`, which points to the matching download endpoint; the files are never served from a public address and need your bearer token. `type` keeps one kind of file, `checked_from` and `checked_to` filter by the day of the check (uploads have no date and drop out when either is used), and `sort` orders by `checked_at` or `type`. A worker of another client, or a registration worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `checked_at`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-checked_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: checked_from
parameters.description: Only evidence of checks made on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. The uploaded `passport` and `document` have no date and are left out when this or `checked_to` is used. Must not be after `checked_to`.

parameters.name: checked_to
parameters.description: Only evidence of checks made on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. The uploaded `passport` and `document` have no date and are left out when this or `checked_from` is used. Must not be before `checked_from`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only this kind of evidence: `dbs_certificate`, `rtw_screenshot`, `passport` or `document`.

operations.summary: List DBS and right to work workers
operations.description:
Lists the workers your account monitors for DBS and right to work, 25 to a page by default (`per_page` 1 to 100), sorted by last name unless `sort` says otherwise. A worker is listed when it is enrolled for a DBS certificate, a right to work check or both, active or not (`is_active` filters them); workers that are monitored only for a professional registration belong to the Registration Monitoring API and are not shown. The list is scoped to the client of the API key.

`search` takes words that must each match the first name, last name, email or profession. `check_type` keeps the workers enrolled for `dbs` or for `rtw`. `compliant` is `true` for workers whose every enrolled track is in good standing (DBS status `BLANK_NO_NEW_INFO`, right to work status `has_right`; a track not yet checked is not in good standing) and `false` for the others. `candidate_ref` narrows the list to the worker linked to that Hub candidate (only workers that Hub staff linked have one); a `candidate_ref` that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A filter value that is not allowed is `422 validation_failed` too.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `dbs-rtw:workers:read`.

operations.summary: Change the monitoring settings of a worker
operations.description:
Changes how often a worker is checked and whether monitoring is on. Send at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`); a body with none of them is `422 validation_failed`. In Registration Monitoring `check_frequency` is the schedule of the registration. In DBS & Right To Work `check_frequency` sets every track the worker is enrolled for, and `dbs_check_frequency` or `rtw_check_frequency` sets one track and wins over `check_frequency` for it; a track the worker is not enrolled for is left alone.

Side effects: a changed frequency reschedules the next check of the track while the worker is active, counted from the last check (or the start date when there has been none) for a registration and from now for DBS and right to work, so the new `next_check_due_at` is in the answer. Switching a worker off (`is_active` false) clears every next check date and stops scheduled checks; switching it on again reschedules each track from its frequency. Nothing is checked immediately, no email, alert or webhook is sent, and nothing is charged by this call, but an active worker counts towards the monthly bill (`GET /billing/usage`), so switching a worker off removes it from the bill from then on.

The answer holds `registration` (Registration Monitoring) or `dbs` and `rtw` (DBS & Right To Work, null for a track the worker is not enrolled for). A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the surname used for the DBS check. The DBS certificate number, the right to work document and the share code are not edited here (a share code has its own endpoint, `PUT /workers/{id}/share-code`), and how often and whether the worker is checked is changed with `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

operations.summary: Renew a right to work share code
operations.description:
Replaces the share code of a worker that is monitored with a share code (`rtw.document_type` is `share_code`). A share code is valid for 90 days, so renew it when `rtw.share_code_expires_at` is near or `rtw.share_code_stale` is true (the scheduled right to work run skips a worker whose code is stale, and alerts are raised 14 days and 3 days before it expires and when it has expired). The code is stored in upper case; entering it sets `rtw.share_code_provided_at` to today and so restarts the 90 day window at once. The call does not run a check: the next scheduled check, or `POST /workers/{id}/verify` with `track` `rtw`, uses the new code. The call returns the worker.

operations.summary: List the check history of a worker
operations.description:
Lists every check made for one worker on one track, newest first, 25 to a page by default. In Registration Monitoring the track is `registration` and each row is a registration check (`status`, `status_changed`, `previous_status`, `expiry_date`, ...). In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`), which is required for a worker enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`, and `422 invalid_track` for any other value); a DBS row has the Update Service `status` and `has_evidence_pdf`, a right to work row has `status` (`has_right` or `no_right`), `method`, `expiry_date` and `has_screenshot`. A check that failed to reach a result is in the history with `result` `error` and does not change the worker's status. `checked_from` and `checked_to` filter by the day of the check and `sort` orders by `checked_at` or `id`.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

operations.description:
Asks for one worker to be checked now instead of waiting for the schedule: a registration against the regulator's register (Registration Monitoring), or the DBS certificate against the DBS Update Service or the right to work against the Home Office service or the passport image (DBS & Right To Work). The call creates a verification job and answers `202` with its `job_id` at once; the check runs in the background. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`, read the result on the worker (`GET /workers/{id}`) and in its history (`GET /workers/{id}/verification`), and the evidence on `GET /workers/{id}/evidence`.

Registration Monitoring has one track (`registration`) and ignores `track`. In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) when the worker is enrolled for both; for a worker enrolled for one track it is optional. A `track` that is not `dbs` or `rtw` is `422 invalid_track`, and omitting it for a worker enrolled for both is `422 track_required`.

The rules are the ones a person pressing Re-check in Hub meets, and a refusal is `422 verification_refused` with the reason in `message`: manual re-checks are not enabled for the account, the worker is not active, the worker is not enrolled for the track, the account may not run checks (the free trial has ended and Direct Debit is not set up, or the regulator's connector is switched off or has used its monthly allowance), or the regulator's connector is paused. When the check ends it can change the worker's status: a change raises an alert and the `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`, `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and the first registration result sends `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification`. A manual check is not charged separately: monitoring is part of the account's subscription (`GET /billing/usage`). Where the verification engine is switched off the request is only recorded: the job stays `pending` and no regulator is called.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body for the same worker within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same `job_id`) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing a second check; without it every call queues a new job. Another client's worker, or one of the other portal, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: Which track to check.

track.description: The track to check: `dbs` (the DBS Update Service) or `rtw` (right to work). Required when the worker is enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`); optional when the worker is enrolled for one. Any other value is `422 invalid_track`.

operations.description:
Adds a candidate exactly as the Add Candidate page does, with no service set up (every service starts `not_required`; the portal APIs set up what they need when you use them). It is the only way to create a person through the API: portals never create one for you, they take the `candidate_ref` this call returns. Send `first_name`, `last_name` and `email`; `phone`, `roles` (up to 10), `specialties` (up to 10), `candidate_reference`, `compliance_officer` and `is_active` are optional.

Side effects: the candidate is created in Hub and in the account's HB Portal record, and unless `is_active` is false the candidate is emailed their activation link (as every portal does for a candidate it adds). No email is sent for an inactive candidate, or when the account is set to activate candidates by hand; a failure to send never undoes the candidate, and the email can be sent again from the Emails menu on the candidate page. The action is recorded in the candidate's activity as made by the person who created the API key (or, if that person is gone, the client's first user).

Duplicates and errors: an email address the client already has is `422 validation_failed` on `email`: look the person up with `GET /hub/candidates?search=` and use their `candidate_ref`. Other field errors are `422` on the field. `422` on `email` also answers an account that has no HB Portal client yet. If the account has no Hub user to add the candidate as, the answer is `409 conflict`.

Idempotency: send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters). The same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and creates nothing; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`; only a successful answer is remembered, so a call that failed validation can be corrected under the same key. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:write`; the call counts against the key's hourly limit.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

last_name.description: The candidate's last name, up to 100 characters.

email.description: The candidate's email address (up to 191 characters). It must not belong to another candidate of the client, otherwise `422` on `email`. The activation link is sent here.

roles.description: The roles the candidate holds, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

compliance_officer.description: The name of the client's compliance officer for this candidate, up to 150 characters.

operations.description:
Lists the client's candidates in Hub, the people every other portal API refers to. `candidate_ref` is the uuid that identifies a person in all of them: take it from here, or from the answer of `POST /hub/candidates`, and use it in paths, bodies and filters of the portal APIs. Each row shows identity, roles, the overall compliance status and the next expiry date; the services a candidate has with each portal are on `GET /hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`. Inactive candidates are listed too (`is_active` false); filter them out with `is_active=true`.

Filters: `search` (every word must match the name, email, a role or your own `candidate_reference`; at most 100 characters), `status` or `compliance_status` (the same filter under two names: `compliant`, `expiring_soon`, `expired`, `pending` or `na`), `role` (an exact role name the candidate holds), `is_active` (`true` or `false`), `added_from` / `added_to` (when the candidate was added) and `updated_from` / `updated_to` (when they were last changed). Each range works on whole UTC days: `_from` is the start of the UTC day of the value, `_to` its end, so a time of day in the value is ignored; a `_to` before the `_from` is `422` on `_to`. `sort` accepts `name` (the default, ascending), `email`, `added_at` and `updated_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25); a page past the last is empty and `meta.total` stays correct.

Use it to find a candidate before creating one (an email address can exist once per client) and to keep your own records in step: poll with `updated_from` set to the last time you looked. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a bad filter, date, `sort` or paging value; the standard `401`, `403` and `429` of every call.

operations.description:
Returns one candidate with everything the list shows plus the compliance counts (`compliance`: how many items are compliant, expiring soon and expired) and the services the candidate has with each portal (`services`: one entry for every Hub service, with who manages it, its status, dates and the `portal_id` the portal itself uses; a service the candidate does not have is `not_required`). Use it to see where a person stands before booking, assigning or requesting something for them.

`{candidate_ref}` must be a uuid. A value that is not a uuid, a candidate that does not exist and another client's candidate all answer `404 not_found`, so a reference cannot be used to find out whether someone belongs to another organisation. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

operations.description:
Changes a candidate's identity and Hub's own fields; only the fields you send change, and fields you leave out keep their value (a PATCH has no required field). It accepts `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `phone`, `roles`, `specialties`, `candidate_reference`, `compliance_officer` and `is_active`. `roles` and `specialties` replace the whole list, so send every value you want to keep. `phone`, `candidate_reference` and `compliance_officer` can be set to `null` to clear them.

Name, email and phone are also written to the candidate's HB Portal record (and the first and last name to their login), because the portals read them from there: a change here is what the portal APIs and emails show next. `is_active` makes the candidate active or inactive, as the buttons on the candidate page do (there is no delete; inactive is the equivalent). No email is sent. The change is recorded in the candidate's activity as made by the person who created the API key.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` on the field for an invalid value, and on `email` when another candidate of the client already uses that address; a malformed, unknown or other client's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`. Sending the same body again gives the same result, so a retry is safe; the call does not take `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `hub:candidates:write`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

first_name.description: The candidate's first name, up to 100 characters.

last_name.description: The candidate's last name, up to 100 characters.

email.description: The candidate's email address (up to 191 characters). It must not belong to another candidate of the client, otherwise `422` on `email`. The activation link is sent here.

phone.description: The candidate's phone number, up to 50 characters.

roles.description: The roles the candidate holds, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

specialties.description: The candidate's specialties, at most 10, each up to 100 characters.

candidate_reference.description: The client's own reference for the candidate, up to 100 characters.

compliance_officer.description: The name of the client's compliance officer for this candidate, up to 150 characters.

is_active.description: False to add the candidate as inactive; no activation email is sent. On an update, true makes the candidate active again and false makes them inactive. Default true when adding.

operations.description:
Hides every alert that is currently shown and answers `{ "data": { "dismissed": n } }` with how many were hidden (`0` when none were shown, which is not an error). Dismissals hold until each request changes status. Like `POST /alerts/dismiss`, the dismissals are shared with your account's users and also clear the Alerts page in Hub, and the requests themselves are not changed. There is no body.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:alerts:write`.

Hides one alert from your account's alert list. `key` is the `key` of a row from `GET /alerts`; only an alert that is currently shown can be dismissed, otherwise `404 not_found`, so repeating the call for an alert that is already dismissed answers `404`. The answer is `{ "data": { "dismissed": 1 } }`. A dismissal holds until the request changes status, then a new alert appears if the new status calls for one.

The dismissal is recorded against the API key's owner and is shared with everyone in your account: it also disappears from the Alerts page in Hub. It does not change the request. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:alerts:write`.

key.description: The `key` of the alert to dismiss, from `GET /alerts`. Only an alert that is currently shown can be dismissed.

operations.description:
Lists your account's alerts, as the Alerts page does: requests that were `rejected` and need resubmitting, and assessments that ended `not_fit` with a fail letter. Both are `critical`. Each row has a stable `key` (for example `rejected:4821`), the `type`, the `status_label`, the candidate (`candidate_ref`, `candidate_name`), the `clearance`, the `request_id` (null for an older questionnaire with no request), the `submission_id`, a `description` and the time `at`. For a rejection the `description` carries the reviewer's note, which is why the list is health data. `type` filters to one kind and `sort` accepts `at` and `type`.

An alert you dismissed is left out until its request changes status. The call is written to the API log without its bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:alerts:read`. This is health data. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `at`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Alerts: `rejected` or `not_fit`. Credit transactions: `all`, `credit` or `debit`. One of: `rejected`, `not_fit`.

operations.description:
Lists your account's candidates so you can choose who a request is for. Archived and locked candidates are left out. Every word of `search` must match the candidate's name, role or email (so `ann lee` finds Ann Lee), `has_forms=true` keeps only candidates who already have an Occupational Health questionnaire assigned and `false` only those who do not. Rows have the `candidate_ref` (the Hub uuid used by every API), `name`, `email`, `role`, `forms` (the questionnaires assigned) and `has_forms`. `sort` accepts `first_name`, `last_name` and `email`; the default is first name then last name.

A candidate cannot be created here: candidates already exist in Hub, so create one with `POST /api/v2/hub/candidates` and use the same `candidate_ref` in this API. `candidate_ref` is `null` only for a candidate Hub has not synced yet. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-first_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name, role or email (requests: candidate name or email or reference).

parameters.name: has_forms
parameters.description: `true` returns only candidates with an OH questionnaire assigned, `false` only those without. One of: `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`.

operations.summary: Send the health questionnaire reminder email
operations.description:
Emails the candidate a reminder to complete their health questionnaire, exactly as the reminder button in Hub does. The answer `{ "data": { "candidate_ref", "sent": true } }` confirms that the email was queued for the candidate's address. There is no body.

Every call sends one real email, so the call is not idempotent and takes no `Idempotency-Key`: do not retry it blindly after a timeout, and do not call it in a loop (the candidate is also reminded automatically by the chase settings in `GET /settings`). A candidate with no email address answers `422 validation_failed` on `email` and nothing is sent. The call is limited to 20 a minute per key, then `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header. An unknown, malformed or another account's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:write`. Side effect: one email to the candidate; nothing is charged.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

operations.summary: Get a candidate with their request history
operations.description:
Returns one candidate (the same row as the list, plus `status`, the candidate's account status) and their `history`: the candidate's requests that have a completed questionnaire, newest first, in the same shape as `GET /requests`. Requests still waiting for the candidate to complete the questionnaire are not in the history: find them with `GET /requests?candidate_ref=`. Archived candidates can be read here even though the list leaves them out.

An unknown, malformed or another account's `candidate_ref` answers `404 not_found`, never `403`. Every view is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

operations.description:
Lists the clearance types your account may choose when it creates a request. Each has an `id` (send it as `clearance_type_id` in `POST /requests`), a `name`, `needs_immunisations` (a new starter's request then needs `imms_method`, and may carry immunisation files), `has_scope_choice` (a new starter may ask for `full` or `temporary` clearance in `scope`) and `has_online_form` (Hub has a health questionnaire the candidate can complete online; otherwise the questionnaire is on paper and goes by email).

The questionnaires of a clearance type are derived from it and never chosen: use `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire` to see which forms a request for the type assigns and every question on them, and `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` to answer them for the candidate. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every type; `sort` accepts `id` and `name`.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.summary: Get the questionnaire of a clearance type
operations.description:
Returns the health questionnaires that a request for this clearance type assigns to a candidate, with every question and how to answer it, so you know what you will have to send before you create a request. The forms are derived from the clearance type: you never pick a form yourself, and the list follows the clearance type for your account (a list set for your account wins over the standard list of the type). `{clearance_type}` is an `id` from `GET /clearance-types`; a type your account may not use answers `404 not_found`.

Each form has `fieldsets` (headings, in questionnaire order) with `questions`. A question has a `key` (the name you answer it under), its `label`, a `type`, whether it is `required`, its `options` for a choice, a `max_length`, and `show_when` for a question that only appears after another answer (a hidden question is not required and its answer is discarded). `answer_format` says in words what to send for that kind of question. `documents` lists whether supporting documents are needed with the answers, the documents the candidate is normally asked for and the file limits. A clearance type with no online questionnaire returns an empty `forms` list: its request is handled by email and paper and has nothing to answer through the API.

This is the same questionnaire the candidate sees, at the version in use now. `request` is null here; read `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` once a request exists to see where each form stands. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: clearance_type
parameters.description: The clearance type id (integer), from `GET /clearance-types`.

operations.description:
Lists the credit packages that can be bought on the billing page in Hub: the number of `credits`, the `price_pence`, `vat_pence` (always 0: Occupational Health is not charged VAT), `total_pence` and the price of one credit (`per_credit_pence`), with `currency` `GBP`. Nothing can be bought through the API; send the user to `top_up_url` from `GET /credits`. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every package.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

operations.description:
Returns the credits your account holds (`balance`, whole credits), how many were used this month (`used_this_month`), whether credits are being taken at all (`deducting`), what a new starter costs (`credits_per_new_starter`) and the price of one credit in pence (`price_per_credit_pence`, with `currency` `GBP`). Credits are read only in the API: they are bought on the billing page in Hub, whose address is `top_up_url`, and there is no top-up call.

A credit is taken when the candidate's questionnaire is submitted (by the candidate, or by you with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`), only when `deducting` is true, only for a new starter's first submission, and renewals are free. A short balance never blocks a request or a submission: it is simply not charged. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the credit ledger, newest first: each purchase or use of credits with its `description` and `note`, the `amount` of credits moved (always positive; `is_credit` is true for credits added and false for credits used), when it happened (`created_at`) and the candidate it belongs to (`candidate_ref` and `candidate_name`, null for a purchase). `type` is `all` (default), `credit` or `debit`, and `created_from` and `created_to` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, or an ISO 8601 time) bound the period. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only credit movements recorded on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only credit movements recorded on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Alerts: `rejected` or `not_fit`. Credit transactions: `all`, `credit` or `debit`. One of: `all`, `credit`, `debit`.

operations.summary: Create an embed session for a health questionnaire
operations.description: Creates a session that lets the Healthier Business SDK show one questionnaire (`form_shortcode`) of an existing request to its candidate inside your own page. The request must take online answers and have no outcome yet, and the form must be one of the request's forms (`GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`) that the candidate has not sent. `origin` is the address of the page that will show it (scheme, host and port only) and must be one of the origins your account allows. The answer holds a single-use `launch_token` valid for 5 minutes, the `frame_url` and the `session_id`; pass the token to the SDK in the browser. Errors: `404 not_found` for an unknown request, `422` for a form that is not one of the request's or an origin that is not allowed, `409` with the request's blocker code (`request_not_online`, `request_closed`) or `form_not_pending`. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:embed:create`. Health answers are never stored by this call.

schema.description:
`POST /embed/sessions`: one questionnaire of a request to show inside your own page, and the page's origin. The key's scope is the
permission.

request_id.description: The request, by its `id`. It must take online answers and have no outcome yet.

form_shortcode.description: The questionnaire, by its `shortcode` from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`. It must be one of the request's forms that the candidate has not sent.

origin.description: The website that will show it, as scheme, host and port only. It must be one of the origins your account allows (Developer, Embed). https is required, except for localhost.

schema.title: OhCreateEmbedSessionBody

operations.description: Issues a new single-use launch token for a session that is still open and kills the previous one. A finished session answers `409 session_finished` and an expired one `410 session_expired`; start a new session then. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:embed:create`.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The session_id of the record (integer).

operations.description:
Lists the health questionnaires in your account's form set: the `shortcode`, the `title` and how many `questions` each has. A `shortcode` is how a questionnaire is named everywhere else: in `GET /forms/{shortcode}`, as the `form` filter of `GET /requests`, as `hq_form` in the answer of `POST /requests` and in the path of `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every form; `sort` accepts `shortcode` and `title`.

This is the whole form set of the account, not the forms of one request. Which forms a request has follows from its clearance type: read `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire` before you create a request, or `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` afterwards.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `shortcode`, `title`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-shortcode`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description:
Returns one questionnaire of your account's form set: its `title`, the `version` in use (title, version number and when it was last updated) and `template`, the node tree the questionnaire preview draws (sections, questions, their options and conditions). It is for displaying or previewing a questionnaire. To answer one, read the flat list of questions with their keys and answer formats from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` instead.

A `shortcode` outside your account's form set, or one Hub does not have, answers `404 not_found`. The version is the one in use now; a questionnaire that is edited later changes what new candidates see, not what was already submitted.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: shortcode
parameters.description: The questionnaire shortcode, from `GET /forms` (or `forms[].shortcode` of a questionnaire answer). A shortcode outside the client's form set is a 404, and so is one that is not a form of the request when you submit answers.

operations.description:
Returns the Occupational Health account the API key belongs to: the client `id` (the same number as the Hub client id) and `name`, who is emailed about requests (`notifications`: `hb` for Healthier Business, `agency` for your own address, or `both`), who may upload documents (`document_upload`: `candidate`, `agency` or `both`) and whether uploads are allowed at all (`allows_uploads`). Call it once at start-up to check that the key reaches the account you expect.

`ftw_routing_configured` says whether a new request has somewhere to be emailed. When it is `false`, `POST /requests` still succeeds but the request has no destination mailbox: it is stored and nobody is emailed, so ask Healthier Business to finish setting the account up before you rely on it. `credit_balance` is the number of credits held and `credits_deducting` says whether credits are taken at all (see `GET /credits`); a short balance never blocks a request.

Everything is scoped to the account of the key and there is no way to read another client's profile. An account without Occupational Health answers `403 portal_unavailable` on every endpoint of this portal. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Streams a generated report: `xlsx` or `pdf` (the report's own format, as `format` in `GET /reports`) or `csv` for any report, built from the same data (UTF-8 with a byte order mark; a cell that starts like a formula is prefixed with an apostrophe). The file is named `{report}-{date}.{format}`. Generate the report first: before a run, or after the stored result has expired, the answer is `404 not_found` with the message `Generate the report first.` The other format of a report (for example `pdf` for a spreadsheet report) is `404` as well.

The file is health data: it is only streamed, for your account, and never written to the API log. Each download is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:reports:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The report type: `all_requests`, `activity` or `expiring`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `xlsx` or `pdf` (the report's own format) or `csv` (every report).

operations.description:
Queues a report to be built in the background, as the Reports page does, and answers `202` at once with `{ "data": { "type", "status": "processing" } }`. The report is not ready yet: poll `GET /reports` until its `status` is `complete`, then download it with `GET /reports/{type}/{format}`. `{type}` is `all_requests`, `activity` or `expiring`; an unknown type answers `404 not_found`. A run that is already processing is left alone (the call still answers `202`), and a new run replaces the previous report's data.

The call is limited to 10 a minute per key, then `429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header. The report covers your account only. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:reports:write`. Side effect: one background job; nothing is emailed or charged.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The report type: `all_requests`, `activity` or `expiring`.

operations.description:
Lists the three reports your account can generate: `all_requests` (a spreadsheet of every request), `activity` (a PDF of recent activity) and `expiring` (a spreadsheet of clearances about to expire). Each row has the report's `title`, `subtitle` and `format` (`xlsx` or `pdf`) and the progress of the last run: `status` (`idle`, `processing` or `complete`), `percent`, `count` (the rows in it) and `generated_at` (ISO 8601 UTC, null until it finishes). `sort` accepts `type`, `title` and `generated_at`. The list is short and fixed, so it is one page that holds every report.

Reports are built in the background: start one with `POST /reports/{type}/generate`, poll this list until `status` is `complete`, then download it. The files and their data are kept per account. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:reports:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `type`, `title`, `generated_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-type`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.summary: Get the choices and upload limits of a new request
operations.description:
Returns the values `POST /requests` accepts, each with a label: `request_types` (`new_starter`, `renewal`), `scopes` (`full`, `temporary`), `hq_methods` (`online`, `paper`) and `immunisation_methods` (`agency`, `candidate`). `upload_kinds` names the file fields (`paper_hq`, `immunisation`, `previous_ftw`) and `uploads` gives the limits that apply to every file you send: the allowed `extensions`, the size of one file in kilobytes (`max_kb`), the number of files (`max_files`) and their total size (`max_total_kb`).

Read it once to build a request form, or to check a file before sending it. A file that breaks a limit is refused with `422 validation_failed` on the file field, and nothing is created. The limits of the files sent with answers to a questionnaire are different and are given in `documents.upload` of `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.summary: List the questionnaire answers of a request
operations.description:
Returns the answers of the completed questionnaire grouped by fieldset, in the order and with the wording of the questionnaire: each group has a `fieldset` heading and `items`, each with the question `label` and the `value` given. A signature answer also carries `image`, a PNG data URL. It is the same for a questionnaire the candidate completed and one you submitted for them with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. A request that is still waiting for the candidate has no answers and returns an empty page; a request with several forms shows the answers of its questionnaire. `sort` accepts `fieldset`.

An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Every view is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only, and the call is written to the API log without its bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. This is health data: do not store or forward it more widely than you must. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `fieldset`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-fieldset`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description:
Creates an Occupational Health request for a candidate, exactly as the New Request page does. `candidate_ref` is one of your candidates (otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`, not a 404), `request_type` is `new_starter` or `renewal`, `clearance_type_id` comes from `GET /clearance-types` and `hq_method` says how the health questionnaire is completed. For a new starter whose clearance type needs immunisations, `scope` (`full` or `temporary`) and `imms_method` are required; otherwise `scope` is ignored and treated as `full`. Files (`paper_hq`, `immunisation`, `previous_ftw`) go in a `multipart/form-data` body; their limits are in `GET /request-options`; without files JSON works too.

With an online questionnaire (`hq_method` `online`) and a Hub form for the clearance type, the forms of the clearance type are assigned to the candidate (you cannot choose them: see `GET /clearance-types/{clearance_type}/questionnaire`) and the candidate is emailed to complete them (send `notify_candidate: false` to skip that email when you will answer for the candidate with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`; everything else is unchanged). The request waits (`status` `awaiting_candidate`) and is emailed to Healthier Business, with its files, once the questionnaire is in. The candidate can complete it, or you can answer it for them with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. With a paper questionnaire, or no Hub form, the request is emailed to Healthier Business at once with the uploaded files and its status is `submitted`. The webhooks `occupational-health.request.submitted` and, when it applies, `occupational-health.request.awaiting_candidate` are queued.

The requester Hub needs (the reply-to of the email) is the user who created the API key, else your account's first user; with neither the call answers `422` on `api_key`. This call does not take credits: when credit deduction is switched on (`GET /credits` shows `deducting`), the first completed questionnaire of a new starter costs `credits_per_new_starter` credits and renewals are free; a short balance never blocks. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: repeating the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`, and a repeat that the cache no longer holds answers `200` with `duplicate: true`. Without it every call is its own request. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:write`.

credits.description: Not charged by this call. When credit deduction is on, the first completed questionnaire of a new starter costs credits_per_new_starter credits (GET /credits); renewals are free.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: The fields of `POST /requests`. Send `multipart/form-data` (needed for files); a JSON body also works when no files are sent. The form's `token` is the `Idempotency-Key` header.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the request is for: their `candidate_ref` from `GET /candidates`. It must be one of the client's candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref` (not a 404).

notify_candidate.description: Optional, default `true`. With an online questionnaire, `true` emails the candidate that forms were assigned to them. Send `false` to skip that email when you will answer the questionnaire for the candidate with `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`. Nothing else changes: the request, its status, the Healthier Business email, credits and webhooks are the same. Ignored for a paper questionnaire.

request_type.description: `new_starter` for a first clearance, `renewal` to renew an existing one. A renewal can carry the previous certificate in `previous_ftw`.

scope.description: `full` or `temporary` clearance. Required for a new starter whose clearance type needs immunisations (`has_scope_choice` in `GET /clearance-types`); otherwise ignored and treated as `full`.

hq_method.description: How the health questionnaire is completed: `online` (the candidate completes it in Hub) or `paper` (you upload the completed form in `paper_hq`).

imms_method.description: Who uploads the immunisation documents: `agency` (you, in `immunisation`) or `candidate`. Required for a new starter whose clearance type needs immunisations.

paper_hq.description: The completed paper health questionnaire, one or more files. Required when `hq_method` is `paper`. File types and sizes: `GET /request-options`.

immunisation.description: Immunisation documents, used for a new starter with `imms_method` `agency`. File types and sizes: `GET /request-options`.

previous_ftw.description: The candidate's previous Fit to Work certificate, used for a renewal. File types and sizes: `GET /request-options`.

operations.summary: List the documents of a request
operations.description:
Lists the documents of a request: the supporting documents the candidate uploaded with the questionnaire (`type` `supporting`, `source` null) and the Fit to Work certificates and fail letters (`type` `ftw`, with `source` `submission` for the request's own document or `candidate` for the candidate's standing one, and `general` true for the latter). Each row has an `id`, `filename`, `size` in bytes, `uploaded_at` and a `download_url` that points at the download endpoints below. `sort` accepts `uploaded_at`, `type` and `name`.

A request with no completed questionnaire has no documents and returns an empty page. The files you send with `POST /requests` (paper questionnaire, immunisation and previous certificate files) go to Healthier Business by email and are not listed or downloadable, as on the Requests page. The documents sent with answers through `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` are stored with the candidate's submission and appear here as supporting documents. An unknown or another account's request answers `404 not_found`. The webhook `occupational-health.document.available` tells you when a new certificate or letter is recorded.

The key needs the scope `occupational-health:documents:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

Streams one supporting document the candidate uploaded for the request, with the content type and name it was uploaded with. `{id}` is the request and `{file}` the document `id` from `GET /requests/{id}/documents`. The file is found through your account's own request, so another account's file answers `404 not_found` even when its id is guessed, and so does a file that has gone from storage. There are no signed or public links: every download needs the bearer token.

Each download is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only, and the call is written to the API log without its bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:documents:read`. This is health data. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

A cell that starts like a spreadsheet formula (`=`, `+`, `-` or `@`) is prefixed with an apostrophe so it is not run.

The file name is `occupational-health-requests-{date}.csv` and the response is `private, no-store`. Each download is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Each download is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only, and the call is written to the API log without its bodies. Lists your account's Occupational Health requests: the same rows, filters and order as the Requests page in Hub. A row is a request that is waiting for the candidate to complete the online questionnaire, or a completed questionnaire with its outcome. Every request has one `id` that never changes (`OH-{id}` is its `reference`), also after the candidate or you complete the questionnaire; an older questionnaire that has no request has `id: null` and is addressed as `form-{submission_id}`. `status` is always one of six client statuses (`submitted`, `awaiting_candidate`, `rejected`, `full_clearance`, `temporary_clearance`, `fail`); staff-only statuses are never returned.
