operations.summary: Get the questionnaire of a request
operations.description:
Returns the questionnaires of one request, the ones a candidate (or you, on their behalf) has to complete, with every question and how to answer it, and where each form stands. `{id}` is the request `id` from `POST /requests` or `GET /requests`; a request of another client, or an older questionnaire with no request (`form-{id}`), answers `404 not_found`. The forms are the ones the request's clearance type derives; they cannot be chosen.

`request.accepts_answers` says whether answers can be sent now. When it is false, `request.blocked_by` has the reason as an error code: `request_not_online` (the request has a paper questionnaire, or Hub has no form for its clearance type) or `request_closed` (an outcome is already recorded). Each form has a `state`: `due` (not sent), `saved` (the candidate saved it and has to upload documents themselves: it cannot be sent through the API), `submitted`, `resubmit` (rejected, to be sent again) or `more_info` (the reviewer asked for more information), with `can_submit` telling you whether to call `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers` for it. A form that was sent has its `submission_id`, `submission_reference`, `submitted_at` and `submitted_by` (`candidate`, or `client_api` when it was sent through this API). The state is the candidate's: a form the candidate sent within the last 90 days counts for every request that names it.

The answers are not returned here: they are health data, read with `GET /requests/{id}/answers`. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

operations.summary: Submit the answers to a questionnaire for a candidate
operations.description:
Sends one questionnaire of a request for the candidate, on their behalf, exactly as if the candidate had filled it in and sent it. `{id}` is the request `id` and `{shortcode}` one of its forms (`GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`; the forms follow from the request's clearance type and cannot be chosen). Send the answers as an object of question `key` to answer in `answers`, in the shapes `answer_format` describes, and the supporting documents in `documents` when the questionnaire needs them (`multipart/form-data`; otherwise JSON works). No defaults are filled in: send every question that is shown. A request with several forms has one call per form, in any order.

The answers are validated with the same checks as the candidate's own form: required questions, types, lengths, the options of a choice, date and phone formats, structured answers, and conditional questions (a question that is hidden by another answer is not required and its answer is dropped). Every problem comes back together as `422 validation_failed` with one message per question under `details` as `answers.{key}` (so `answers.is_epp`), and `documents` for a file problem. An answer to a key that is not a question of the form is `422` too, so a mistyped key is never silently lost. Nothing is saved when the call is refused.

A questionnaire that needs documents (`documents_required`) must come with at least one file in this call: the API has no saved-draft step, so a form is either sent whole or not at all. The files are stored with the candidate's submission like the ones a candidate uploads (JPG, PNG or PDF, up to 20 files of 8 MB each, see `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`). An account that does not allow uploads cannot send documents (`422` on `documents`).

On success the state is what the candidate's own submission produces: the candidate's questionnaire is saved with its reference and the status `proc` (the request's client status becomes `submitted`, or stays `awaiting_candidate` while another form of the request has still to be sent), the candidate's last form is updated, credits are taken when credit deduction is switched on (a new starter's first submission; a short balance never blocks it; see `GET /credits`), the Fit to Work request is emailed to Healthier Business with its documents once the request's first form is in (the candidate is not emailed anything), and the webhook `occupational-health.request.questionnaire_completed` is queued with `submitted_by` `client_api` (ids and statuses only, never an answer). Hub records that you, not the candidate, sent it: the API key and the key owner are stored with the submission and appear in the activity trail, and `submitted_by` is `client_api` in this answer and in `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`. Hub also queues the legacy form callback of the account, if it has one, as for any submission. The response holds ids and statuses only; read the answers back with `GET /requests/{id}/answers`.

Conflicts, each with its own code: `409 request_not_online` (the request has a paper questionnaire or no Hub form), `409 request_closed` (an outcome is already recorded), `409 form_not_assigned` (the form is not assigned to the candidate), `409 form_already_submitted` (the candidate, or an earlier call, already sent this form within the last 90 days), `409 form_awaiting_documents` (the candidate saved it and has to upload their documents). A shortcode that is not one of the request's forms is `404 not_found`, and `503 service_unavailable` means the answers could not be saved and nothing was sent: send them again.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and sends nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Only a successful answer is remembered. Without it, repeating a call that succeeded is `409 form_already_submitted`. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:write`. Neither the answers nor the response are written to the API log.

credits.description: Not charged by this call as a payment. When credit deduction is on (GET /credits shows deducting), a new starter's first submitted questionnaire costs credits_per_new_starter credits, taken from the balance in the same place the candidate's own submission takes them; renewals are free. A short balance never blocks the call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

parameters.name: shortcode
parameters.description: The questionnaire shortcode, from `GET /forms` (or `forms[].shortcode` of a questionnaire answer). A shortcode outside the client's form set is a 404, and so is one that is not a form of the request when you submit answers.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: The fields of `POST /requests/{id}/questionnaire/{shortcode}/answers`: the answers to one questionnaire, and its supporting documents when it needs them. Send `multipart/form-data` (needed for files; write the answers as `answers[key]=value`, and a list as `answers[key][]=value`); a JSON body `{ "answers": { "key": value } }` also works when no files are sent, and is the easier way to send structured answers. The keys and the shape of each answer come from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`.

answers.description: The answers, an object of question `key` to answer. Required (send an empty object when every question is optional and you have no answers). Take the keys and the shape of each answer from `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire` (`answer_format`): a text or a choice is a string, a tick box is true or false, a multiple choice is a list of option values, a date range is two dates, a rating grid is an object of row to column, a repeating group is a list of rows and a signature is a PNG data URL. Send every question that is shown; a question left out counts as unanswered, and a required one then fails with `422` on `answers.{key}`. A key that is not a question of the questionnaire is `422` as well. No defaults are filled in for you. With `multipart/form-data` send `answers[key]=value` and `answers[key][]=value` for a list.

documents.description: Supporting documents for the questionnaire, up to 20 files. Needed (at least one) when the questionnaire says `documents_required` in `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`; not accepted when the account does not allow uploads (`422` on `documents`). Send as `multipart/form-data` (`documents[]`). Allowed types are JPG, PNG and PDF, up to 8 MB each: the limits are in `documents.upload` of the questionnaire answer. The files are stored with the candidate's submission exactly like the ones a candidate uploads.

schema.title: OhSubmitAnswersBody

operations.description:
Returns one request in full: the same row as the list plus `review_note` (the reviewer's note for you, for example why a request was rejected), `issued_at` (when a clearance was issued), `next_renewal` (the date the clearance expires, `YYYY-MM-DD`) with `renewal_state` (`valid`, `expiring` or `expired`), and `candidate_status`, the candidate's account status. The renewal fields are set once a clearance has been issued.

`{id}` is a request id such as `5` (the id from `POST /requests` or the list, the same before and after the questionnaire is completed) or `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request. A request of another account, or one that does not exist, answers `404 not_found`, never `403`. The questionnaire answers are not part of this answer: read them with `GET /requests/{id}/answers`, and what the candidate still has to complete with `GET /requests/{id}/questionnaire`.

The view is recorded in the Occupational Health access trail, with the API key as the actor and ids only, and the call is written to the API log without its request and response bodies. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. This is health data. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request id, an integer such as `5`: the same before and after the candidate completes the questionnaire. The request read endpoints (`GET /requests/{id}`, `/answers`, `/documents`, `/ftw`) also accept `form-{submission_id}` for an older questionnaire that has no request; the questionnaire endpoints take a request id only.

operations.description:
Returns the five counters above the Requests table in Hub: `total`, `submitted` (with Healthier Business), `awaiting_candidate`, `cleared` (full plus temporary clearance) and `rejected_or_fail`. Requests that are still waiting for the candidate and requests with a completed questionnaire are counted together, using the same six client statuses as the list, so the numbers match the table. There are no filters: the counts are always for the whole account.

Use it for a dashboard tile or to decide whether to read the list at all. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:requests:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Returns the account's Occupational Health settings exactly as the Settings page in Hub shows them, so an integration can display or check them. `notifications` and `document_upload` repeat the profile; `return_email` is the address a completed questionnaire is returned to and `copy_emails` the addresses copied on it (comma separated, empty when none). `allow_upload` is whether candidates and your team may upload documents, and `allow_temporary_clearance` whether temporary clearance may be recorded for your requests.

`chase` describes how a candidate who has not completed their questionnaire is reminded by email: `first_reminder_days` after the request, then every `interval_days`, at most `max_emails` reminders, nothing more after `stop_after_days`, and `notify_on_limit` says whether you are told when the limit is reached. `emails` lists the notification addresses of the account with their `purpose` and `type`.

The settings cannot be changed through the API: they stay on the Settings page in Hub. The key needs the scope `occupational-health:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Returns where the candidate stands with their training access, worked out by Hub: `groups` (one per course group the candidate has: `group_id`, `title`, `payer`, `status`, `expires_at` and `renewal`), the `terms` (`accepted`, `version`, `accepted_at`), the `renewal` block (`mode` is `auto` or `manual`, `open_request` says a renewal request waits for approval) and a `quote` for starting the groups that need access. `payer` is `client` when the account's credits pay for the group and `candidate` when the candidate pays; Hub decides it and it cannot be changed through the API. `status` is `not_started`, `payment_pending`, `awaiting_approval`, `active`, `expiring` or `expired`; the candidate can open courses only in `active` and `expiring`.

`quote.agency` (null when no group needing access is agency-paid) holds `credits_needed`, the `balance` the account can spend, `can_afford` and the credits per group. `quote.candidate` (null when none is candidate-paid) holds the price in pence (`net_pence`, `vat_pence`, `gross_pence`, and per group), and `allow_24_months` with `gross_pence_24_months` when the account lets candidates pre-pay a second year. To start access call `POST /candidates/{candidate_ref}/access/start`. Another client's candidate, an unknown one and a malformed `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, charged or sent.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

operations.summary: Get a candidate payment link's status
operations.description: Returns where a payment link created by `POST /candidates/{candidate_ref}/access/start` stands: `status` is `pending` (the candidate can still pay), `paid` (HB Pay confirmed the payment and the access is on), `expired`, `superseded` (a newer link replaced it), `refunded` (the payment was refunded and the access taken back) or `cancelled` (the groups no longer needed paying for). The answer never holds the link itself. Another client's candidate or payment, an unknown id and a malformed one answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:read`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

parameters.name: payment_id
parameters.description: The payment_id of the record (integer).

operations.description:
Starts the candidate's access to the course groups that need it, as the candidate's own Start button does, and answers what happened. Hub decides who pays each group (the group's setting, else the candidate's `training_charge`); the request cannot change it, and a candidate-paid group is never paid from credits. Agency-paid groups are charged to the account's credits in one transaction (nothing is taken when the balance does not cover them all), groups that cost nothing are opened free. `group_ids` (optional) limits the start to some of the candidate's groups that need access now; leave it out to start every one. `months` (`12` or `24`, default `12`) only matters for candidate-paid groups and is used only when the account allows the 24 month option.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters) so a retry after a lost answer starts and charges once: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; only a success is remembered. A second call without a key finds nothing left to start and answers `none`. Each call that switches access on queues one `online-training.access.started` webhook. At most 30 calls a minute per key and 5 a minute per candidate; more is `429 rate_limited`. Two optional daily stops per key can be switched on for the account's integration: a cap on the credits it may spend through the API and a cap on the access starts, each answering `429 credit_cap_reached` or `429 start_cap_reached` before anything is charged (off by default).

When some groups are candidate-paid the call also creates a one-time payment link: `payment.url` is a Hub page you give to the candidate (it is shown only in this answer). The candidate agrees to the payment terms and pays through HB Pay; only HB Pay's confirmation switches the access on, and then `online-training.access.started` fires with `source` `payment`. The link works for 7 days or until it is paid, and a newer link for the same candidate replaces it (the older one is `superseded`). Read its status with `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/access/payments/{payment_id}`. `return_url` (optional) must be on one of the origins registered under Developer, Embed; the payment pages then offer a "Back to" button to it.

Send `max_credits` (decimal, optional) to refuse a start that costs more than you expect: when the credits the account would pay now are higher the answer is `409 quote_changed` (`details` holds the current `credits_needed`, `balance` and `can_afford`) and nothing is started, charged or created (no payment link either). Leave it out and the call behaves as before.

Answers: `200` with `outcome` `enabled` (`credits_charged`, `balance_after` and the `groups` switched on with their `expires_at`), `none` (nothing needed access), `payment_required` (the candidate pays for the groups: `payment` holds the link; nothing else was started) or `partial` (the same, and the groups the account pays were started: see `started`). Errors: `402 insufficient_credits` (nothing was charged or started; `details` has `needed` and `available`), `409 renewal_list_required` (the account requires candidates to be on its renewal list), `409 renewal_approval_required` (a manual renewal needs approval: the request is recorded and the agency emailed once; `details` has `state`, `payer` and `next`), `503 payments_unavailable` (card payments are not set up, so no link was created and nothing was started), `422 validation_failed` for a `group_ids` entry that is not one of the candidate's groups needing access, a bad `months`, or a `return_url` that is not on one of your registered origins. Another client's candidate and an unknown `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:access:write`.

parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

group_ids.description: The course groups to start, a subset of the groups that need access now (see `GET .../access`). Default: every group that needs access.

months.description: `12` or `24`. Only matters for candidate-paid groups, and 24 is used only when the account allows it. Default 12.

return_url.description: Where the payment pages may send the candidate back to (a "Back to" button). Must be on one of your registered embed origins. Only used when the candidate pays.

max_credits.description: The most credits this start may take from the account (decimal). When the live quote is higher the call answers `409 quote_changed` with the current quote and starts, charges and creates nothing. Candidate-paid groups cost no credits and do not count. Optional.

operations.description:
Streams a combined training certificate as a PDF (`application/pdf`, shown inline, never cached) for the candidate's completed courses, with a file name such as `training-certificate-000123-261028.pdf`. `type` chooses which completions go on it: `current` (the default: completed, not expired, and still assigned), `assigned` (completed and still assigned, expired ones included), `excl-expired` (completed and not expired, assigned or not), `all` and `incl-expired` (every completion on record), `range` (completed between `date_from` and `date_to`, both required, UK dates, the last day included), `course` (the latest completion of one course, `course_id` required), and `care` or `cstf` (every completion, with the care or CSTF headings when the account uses them, otherwise the standard certificate). There is one line per completion on record, so a course renewed several times appears once per completion except under `course`.

When no completed course matches, the answer is `422` with the code `no_certificates`, not an empty PDF: change the `type` or the dates. A `date_to` before `date_from`, a missing `date_from`, `date_to` or `course_id` for its type, or an unknown `type` is `422 validation_failed` on that field. Another client's candidate, an unknown one and a malformed `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The certificate is the one Hub produces; the call only reads, nothing is stored or emailed, and the `online-training.certificate.issued` webhook is for certificates staff supply in Hub, not for this call. The key needs the scope `online-training:certificates:read`.

parameters.description: Which certificate: `current` (default), `assigned`, `all`, `excl-expired`, `incl-expired`, `range` (needs `date_from` and `date_to`), `course` (needs `course_id`), `care` or `cstf`.

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.description: With `type=range`: the first day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UK date).

parameters.name: date_to
parameters.description: With `type=range`: the last day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UK date), not before `date_from`.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: With `type=course`: the course id.

operations.summary: Set the courses of a candidate
operations.description:
Sets the exact list of courses the candidate should have, exactly as the Assign Courses page in Hub does: courses in `course_ids` that the candidate does not have are added, assigned courses that are not in the list are removed (their results and history are kept, and no credits are refunded), courses already assigned are left alone, and `[]` removes every course. Instead of `course_ids` you can send `candidate_group_id`, and the courses of that candidate group (limited to courses the account may assign) are assigned; the group is also saved on the candidate. Settings you leave out (`training_charge`, `renewal_mode`, `renew_training`, `send_reminders`, `framework_id`, `fixed_renewal`) keep the candidate's current values; a candidate who is new to Online Training starts from the account's defaults. `framework_id` and `fixed_renewal` are ignored unless the account lets candidates choose them.

Who can be assigned: a Hub candidate of the account (`candidate_ref` from `POST /hub/candidates`). If the candidate has no Online Training record yet, one is made first, as the Hub pages make it: the account's candidate with the same email is adopted, otherwise a new record and learner login are created, and the candidate keeps the same `candidate_ref`. The activation email is sent for a new login unless `send_activation_email` is false or the account activates candidates by hand. Every course id is checked against the catalogue (`GET /courses`) before anything is written or created: one that is not available is `422 validation_failed` on `course_ids` and nothing changes.

Side effects: the candidate is emailed about the courses added (as in Hub), and the webhook `online-training.course.assigned` is queued for the added courses. Nothing is sent when nothing is added. Repeating the same call changes nothing, so it is safe to retry after a lost answer; the call does not take `Idempotency-Key`.

Credits: by default agency-paid credits are taken when the candidate starts a course group, so `credits_charged` is normally 0. When the account is set to charge at assignment and the credits are not enough, the answer is `402 insufficient_credits` with `needed` and `available` (credits) in `details`, and no course is written (a candidate record made by this same call stays, without courses). Check `GET /credits` first. Other errors: `404 not_found` for an unknown or other client's `candidate_ref`; `422` on `candidate_group_id` for a group that is not one of the account's active groups, and on any field with an invalid value. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:write`.

credits.description: Agency-paid credits are normally taken when the candidate starts a course group, so credits_charged is usually 0. When the account charges at assignment, an unaffordable assignment answers 402 and writes nothing.

parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

schema.description: The courses and settings of the candidate. The list in `course_ids` (or the courses of `candidate_group_id`) is the full set the candidate should have afterwards: courses not in it are removed. Settings left out keep the candidate's current ones (a new candidate starts from the account's defaults); send only what you want to change.

Required unless `candidate_group_id` is sent; `[]` removes every course. Every id must be in `GET /courses`, otherwise `422` on `course_ids` and nothing is written. Duplicates are ignored.

candidate_group_id.description: One of the account's active candidate groups (a saved set of courses). When `course_ids` is left out, the courses of the group (with group placeholders expanded, and limited to courses the account may assign) are assigned. The group is also saved on the candidate. A group that is not one of the account's active groups is `422` on this field. Send `null` or leave it out to change no group.

training_charge.description: Who pays for the training: `client` (agency-paid, taken from the account's credits, normally when the candidate starts a course group) or `candidate` (the candidate pays). Left out: the candidate's current setting, or the account's default for a new candidate.

renewal_mode.description: `auto` to renew the candidate's training automatically with reminder emails (this is also what puts them in the `training.expiring` and `training.expired` webhook events), `manual` to leave renewal to you. Left out: the current setting, or the account's default for a new candidate.

renew_training.description: The old v1 flag: true puts the candidate on automatic renewal (`renewal_mode` `auto`, unless `renewal_mode` is sent); false puts them on `manual`.

send_reminders.description: Whether renewal reminder emails are sent to the candidate. Left out: the current setting.

framework_id.description: The course framework, only when the account lets candidates choose one (otherwise ignored, as in Hub).

fixed_renewal.description: The fixed renewal option (`0`, `1` or `2`), only when the account lets candidates choose it (otherwise ignored, as in Hub).

send_activation_email.description: Used only when this call has to create the candidate's course record and login: false creates it without emailing the activation link. Default true; the email is also skipped when the account activates candidates by hand. Ignored for a candidate who already has a record.

operations.summary: Send a reminder email to a candidate
operations.description:
Emails the candidate a reminder through Hub's mailer, as the Send Reminder buttons in Hub do. `email_type` is `training_reminder` (their training needs attention; sent with the account's reminder wording and an opt-out link) or `course_completion_reminder` (they have courses not completed yet; the email lists them, and the answer's `incomplete_courses` says how many). The answer is `{ "data": { "email_type", "message" } }`, and for the second type also `incomplete_courses`. It confirms the email was queued, not that it was delivered or read.

Each successful call sends one email, and nothing limits how often you may call, so avoid reminding the same person repeatedly. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters) so a retry after a lost answer does not send it twice: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`; only a success is remembered.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` on `email_type` when the type is not one of the two, when the candidate has no email address, or (for `course_completion_reminder`) when the candidate has no incomplete courses to remind them about. Another client's candidate and an unknown `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:emails:write`.

operations.description:
Lists the account's candidates who have Online Training (candidates that were archived are left out), ordered by first name, then last name unless you sort. A candidate is identified by `candidate_ref`, the uuid of the Hub core API, where candidates are created and edited; here you only read their training. Each row has identity (read only), `account_status` (`active` once the candidate has activated their login, `pending` before), `training_status`, the counts of courses assigned, completed and expired, who pays (`paid_by`), `renewal_mode`, `completed_at` and `expires_at`. `training_status` is null for a candidate with no course assigned.

Filters: `search` (every word must match the first name, last name or email), `candidate_ref` (one candidate; an unknown or other client's reference gives an empty list, not an error), `status` (`up_to_date`, `expiring_soon`, `expired` or `not_completed`; only candidates with courses are matched), `enrolled` (`true` for candidates with courses, `false` for none), `course_id` (candidates who have that course assigned) and `expires_from` / `expires_to` (on `expires_at`, each bound a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `expires_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

A candidate who exists in Hub but has never been given online training is not listed (assign a course to start them). The status buckets are the ones Hub stores for its dashboard, so a filtered list matches the dashboard tiles. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

A candidate who has completed everything therefore gets an empty list. `sort` accepts `course_name`, `module_id`, `assigned_at`, `completed_at` and `expires_at`; prefix with `-` for descending (the default order is by module name). Another client's candidate, an unknown one and a malformed `candidate_ref` answer `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `online-training:renewals:read`. operations.description:
Approves the renewal of a candidate on manual renewal, as the Approve button in Hub does: the agency-paid course groups whose access has run out are charged to the account's credits in one transaction (nothing is taken when the balance does not cover them) and their access starts again; the candidate stays on manual renewal, so the next renewal needs approval again. The open request, if any, becomes `approved`; with none, an approved request is recorded (`source` `client`). Queues `online-training.access.started` (`source` `renewal`, `started_by` `api`) for the groups really renewed and `online-training.renewal.approved`, each once. The answer is the approved request.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters) so a retry after a lost answer approves and charges once: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; only a success is remembered. A second call without a key finds nothing due and answers `409 nothing_due`. At most 30 calls a minute per key and 5 a minute per candidate; more is `429 rate_limited`, and an account that switched on the daily credit cap answers `429 credit_cap_reached` when the approval would pass it.

Send `max_credits` (decimal, optional) to refuse an approval that costs more than you expect: when the live quote is higher the answer is `409 quote_changed` (`details` holds the current `credits_needed`, `balance` and `can_afford`) and nothing is charged.

Errors: `409 not_manual` (the candidate is on auto renewal), `409 nothing_due` (no access has run out and no renewal date has passed), `402 insufficient_credits` (nothing was charged or changed; `details` has `needed` and `available`), `404 not_found` for another client's or an unknown candidate. The key needs the scope `online-training:renewals:write`.

operations.description:
Declines the candidate's open renewal request. operations.description:
Returns one candidate with a summary of their training and the courses assigned. The candidate fields are those of the list; `summary` counts the courses by state (`total`, `completed` including expiring and expired ones, `needs_renewal` for expired ones, `expiring_soon` and `not_started`) and `courses` lists every assigned course with its latest result (status, grade, dates and whether a certificate is available), the same rows as `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}/results`. Use it to answer "where does this person stand" in one call.

`{candidate_ref}` must be a uuid. A malformed value, an unknown candidate, another client's candidate and a Hub candidate who has no Online Training record yet all answer `404 not_found`: there is no training to read until a course is assigned with `PUT .../courses`. The key needs the scope `online-training:candidates:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: The candidate's `candidate_ref`: the uuid the Hub core API gives the person (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Another client's candidate, or a malformed value, is a 404.

operations.summary: List the courses the account can assign
operations.description:
Lists the courses in the account's catalogue, the only courses `PUT /candidates/{candidate_ref}/courses` accepts: use a course `id` in `course_ids`. Each row has the course `id` and `name` and the training pack it belongs to (`group_id`, `group`; both null for a course outside a pack). A course the account has not been given is not listed and is refused on assignment.

Filters: `search` (part of the course name, case-insensitive, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `name` and `group`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25); the catalogue is short, so the default page often holds all of it. The key needs the scope `online-training:courses:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`, `group`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Every word must match the candidate name or email (courses: the course name).

operations.description:
Returns the credit balance the account can spend (`balance`: the pool owner's balance when the account shares a pool), the credits used since the start of the current calendar month in UK time (`used_this_month`) and the credit packages that can be bought (`packages`, each with `credits` and integer-pence prices `price_pence`, `vat_pence` and `total_pence`, `currency` `GBP`). Credits are units, not money, and can hold fractions (`2.5`); only the packages carry money.

The API cannot buy credits: top-ups are paid for in Hub, and the balance changes by itself when candidates start courses. Use `GET /credits/transactions` for the ledger behind the balance. The key needs the scope `online-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the credit ledger, newest first: one row per movement, with its `description` (for example `Credits used`), the credits moved (`amount`, always positive; `is_credit` is true for credits added and false for credits used), the `balance` after it and the candidate it belongs to (`candidate_ref` and `candidate_name`, both null for a movement with no candidate, such as a top-up). When the account shares a credit pool, only the pool's top-ups and the charges of the account's own candidates are listed, so the rows do not add up to the pool's whole history.

Filters: `type` (`all`, the default, `credit` or `debit`) and `created_from` / `created_to` (the first and last day, as `YYYY-MM-DD` UK dates: `2026-10-05` covers 00:00 to 23:59:59 UK time). The list has a fixed order (newest first) and cannot be sorted: a `sort` parameter is `422`. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). The key needs the scope `online-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Credit transactions: `all`, `credit` (credits added) or `debit` (credits used). One of: `all`, `credit`, `debit`.

operations.description:
Returns what the Online Training dashboard in Hub shows, so an integration and the screen always agree: the `tiles` (candidates with training, how many are up to date, expiring soon and expired, and `updated_at`, when the stored statistics were last refreshed), `compliant_pct` (the share that is up to date as a whole percentage, 0 when nobody has training), `needs_attention` (at most five candidates who need action first: expired ones, then those expiring soon, then those who have not completed) and `recent_activity` (the latest five course completions). People are named by `candidate_ref`, so you can open them with `GET /candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

The tiles come from statistics Hub stores per candidate and refreshes in the background, not from a live count of every course, so they can lag a recent change by a short time; `updated_at` says how fresh they are. The expired and expiring buckets can overlap, so the tiles need not add up to `total`. The key needs the scope `online-training:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.summary: Create an embed session for a course or test
operations.description: Creates a session that lets the Healthier Business SDK show a course (`kind: course`) or its test (`kind: test`) to one candidate inside your own page. The course must be assigned to the candidate, still to do (not passed, or passed and due for renewal) and delivered by Course Studio. `origin` is the address of the page that will show it (`https://learn.example.com`, scheme, host and port only) and must be one of the origins your account allows. The answer holds a single-use `launch_token` valid for 5 minutes, the `frame_url` and the `session_id`; pass the token to the SDK in the browser and never put it in a link. A course and its test are separate sessions. Each key may create or refresh sessions for one candidate 10 times a minute (`429 rate_limited`, `Retry-After`). Errors: `404 not_found` for an unknown candidate or a course the candidate does not have, `409 course_not_embeddable` for a course that Course Studio does not deliver, `409 course_not_pending` for a course the candidate has finished, `409 course_access_required` when their access has not been started, `409 payment_pending` when they have a payment link that is not paid yet, `409 renewal_approval_required` when a manual renewal waits for your approval (the request is recorded and your agency is emailed once), `409 access_expired` when their access has ended and must be renewed, `422` for an origin that is not allowed. The four access errors carry `details` with `state` (`not_started`, `payment_pending`, `awaiting_approval` or `expired`), `payer` (`client` or `candidate`) and `next` (`start_access`, `pay`, `await_approval` or `renew`), so you know what to do. The key needs the scope `online-training:embed:create`. Nothing is charged and no access is started.

schema.description:
`POST /embed/sessions`: the course or test of one candidate to show inside your own page, and the page's origin. The key's scope is the
permission.

kind.description: What to show: `course` for the course content, `test` for its test. They are separate sessions; create the test session when the candidate reaches the test.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate, by their `candidate_ref` (the uuid of the Hub core API). Must be a candidate of your account who has the course.

course_id.description: The course, by its `id` from `GET /courses`. It must be assigned to the candidate, still to do, and delivered by Course Studio.

origin.description: The website that will show it, as scheme, host and port only. It must be one of the origins your account allows (Developer, Embed). https is required, except for localhost.

schema.title: OtCreateEmbedSessionBody

operations.description: Issues a new single-use launch token for a session that is still open and kills the previous one. Call it from your server when the SDK asks for a new token (the frame is about to lose access). A finished session answers `409 session_finished` and an expired one `410 session_expired`; start a new session then. The key needs the scope `online-training:embed:create`.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The session_id of the record (integer).

operations.description:
Returns the Online Training account the key belongs to: its `id` and `name`, who pays for candidates' training by default (`training_charge`: `client` means the account's credits, `candidate` means the candidate pays), and `shares_credits_with`, the id of the account that owns the credit pool when this account shares another account's balance (null when it has its own). Use it as a first call to check that the key reaches the account you expect.

`credits` is the credit count stored on this account itself, in whole or part credits. When `shares_credits_with` is set the credits you can actually spend are the pool owner's, so read `balance` from `GET /credits` rather than this field. A client that has no Online Training account gets `403 portal_unavailable` on this and every other call of the portal. The key needs the scope `online-training:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the manual renewal requests of the account's candidates, newest first: one row per request with its `status` (`requested` waits for approval, `approved` renewed the access, `declined` was refused), who asked (`source`: `candidate`, `client` or `embed`), when it was asked, approved or declined, the credits an approval took and the `reason` of a decline. A candidate on manual renewal has one open request at a time; asking again after an approval or a decline records a new one.

Filters: `status` (`requested`, `approved` or `declined`) and `candidate_ref` (one candidate; an unknown or other client's reference gives an empty list, not an error). The list has a fixed order (newest first) and cannot be sorted: a `sort` parameter is `422`. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). To act on a request use `POST /candidates/{candidate_ref}/renewal/approve` or `.../decline`. The key needs the scope `online-training:renewals:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only candidates whose training has this status. One of: `requested`, `approved`, `declined`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only rows for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API.

operations.description:
Invites a Hub candidate to book a place that the account pays for, with the same steps as the Invites page: the funds are checked, the invitation is made, and it is sent at once. The candidate receives an email with a one-time link that is valid for 8 weeks; the invited name and address are taken from the Hub candidate (the candidate must have an email address, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`: add it with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`). The course is the one set for the account; you do not choose it, and the candidate chooses the session. `contact_name` and `contact_email` are optional: the person at the account who is copied in on the email. The link is also returned as `url`.

Typical sequence: create the invitation, wait for `practical-training.booking_invite.opened` (the candidate opened the link; sent once) and `practical-training.booking_invite.used` (the candidate booked; the booking then follows its own `booking.*` events), and read the result with `GET /booking-invites/{invite}`. Withdraw an unused invitation with `DELETE /booking-invites/{invite}`. Webhook sent by this call: `practical-training.booking_invite.sent`.

Credits and money: nothing is charged by this call. The place is paid for, with credits or balance, only when the candidate books. This call only checks that the account can pay: with booking credits for accounts that pay for invitations with credits, otherwise with the booking balance. When it cannot, the call answers `402 insufficient_credits` with `available` (`pays_with`, `balance_pence`, `credits`) beside the error, and no invitation is made. Some accounts are allowed to send invitations without funds.

A candidate invited in the last month is not invited again (unless the earlier invitation's booking was cancelled): the call answers `409 conflict`, no email is sent and no invitation is kept. Accounts without booking invitations get `403 invites_not_enabled`. An unknown candidate is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does not send a second email; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header a repeat inside the month is a `409 conflict`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

credits.description: Not charged by this call. The call only checks that the account can pay for the place (booking credits, or booking balance, depending on the account); the place is paid for when the candidate books. A short balance is 402 insufficient_credits.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /booking-invites`: invites a Hub candidate (the email comes from the candidate). The contact is the person at the
client who is copied in, as on the Invites page.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (uuid) of the person to invite: a candidate of your account in the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Required. The invited name and email address are taken from this candidate. An unknown candidate, or one without an email address, is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; add the address with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

contact_name.description: The name of the person at your account who is copied in on the invitation email. Optional, at most 150 characters. When left out, nobody is named.

contact_email.description: The email address of that contact, who is copied in on the invitation email. Optional, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. When left out, nobody is copied in.

schema.title: PtStoreBookingInviteBody

operations.description:
Withdraws an invitation: the candidate's link stops working at once and the invitation disappears from the list (a later `GET /booking-invites/{invite}` answers `404 not_found`). `{invite}` is the invitation id. No email is sent to the candidate and no webhook event is sent. Nothing is charged or refunded, and a booking that was already made with the link is not affected. Use it for an invitation that is still `unsent` or `waiting`; an invitation that is already `used` can be withdrawn too, but the booking it made stays.

The answer is `{"data": {"id": 17, "withdrawn": true}}`. An invitation of another client, or one that does not exist or has already been withdrawn, answers `404 not_found`, so the call is safe to repeat. Accounts without booking invitations get `403 invites_not_enabled`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: invite
parameters.description: The booking invitation id (integer).

operations.description:
Lists the invitations the account has made, newest first by default. An invitation is an email with a one-time link that lets one candidate choose a session and book a place that the account pays for. `status` is `unsent` (created but not sent), `waiting` (sent, not yet used) or `used` (the candidate booked; `booking_id` is then set). Filter with `state` (the same three values), `candidate_ref` (a Hub candidate of the account, matched on the invited email address; otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `search` (part of the invited name or email, at most 100 characters), `created_from` and `created_to` (when the invitation was made) and `used_from` and `used_to` (when the booking that used it was made); a date alone is a UK calendar day, a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant. `sort` accepts `id` and `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending; the default is newest first). The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Only accounts that have booking invitations switched on can use this endpoint; for any other account it answers `403 invites_not_enabled`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Part of the invited name or email address as saved on the invitation. At most 100 characters.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: used_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `used` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `used_to`.

parameters.name: used_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `used` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `used_from`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only invitations in this state: `unsent` (made, not sent), `waiting` (sent, not yet used) or `used` (the candidate booked).

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only invitations to this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid of one of the account's Hub candidates, matched on the invited email address. An unknown candidate is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

operations.description:
Returns one invitation: the invited candidate, its status, the course, the contact who is copied in, the candidate's link (`url`, only while the link still works, otherwise `null`), when the link expires, and the booking made with it once it is used. `{invite}` is the invitation id. An invitation of another client, one that does not exist, and one that has been withdrawn answer `404 not_found`.

Only accounts that have booking invitations switched on can use this endpoint (`403 invites_not_enabled` otherwise). The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: invite
parameters.description: The booking invitation id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns the public booking page address that you can give to candidates so that they book a place on this account themselves (for example in an email or on your own site), together with the account's Sage contact id that the address is built from. The link opens the Practical Training booking page for your account: the candidate chooses a session and pays or is invoiced as the page allows. It is not a one-time link. To send one candidate a personal one-time link that books a place you pay for, create a booking invitation instead (`POST /booking-invites`, only for accounts that have invitations switched on).

When the account has no Sage contact id, `booking_url` and `sage_contact_id` are both `null`: the account has no booking link and you should ask Healthier Business to set one up. There is no fallback to a general open link.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:account:read` and the client must have a Practical Training account (`403 portal_unavailable` otherwise). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Cancels a booking that holds a seat (`booking_status` `booked` or `rescheduled`) and returns the booking with its new status `cancelled`, or `refunded` when money or credit was paid back. The seat is released, the cancellation email is sent to the candidate with the agency copied in, and the webhook event `practical-training.booking.cancelled` is sent (once, with the final status and a `refund` object). There is no body.

What is paid back goes to the original payment method, by these rules (48 hours is measured to the session's start): a booking paid with `credits` gets its credit back, and one paid with `balance` gets its price back to the booking balance, when the session is 48 hours or more away, or when it is inside 48 hours and the account still has a free cancellation this month; otherwise nothing is returned (the cost is logged on the booking, nothing is charged automatically). A booking paid by card (`candidate_pays`) is refunded to the card: nothing inside 48 hours, 20% when the candidate has already used the online training, otherwise everything the card paid. An `invoice` or free booking has nothing to return, so it becomes `cancelled`. `refund` on the answer (and in the webhook) says what was returned: `method` (`credits`, `balance` or `card`), `amount_pence` and `currency` (or `credits`), and `partial`; it never shows card details.

Errors: `404 not_found` for a booking that is not the account's. `409 conflict` when the booking cannot be cancelled: it does not hold a seat (already cancelled or refunded, or a `pending` candidate-pays booking that has not been paid, which has no seat to release) or its session has already started. `503 service_unavailable` when a card refund is due and the payment provider did not make it: the booking is then left untouched, so you can call again. The call is safe to repeat: a booking is refunded at most once, and the second call answers `409 conflict`.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns the attendance certificate of a booking as a PDF file (`Content-Type: application/pdf`, shown inline, named `TDTA_{booking id}.pdf`). A certificate exists once any recorded training day of the booking is `passed` or `present`; the booking's `certificate_available` field tells you in advance. Before that, the call answers `409 conflict` with the message "The certificate is not available yet.". A booking of another client answers `404 not_found`. The PDF is generated on request and nothing is charged or sent. The webhook event `practical-training.booking.certificate_available` tells you when `certificate_available` turns true (a training day is recorded `passed` or `present`), and when access to the certificate was bought or granted.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Books the place you hold (`hold_hash`) for a Hub candidate (`candidate_ref`), exactly as the Bookings page does. The session is the one the hold was made on; it is not sent again. The attendee's first name, last name, email, phone and job role (the candidate's first role) are taken from the Hub candidate; you do not send personal data. A candidate without a first name, an email address or a phone number answers `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` with a message that names what is missing: add it with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}` and call again. Typical sequence: `GET /training-events`, `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`, `POST /bookings`.

`pay_option` decides how the place is paid for. `credits` takes one booking credit for the course and `balance` takes the session price from the booking balance; both are taken now, inside the same transaction as the booking, and the booking is confirmed at once (`booking_status` `booked`, `pay_status` `completed`). `invoice` (or `inv`) confirms the booking at once without taking credits or balance; it is allowed only when invoicing is switched on for the account and the session price is within the account's credit limit. `candidate_pays` leaves the booking `pending`, emails the candidate a payment link (with the agency copied in) and returns the same link as `payment_url`; the booking is confirmed when the candidate pays, and until then it holds no seat, so it cannot be cancelled through the API. When the candidate does not pay, the scheduled housekeeping (when it is running) sets the booking to `abandoned` after two days, or six hours before the session if that is earlier. Too few booking credits for the course, or too little balance for the price, is `402 insufficient_credits` (`available` shows `pays_with`, `balance_pence`, `credits` and `price_pence`); invoicing that is not switched on, or a price over the credit limit, is `422 booking_rejected` with the reason in `message`. Check `GET /credits` first.

For a confirmed booking the seat is taken, the confirmation emails are sent to the candidate and to the agency (`agency_email` when you send it, otherwise the account's notification address; `agency_contact_email` is stored on the booking as the contact and is used as the agency address for some accounts), Healthier Business is notified, and the webhooks run. Webhooks: `practical-training.booking.created` for every new booking, and `practical-training.training_event.seats_low` when the session is nearly full. A `candidate_pays` booking later sends `practical-training.booking.confirmed` when it is paid. The held place is removed once the booking is made; if the booking is rejected, the hold is kept so you can correct the call.

Other errors: `422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash` when the hold does not exist, belongs to another account or has expired (create a new hold), and on `candidate_ref` when it is not a Hub candidate of the account. A full session is `422 no_places_left`, as it is when you hold a place. `422 booking_rejected` also covers a session that is no longer open for booking, and a candidate who already has a pending, booked or rescheduled booking on the same session (matched on email).

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does not book twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Only a successful answer is remembered. Without the header, repeating a call that succeeded fails because its hold is gone. The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:write`.

credits.description: Taken by this call when pay_option is credits (one booking credit for the course) or balance (the session price from the booking balance), and the booking is confirmed at once. invoice adds to invoicing; candidate_pays charges the candidate when they pay. Too few credits or too little balance is 402 insufficient_credits; invoicing that is not allowed is 422 booking_rejected.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /bookings`: books a held place for a Hub candidate. The attendee's name, email, phone and job role come from the Hub
candidate and are not sent; the session is the one the hold was made on; the key's scope is the permission.

hold_hash.description: The `hold_hash` returned by `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`. Required. It must be a live hold of your own account: a hold that does not exist, has expired, belongs to another account or has already been used is `422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash`. The booking is made on the session the hold was made on. A successful booking removes the hold; a rejected booking keeps it.

candidate_ref.description: The `candidate_ref` (uuid) of the person to book: a candidate of your account in the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). Required. The attendee's first name, last name, email, phone and job role (the candidate's first role) are taken from this candidate. An unknown candidate, or one without a first name, an email address or a phone number, is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`; add the missing detail with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`.

pay_option.description: How the place is paid for. Required. `credits`: one booking credit for the course is taken now. `balance`: the session price is taken from the booking balance now. `invoice` (or its alias `inv`): the booking is confirmed and invoiced, if invoicing is switched on for your account and the price is within its credit limit. `candidate_pays`: the booking stays `pending` and the candidate is emailed a payment link, which is also returned as `payment_url`. Too few credits or too little balance is `402 insufficient_credits`; invoicing that is not allowed is `422 booking_rejected`. Check `GET /credits` first.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your account who is responsible for the booking (the agency contact). Required, at most 150 characters. Stored on the booking.

agency_contact_email.description: The email address of the agency contact. Required, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. Stored on the booking; for some accounts it is the address that receives the agency emails.

agency_email.description: The address that receives the agency's confirmation email for the booking. Optional, a valid email address, at most 255 characters. When left out, the account's notification address is used.

operations.description:
Lists the account's practical training bookings, whoever made them (this API, the Bookings page, a booking link or an invitation), newest first by default. Each row carries the course, the location, the session dates, the booking and payment status, the price recorded on the booking, the attendance result and whether a certificate is available. Session times (`start_date`, `end_date`) are UTC instants with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC, so a 09:00 session in British Summer Time is `08:00:00Z`. The candidate is shown as `candidate_ref` (the Hub candidate uuid) plus the name on the booking; the email, phone and job role are not returned: read them from the Hub candidate. `candidate_ref` is `null` for a booking made for someone who is not a Hub candidate of this account.

Filters: `status` (`pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled`, `refunded`, `abandoned`; send it more than once, as `status[]=booked&status[]=pending`, for several; unknown values are ignored), `course_id`, `location_id`, `candidate_ref` (must be a Hub candidate of the account, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (the session start; a date alone such as `2026-07-01` is that whole UK calendar day, a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant), `created_from` and `created_to` (when the booking was made; a date alone is a UK calendar day, which in British Summer Time starts at 23:00Z the day before), `upcoming=true` (the session has not started) or `past=true` (it has started), `attendance` (`passed`, `present` or `absent`) and `search` (part of the candidate's first name, last name or email on the booking, at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, newest first), `start_date` and `status`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Compared with the session's start. Must not be after `start_date_to`.

Must not be before `created_from`.

operations.description:
Returns one booking in full: the list row plus the trainer (`trainer`, with `id` and `name`, or `null`). `{booking}` is the booking id. A booking of another client, or one that does not exist, answers `404 not_found`. A booking made through this API has `booked_by` set to `Agency`. When the booking is the candidate's to pay and was created by this API, the payment link is returned only in the answer of `POST /bookings`, not here.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns the practical training courses that are currently offered, ordered by name, with the price this account pays for each (`client_rate_pence`, integer pence; `0` when the account has no rate of its own for the course) and the course length in hours. Use the course `id` to filter sessions (`GET /training-events?course_id=`) and bookings. The list is short and fixed, so one page holds every course; `page` and `per_page` are accepted for consistency with the other lists. `sort` accepts `course_name` (prefix with `-` for descending).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `course_name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-course_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.summary: Get the booking credits and balance
operations.description:
Returns what the account can currently spend on bookings. Practical Training has two kinds of prepayment and this call shows both. `booking_credits` lists, for each course that still has credits, the number of credits left: a credit is one place on that course, it is a count of places, not money, and it can be fractional (a late reschedule fee can take part of a credit). Courses with no credits left are not listed. `booking_balance_pence` is the booking money balance in integer pence (`currency` is `GBP`); it can be zero or negative.

Use this call before you create a booking with `pay_option` `credits` or `balance`, to check that the account can pay: a booking that cannot be paid that way is rejected with `422 booking_rejected`. When the balance or a course's credits fall to a low level or to zero, the webhook events `practical-training.balance.low`, `practical-training.balance.depleted`, `practical-training.credits.low` and `practical-training.credits.depleted` are sent. You cannot top up through the API.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:credits:read` (moved here from `account:read`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.summary: List the credit and balance movements
operations.description:
Returns the ledger of the account's prepayments, newest first by default: one row for every confirmed deposit (a top-up or an adjustment) and every withdrawal (a booking paid with credits or balance, or a reschedule fee). Only confirmed movements are listed. A row belongs either to the booking money balance (`wallet` is `booking_balance`, and `amount_pence` holds the money) or to one course's credits (`wallet` is the course id as text, and `credits` holds the credit units). The amount is always positive; `type` says whether it was added (`deposit`) or taken out (`withdraw`). `description` and `booking_id` come from the movement's own record and are null when it has none.

Filter by `wallet` (`booking_balance` or a course id such as `12`), by `type`, and by date with `created_from` and `created_to` (a date such as `2026-10-01` is a UK calendar day, so the range runs from UK midnight of the first day to the end of the last UK day, an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time; a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant). Sort by `id` or `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending). A wallet value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page, not an error. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-01`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range starts at UK midnight of that day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this moment. A date alone (`2026-10-31`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day (an hour earlier in UTC during British Summer Time); an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: `booking_balance` for the money balance, or a course id (for example `12`) for that course's credits. At most 100 characters. A value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only movements of this type: `deposit` (money or credits added) or `withdraw` (money or credits taken out).

operations.description:
Holds one place on a session for 30 minutes so that you can collect the candidate's details and then book it with `POST /bookings`. The hold has no body; the session is the `{event}` in the path. The answer contains the `hold_hash`, which you send to `POST /bookings` as `hold_hash`, the time the hold ends (`expires_at`) and the seconds left (`expires_in_seconds`).

An account may hold only one place at a time. While a hold is live, a second call answers `409 conflict` and the body carries the existing hold in `hold`, so you can use it or release it with `DELETE /training-events/hold/{hash}`. A session with no free place answers `422 no_places_left`. A session that does not exist, is not open for booking or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`.

A hold does not take a seat and does not charge credits or balance; nothing is sent to the candidate. The seat is taken, and the account charged, only when the booking is created, and the places can be taken by other bookings in the meantime, so a booking can still fail with `422 booking_rejected` even with a live hold. A hold that is not used ends after 30 minutes. When the scheduled clean-up has removed it, the webhook event `practical-training.slot_hold.expired` is sent; the clean-up runs about every five minutes, but a hold already counts as expired from `expires_at` (booking with it answers `422` on `hold_hash`).

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (at most 255 characters): repeating the call with the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of answering `409 conflict` because of your own hold. Without the header, a retry after a lost answer is a `409` that carries your hold.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:holds:write`.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The training event id (integer).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

operations.description:
Returns the sessions that this account can book: sessions that are active, not hidden, and start in the future, and that are either public or were created for this account (another client's private session is never listed). Each row shows the course, the location, the start and end time, the number of places still free (`remaining_slots`) and the price this account pays for one place (`cost_inc_vat_pence`: the account's rate for the course when it has one, otherwise the session's own price). Session times (`start_date`, `end_date`) are UTC instants with a `Z`: the session's UK local time converted to UTC, so a 09:00 session in British Summer Time is `08:00:00Z`.

This is the first step of booking: choose a session here, hold a place on it with `POST /training-events/{event}/hold`, then book with `POST /bookings`. `remaining_slots` is a snapshot; a place is only taken when the booking is made (holding does not reserve a seat), so the session can still fill before you book. Narrow the list with `course_id`, `location_id`, `start_date_from` and `start_date_to` (a date such as `2026-11-01` is a whole UK calendar day, from the start of the first day to the end of the last; a date-time with `Z` or an offset is that instant) and `available_only=true` (only sessions with at least one free place). `sort` accepts `start_date` (the default, earliest first), `remaining_slots` and `cost`; prefix with `-` for descending. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: Only sessions that start on or after this moment.
