Compared with the session's start. Must not be after `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only sessions that start on or before this moment. A date alone (`YYYY-MM-DD`) is a whole UK calendar day, so the range ends at the last second of that UK day; an ISO 8601 date-time with `Z` or an offset is that exact instant (without an offset it is read as UTC). Compared with the session's start. Must not be before `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: Only sessions of this course (the `id` from `GET /courses`).

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: Only sessions at this location (the `id` from `GET /locations`).

parameters.name: available_only
parameters.description: `true` returns only sessions with at least one free place (`remaining_slots` above 0). `false` or leaving it out also lists full sessions.

operations.description:
Releases a held place before it expires, so that the account can hold another (an account may hold one place at a time). `{hash}` is the `hold_hash` returned when the place was held. Call it when the candidate decides not to book. Releasing is not needed after `POST /bookings`: a successful booking removes its hold itself. A hold that does not exist, has already been used or released, or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`. A hold that has passed its `expires_at` but has not yet been cleaned up is released normally.

Nothing is charged and no webhook event is sent. The call is naturally repeatable: the second call answers `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `practical-training:holds:write`.

parameters.description: The hold token returned when the place or timeslot was held.

operations.description:
Returns one bookable session with the same fields as the list plus the trainer (`trainer`, with `id` and `name`, or `null` when no trainer is assigned yet). `{event}` is the session id from `GET /training-events`. A session that does not exist, is inactive, hidden, already started, or belongs to another client answers `404 not_found`; the response does not say which. Check the `remaining_slots` value again just before you hold a place.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The training event id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns the training locations (name and address), ordered by name, so that you can offer candidates a place to choose and filter sessions with `GET /training-events?location_id=`. `search` matches part of the location name (at most 100 characters). `sort` accepts `location_name` (prefix with `-` for descending). The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `practical-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `location_name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-location_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.description: Part of the location name. At most 100 characters.

operations.description:
Returns the Practical Training account that the API key belongs to: the Hub client id, the account name, the contact and the email addresses held on the account, and whether the account is active. Use it once after you obtain a token to confirm that the key is attached to the account you expect. Everything else in this API is scoped to this one account, and you cannot read another client's data through it.

The key needs the scope `practical-training:account:read`, and the client must have a Practical Training account, otherwise every call of this portal answers `403 portal_unavailable`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The calls of this portal share a throttle of 120 requests a minute per access token (`429 rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header when you exceed it), in addition to the hourly limit per key that applies to every v2 call.

operations.summary: Download a reference as a PDF
operations.description:
Streams the PDF report of a completed reference: the candidate, the referee, the answers and, when the account uses scoring, the score. Use it to keep a copy of the reference in your own records. If the stored file is missing (for example for an older imported reference) it is built from the stored answers for this response only and is not saved, so the call changes nothing; the answer is the same file layout either way. The file is sent as an attachment named `reference-{referee-name}-{uuid}.pdf`.

Your key needs `references:referees:read` and your account must use the References portal. Only a `completed` reference has a PDF: for any other status, or a completed reference with no stored answers, the answer is `404 pdf_not_available`. An unknown referee, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Check `has_pdf` on `GET /referees/{uuid}` first if you want to avoid the error. The PDF contains personal data of the candidate and the referee: store it securely.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Sends one referee a reminder email with their link, adds 1 to their `reminder_count` and queues a `references.reference.reminder.sent` webhook. Use it to chase a single referee; use `POST /requests/{uuid}/reminders` to chase everyone who is due. The same rules apply as for the whole request: the referee must have been emailed and not yet completed, declined, expired or bounced, their request must be open, and they must have had fewer reminders than your References settings allow and be due one (the first falls due a set number of days after the request email, each later one a set number of days after the previous; in the standard settings 5 days, then every 3 days, at most 3).

Your key needs `references:requests:write` (the same scope as the other calls that send emails) and your account must use the References portal. When no reminder can be sent the answer is `409 reminder_not_sent`, and the `message` names the referee and the reason (for example that the next reminder is not due until a date, or that the maximum has been reached). An unknown referee, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Each successful call sends an email, so do not retry a successful call; a retry after a lost answer is refused until the next reminder is due.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Returns one referee's reference in full: the referee's details, the status, the answers as the form asks them (once the referee has submitted), the score and its breakdown when your account uses scoring, the reason for declining when the referee declined, and the sent, opened, submitted and reminder times. Fetch it when a `references.reference.submitted` or `references.reference.declined` webhook arrives (the webhook carries the `reference_uuid`, not the answers).

Your key needs `references:referees:read` and your account must use the References portal. A referee that does not exist, or whose request belongs to another account, answers `404 not_found` (never `403`). Read only: no email, no webhook.

This record holds personal data of a third party and what they wrote about the candidate: the referee's name, email and phone, free-text answers and, if they declined, their reason. Store and display it with the same care as a written reference. The referee's private link to the form is never returned by the API (it works as a credential), so there is no `form_url`; to prompt a referee use `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder`, which emails them their link. The answers omit the referee's own contact details, which are in `referee`. `score` and `score_breakdown` are empty (`null` and `[]`) when the account does not use scoring.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Stops a request you no longer need. The request becomes `cancelled`, which is final: the API cannot reopen it (create a new request instead). Every referee who has not completed or declined (their status is `pending`, `sent`, `opened` or `in_progress`) becomes `expired`, and a `references.reference.expired` webhook is queued for each of them; there is no separate cancelled event. Referees are not emailed about the cancellation. A closed request takes no more answers, referees or reminders. Referees who already completed or declined keep their reference, and you can still read and download it.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. A request that is already `completed` or `cancelled` cannot be cancelled: the answer is `409 request_not_cancellable` with the reason in `message`. An `expired` or `in_progress` or `pending` request can be. An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Repeating the call on a cancelled request is the `409 request_not_cancellable` above, not a success.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Asks for references for one candidate. Choose who gives the referee details with `collection_mode`. With `client_adds` you send the `referees` in the same call: each referee is emailed at once with their private link to the form, and the request becomes `in_progress`. With `candidate_provides` you send no referees: the candidate is emailed a link to a page (the `submission_url` in the answer) where they enter up to the number of referees required; each is then emailed automatically. If the candidate has no email address no email is sent and the call still succeeds; give the candidate the `submission_url` yourself. Referees then answer in their browser: they submit the form or decline. You are told by webhook, and you can read the outcome from the request, the referee and the referee's PDF.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` (add `references:requests:read` to read it back) and your account must use the References portal. The `candidate_ref` must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` (not a 404). Numbers outside the limits, and a `collection_mode` that is not `client_adds` or `candidate_provides` (`both` included), are `422 validation_failed` on the field. A request the references engine refuses answers `422 reference_request_refused` with the reason in `message`: the form is not available to you, `collection_mode` is not one your References settings allow, a `client_adds` request has no referee or has two with the same email address, and so on. A duplicate request for the same candidate is not refused: check `GET /requests?candidate_ref=` first if you want to avoid it.

Side effects: the referee emails above; an activity log entry; and the webhook `references.reference.request.created` is queued once the request exists (the referee emails are queued before it). No credits are charged. The request expires `expiry_days` days from now; nothing happens to it at that moment except that referees can no longer answer and the status becomes `expired`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and creates and emails nothing again; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header every call creates a new request and emails the referees again. The referee details are personal data of third parties: Hub stores them to send the request and to show you the outcome, and they are never put in a webhook.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

candidate_ref.description: The candidate the references are for: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API (`GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`). It must be one of your candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

collection_mode.description: Who gives the referee details: `client_adds` (you send them in `referees`) or `candidate_provides` (the candidate is emailed a link to enter them). The value `both` is not accepted: it is `422 validation_failed` on `collection_mode`, so choose one. A way your References settings do not allow is refused with `422 reference_request_refused`.

template_id.description: The form the referees complete: an `id` from `GET /templates`. When omitted, the request takes your default form (set in References settings). An id that is not available to your account is refused with `422 reference_request_refused`.

references_required.description: How many completed references the request needs. At least your References settings' minimum (and never less than 1) and at most their maximum; the standard settings are 2 and 5. When omitted it is your minimum. A value outside your limits is `422 validation_failed`.

expiry_days.description: Days from now until the request expires: 1 to 365. When omitted it is your References settings' default (14 days in the standard settings).

notes.description: A note stored with the request and shown to your staff, at most 1000 characters. It is not sent to referees by the API call. When omitted there is no note.
examples: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

referees.description: The referees to ask, 1 to 10. Required when `collection_mode` is `client_adds`: every referee is emailed at once. For `candidate_provides` the list is ignored (the candidate gives the referees); you may omit it. Each item has `referee_name`, `referee_email`, `referee_organisation` and `referee_position` (all required) and `referee_phone` and `relationship_to_candidate` (optional). Two referees must not share an email address (compared without regard to case), otherwise `422 reference_request_refused`.

referee_name.description: The referee's full name, at most 255 characters. It appears in the request email and on the reference PDF.

referee_email.description: The referee's email address, a valid address of at most 255 characters. The request and any reminders are sent here. It must differ from the address of every other referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case).

referee_organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for, at most 255 characters.

referee_position.description: The referee's job title or position, at most 255 characters.

referee_phone.description: The referee's telephone number, at most 50 characters. Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, at most 255 characters (for example "Line manager"). Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

example.notes: Care assistant post, start date 2 November.

operations.description:
Gives referees more time. The new expiry is `days` days after the current `expires_at` when that is still in the future, otherwise `days` days from now. The request goes back to `pending` and its status is recalculated, so an `expired` request becomes live again. Every referee who has not completed, declined or bounced gets the new expiry, and a referee who had expired is reopened (back to `sent`, or `pending` if they were never emailed) and can use the same link again. Nothing is emailed and no webhook is fired: remind the referees yourself if you want them to act.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. `days` is required, 1 to 365, otherwise `422 validation_failed`. A `completed` or `cancelled` request cannot be extended (`409 request_not_extendable`), nor can an imported legacy request that nobody answered and that has no expiry date (`409 legacy_request_unanswered`; contact support). An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. The answer is the updated request.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

days.description: How many days to add: a whole number from 1 to 365. It is added to the current expiry when that is still in the future, otherwise to now.

operations.description:
Returns the reference requests of your account, newest first unless you pass `sort`, in the standard list envelope (`data`, `meta`, `links`). Each row is the full request, including its referees, so one call is enough to show progress for many candidates. Use it to find the request of a candidate (`candidate_ref`), to see which requests are still open (`status`), or to find requests that expired or were fully referenced.

Your key needs the `references:requests:read` scope and your account must use the References portal, otherwise the answer is `403 insufficient_scope` or `403 portal_unavailable`. Only requests of your own account are returned; a request of another account never appears. This call is read only: it sends no email and fires no webhook.

`candidate_ref` must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref` (not an empty list). `created_from` and `created_to` accept a date (`2026-10-01`) or an ISO 8601 time; a date means the whole day. Without `sort` the order is newest first. The response contains personal data of the candidate (name, email) and of each referee (name, email, phone); handle it accordingly.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `expires_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. It is matched as a part of the text (not word by word) against the request notes, the candidate's first name, last name, name and email, and each referee's name and email.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows with this status. One of: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `expired`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only requests for this candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise the answer is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: collection_mode
parameters.description: Only requests that collect referee details this way: `client_adds` or `candidate_provides`. Any other value, including `both`, is `422 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: is_expired
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only requests that are expired: those with status `expired` and those whose `expires_at` has passed. Send `false` to return only requests that are not (status other than `expired` and no `expires_at` in the past). Leave it out for both. Accepts `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; anything else is `422 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: is_fully_referenced
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only requests whose references are all in (status `completed`), `false` to return only the others. Leave it out for both. Accepts `true`, `false`, `1` or `0`; anything else is `422 validation_failed`.

operations.summary: Add a referee to a request
operations.description:
Adds one more referee to an open request and emails them straight away with their private link. Use it when a referee declined, expired or bounced and you want to replace them, when you need more referees than you first gave, or to add referees to a `candidate_provides` request yourself. The referee's status becomes `sent` and the request's status is recalculated (a `pending` request becomes `in_progress`). The referee will submit or decline in their browser, and you are told by the `references.reference.submitted` and `references.reference.declined` webhooks. Adding a referee does not itself fire a webhook.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. The request must be open: a `completed`, `cancelled` or `expired` request, or one past its `expires_at`, answers `409 request_not_open` (extend an expired one first). The email address of a referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case) is `409 referee_already_added`; a request that already has 10 referees who have not declined, expired or bounced is `409 referee_limit_reached`; an imported legacy request that nobody answered is `409 legacy_request_unanswered`. An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`; a field that fails validation is `422 validation_failed`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and adds and emails nothing again; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without it, repeating a call whose answer you lost is refused as a duplicate referee (`409 referee_already_added`), so keep the header. The answer is the new referee row; their answers and PDF are read later from `GET /referees/{uuid}`.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

referee_name.description: The referee's full name, at most 255 characters. It appears in the request email and on the reference PDF.

referee_email.description: The referee's email address, a valid address of at most 255 characters. The request and any reminders are sent here. It must differ from the address of every other referee of the request who has not declined, expired or bounced (compared without regard to case).

referee_organisation.description: The organisation the referee works for, at most 255 characters.

referee_position.description: The referee's job title or position, at most 255 characters.

referee_phone.description: The referee's telephone number, at most 50 characters. Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

relationship_to_candidate.description: How the referee knows the candidate, at most 255 characters (for example "Line manager"). Optional; when omitted it is stored as null.

operations.summary: Remind the referees of a request
operations.description:
Chases every referee of the request who is due a reminder, and tells you why the others were not. A referee is due when they have been emailed and not yet completed, declined, expired or bounced, the request is open, they have had fewer reminders than your References settings allow, and the waiting time has passed: the first reminder falls due a set number of days after the request email and each later one a set number of days after the previous (in the standard settings 5 days, then every 3 days, at most 3 reminders); a chase window in your settings can also close. The call does not override these rules, so calling it twice in a row sends nothing the second time. Each reminder is an email to the referee with their link, adds 1 to their `reminder_count`, and queues a `references.reference.reminder.sent` webhook.

Your key needs `references:requests:write` and your account must use the References portal. The answer is `200` even when no reminder is sent: `reminders_sent` is then 0 and `skipped` lists each waiting referee by name with the reason (for example that the next reminder is not due until a date). Referees who have finished are not listed. An unknown request, or one of another account, answers `404 not_found`. Use `POST /referees/{uuid}/reminder` to chase one referee. The scheduled automatic reminders, where they are switched on, count towards the same maximum.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Returns one reference request with its referees: the candidate, the form, the number of references required and completed, the expiry, the `submission_url` for a candidate-provided request, and a row for each referee with their status and reminder count. Poll this to follow progress, or react to the webhooks and fetch it when one arrives. The answers of a referee are not here: read them with `GET /referees/{uuid}`.

Your key needs `references:requests:read` and your account must use the References portal. A request that does not exist, or that belongs to another account, answers `404 not_found` (never `403`). Read only: no email, no webhook. The response contains personal data of the candidate and of the referees.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the record.

operations.description:
Returns the reference forms (templates) you can ask referees to complete: the active forms that belong to Healthier Business and are open to every client, and the active forms your own organisation created. Use an `id` from this list as `template_id` when you create a request (`POST /requests`); without it the request uses your default form, which is the one marked `is_default`. The list gives a summary of each form (name, description, number of questions); the questions themselves are not returned.

Your key needs the `references:templates:read` scope and your account must use the References portal. The list is short, so it is normally one page; it is returned in the standard list envelope and sorted by `name` unless you pass `sort` (`name` or `updated_at`, with `-` for descending). It has no filters or search. Read only: no email, no webhook.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `name`, `updated_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description: Marks one alert as handled: `acknowledged` becomes true and `acknowledged_at` is set to now. Nothing else happens: no email or webhook is sent and no check is run, and the worker is not changed. Acknowledging an alert that is already acknowledged is not an error and leaves its original `acknowledged_at`. The call returns the alert. An alert of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:write` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:write`.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: The alert id (integer).

operations.description: Acknowledges open alerts of the portal in one call. Send `ids` (up to 500 alert ids) to acknowledge those; send `type` to acknowledge every open alert of that type; send neither to acknowledge **every open alert of the portal**, so send an explicit `ids` or `type` unless that is what you mean. When `ids` is sent, `type` is ignored. Only open alerts of this portal and your account count: ids that do not exist, belong to another client or to the other portal, or are already acknowledged are skipped without an error. The answer is how many were acknowledged (`acknowledged_count`, possibly 0). No email or webhook is sent and nothing is checked or billed. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for more than 500 ids or an id that is not an integer. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:write` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:write`.

ids.description: The alert ids to acknowledge, up to 500, from `GET /alerts`. When present and not empty it decides which alerts are acknowledged and `type` is ignored.

type.description: An alert type: every open alert of this type in the portal is acknowledged (for example `rtw_share_code_expiry_14_days`). Ignored when `ids` is sent.

operations.description:
Lists the alerts of your account for this portal, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Registration Monitoring lists registration alerts (every type that does not start with `dbs_` or `rtw_`); DBS & Right To Work lists the `dbs_` and `rtw_` alerts. Acknowledged alerts are included: filter with `acknowledged=false` for the ones that still need a person, which is what a work queue should read. Further filters are `severity` (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`), `type` (an exact alert type, see `type` of an alert), `worker_id` and `created_from` and `created_to` (the day the alert was raised). `sort` orders by `created_at`, `severity` or `type`; the default is newest first.

Where alerts come from: each completed registration check that changes a worker's status, the first check of a worker, and a change of a regulator warning or condition flag raise one; the DBS Update Service raises one when a certificate shows new information or a non-blank certificate is found; the right to work check raises one when the result is no right to work, when a passport image cannot be verified or has a low authenticity score, and when a share code is invalid; and the expiry reminders raise right to work and share code alerts as an expiry approaches. A DBS or right to work alert also sends the `dbs-rtw.alert.raised` webhook. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. A DBS certificate number in an alert's text is always masked (only the last four characters show, for example `********7890`). The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `created_at`, `severity`, `type`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-created_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only alerts raised whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: acknowledged
parameters.description: `false` returns only open alerts (the ones that still need a person), `true` only acknowledged ones. Left out, both are returned. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Only alerts of this severity: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only alerts of this exact type, for example `registration_expired`. See `type` of an alert for the types of this portal. At most 100 characters; a value that is not a type returns an empty list.

parameters.name: worker_id
parameters.description: Only alerts about this worker: a worker id from `GET /workers`.

operations.description: Returns one alert of your account in this portal, with the worker it is about and, for a registration alert, the check that raised it. An alert of another client, or of the other portal (a DBS alert asked for in Registration Monitoring, for example), is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:alerts:read` or `dbs-rtw:alerts:read`.

parameters.name: alert
parameters.description: The alert id (integer).

operations.description: Lists the account's monthly bills, newest period first, 25 to a page by default. A bill that is still a draft is never shown; every other status is (`generated`, `amended`, `ready_for_collection`, `submitted_to_gocardless`, `paid`, `failed`, `cancelled`). Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`. `period_from` and `period_to` filter by the month the bill covers, and `sort` orders by `period_start` or `id`. Bills are read only here: the invoice PDF is `GET /billing/bills/{id}/invoice`, and payment is by Direct Debit set up in Hub. Both monitoring portals list the same bills. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `period_start`, `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-period_start`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: period_from
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `period_to`.

parameters.name: period_to
parameters.description: Only bills whose period starts on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `period_from`.

operations.description: Streams the invoice of one bill as a PDF named after the bill number (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). Only bills that are shown in `GET /billing/bills` have an invoice (a draft bill, a bill of another client, or an unknown id is `404 not_found`). It is the same invoice Hub gives you. Nothing is changed, sent or billed by the download. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

parameters.name: bill
parameters.description: The bill id (integer).

operations.description:
Returns what the account's monitoring costs. There are no per check or per credit charges in Registration Monitoring and DBS & Right To Work: one monthly subscription covers registration, DBS and right to work monitoring, and every active worker (a registration, a DBS-only or a right-to-work-only worker) counts once towards it. A check you ask for through the API is not billed on its own. The answer shows the free trial (it starts when the account's first worker is created and lasts one month), whether the account may run checks (`trial.eligible`: during the trial, or with Direct Debit set up and billing allowed, or under a manual access override), the billing type chosen, this month's estimate under each billing type from today's number of active workers and the pricing tiers in force. Amounts are integer pence with `currency` `GBP`.

The billing type is chosen once in Hub and the Direct Debit is set up there; the set-up link is never returned by the API. Both portals return the same figures. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:billing:read` or `dbs-rtw:billing:read`.

operations.summary: Show the raw data of a registration check
operations.description: Returns what the regulator's register returned for one check, as Hub stored it: `format` is always `json` and `content` is the parsed result (its fields depend on the regulator and can change without notice, so do not build on them; use the worker and check fields for decisions). It is the technical record behind a check and can contain personal data. `content` is null when nothing was stored for the check. A check of another client's worker, or of a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: check
parameters.description: The registration check id (integer), from `recent_checks` of a worker or `GET /workers/{worker}/verification`.

operations.description: Streams the stored file: a PNG screenshot, a page snapshot, or a PDF, depending on the file's `type`. The file is sent with `Content-Disposition: inline`, the media type recorded for its extension (PNG and JPEG images, PDF; a saved HTML page is sent as `text/plain` so it is never run in a browser; anything else as `application/octet-stream`), `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The file can contain personal data: store it as carefully as you store the worker's record. A file that is missing from storage, or belongs to another client's worker, is `404 not_found`. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The evidence file id (integer).

operations.description: Returns the details of one evidence file (type, name, media type, size, when it was captured and the check that captured it) without the file itself. Use `download_url` to fetch the file. A file of another client's worker, or of a worker of the other monitoring portal, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The evidence file id (integer).

operations.description:
Uploads a CSV (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB) and queues it. The call answers `202` with the import row at once and the file is read by a background job: poll `GET /worker-imports/{id}`. The first row of the file is the header; get the column names from `GET /worker-imports/template` and check a file first with `POST /worker-imports/preview`, which uses the same rules and stores nothing. `column_mapping` maps an expected field to the header it is read from (without it the import reads the headers as they are, so they must be the field names, and `first_name` and `last_name` must be present or the import fails; the import never guesses a mapping, so send the `suggested_mapping` of a preview as `column_mapping` to use it). `check_frequency` (default `monthly`), `monitoring_start_date` (default today), `consent_given` (default false) and `is_active` (default true) are used for every row that does not carry its own value.

Each row is validated with the same rules as the preview: a row that fails is counted in `failed_count` with its line number and message and the others go on. A row that names a worker that already exists (the same regulator and registration number; the same DBS certificate number for a DBS-only row; the same name and share code for a right-to-work-only row) updates that worker, restoring it if it was removed; any other row creates one. Imported workers are not linked to Hub candidates. DBS & Right To Work rows can enrol a DBS certificate (12 digits, with `dbs_surname`) and a right to work check by `share_code` only: other document types need an upload and cannot be imported. **A row's `consent_given` defaults to false**: an import does not require the consent that `POST /workers` requires, so send `consent_given` true only when the workers have agreed to be monitored. No webhook is sent for an import; the checks that follow raise alerts and webhooks as usual. The imported workers count towards the monthly bill while they are active.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and file within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same import) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of importing the file twice. The import is not limited to the portal of the path: a file whose rows are of the other portal's kind is processed all the same. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a `check_frequency` that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

file.description: The CSV file, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB. The first row is the header; blank rows are skipped.

column_mapping.description: Which header of the file holds each field, as an object: the key is an expected field (see `GET /worker-imports/template`), the value the header (compared in lower case, trimmed), or null or an empty string to leave the field unmapped. Send it as `column_mapping[first_name]=First name` in a multipart form. Without it the file's headers must already be the field names.

items.description: The file header that holds one field.

check_frequency.description: The check frequency for rows that carry none: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Default `monthly`.

monitoring_start_date.description: The monitoring start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for rows that carry none. Default today.

consent_given.description: Whether the workers have agreed to be monitored, for rows that carry no `consent_given` of their own. Default false: an import does not require consent, so set this to true only when the workers have agreed.

is_active.description: Whether the workers are monitored, for rows that carry no `is_active` of their own. Default true. An inactive worker is not checked.

operations.description: Lists the CSV imports of your account, newest first, 25 to a page by default (`sort` is `id` or `-id`). Both monitoring portals list all of the account's imports, not only those started in the portal of the path, because an import enrols each row for whatever the row contains (a registration, a DBS certificate or a right to work share code). Each row shows the state and the counts as `GET /worker-imports/{id}` does. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.description: A dry run of a CSV: send the same body as `POST /worker-imports` and get back the file's headers, the column mapping used (the one you sent, or a guess from the header names), the first five rows as they would be read, and how many of the rows would be imported or rejected, with the first message of each rejected row (at most 200). Only the first 1000 rows are validated (`truncated` says when the file has more); the real import handles every row. Nothing is stored, no worker is created or changed, nothing is queued, sent or billed, and the file is not kept, so a preview can be repeated freely while you fix the file. The expected columns are those of the portal of the path. Errors: `422 validation_failed` for a missing or oversized file, a file that is not `csv` or `txt`, or a value that is not allowed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:write` or `dbs-rtw:imports:write`.

file.description: The CSV file, `csv` or `txt`, at most 10 MB. The first row is the header; blank rows are skipped.

column_mapping.description: Which header of the file holds each field, as an object: the key is an expected field (see `GET /worker-imports/template`), the value the header (compared in lower case, trimmed), or null or an empty string to leave the field unmapped. Send it as `column_mapping[first_name]=First name` in a multipart form. Without it the file's headers must already be the field names.

items.description: The file header that holds one field.

check_frequency.description: The check frequency for rows that carry none: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Default `monthly`.

monitoring_start_date.description: The monitoring start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, for rows that carry none. Default today.

consent_given.description: Whether the workers have agreed to be monitored, for rows that carry no `consent_given` of their own. Default false: an import does not require consent, so set this to true only when the workers have agreed.

is_active.description: Whether the workers are monitored, for rows that carry no `is_active` of their own. Default true. An inactive worker is not checked.

operations.description: Returns the progress of one import: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), `progress` as a percentage, how many of the `total_rows` were turned into workers (`imported_count`) or rejected (`failed_count`), and the rejected rows in `errors` (line number and message, at most 1000). Poll it every few seconds after `POST /worker-imports` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`. An import of another client is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

parameters.name: import
parameters.description: The import id (integer).

operations.description: Returns the column names a CSV import understands for the portal of the path, in the order of the Hub template: use them as the header row of your file (or as the keys of `column_mapping`). Registration Monitoring expects the registration columns (`regulator`, `registration_number`, ...), DBS & Right To Work the DBS and right to work columns (`dbs_certificate_number`, `rtw_document_type`, `rtw_share_code`, ...). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:imports:read` or `dbs-rtw:imports:read`.

Returns the roles a Hub team member can be given (`client-admin`, `client-manager`, `client-officer`, `client-viewer`) with the permissions each holds for your account, and the catalogue of every permission grouped by area (the Hub core, and `registration-monitoring` and `dbs-rtw` among the services). The permissions include the changes the account's Owner made on the My Team page. It is read only: team members, their roles and the role permissions are managed in Hub, and the API does not list the members. Both monitoring portals return the same answer. Nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:team:read` or `dbs-rtw:team:read`.

Asks for up to 200 workers to be checked now, with the same rules and side effects as `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. Send `worker_ids`, or leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (at most 200: with more active workers the call is refused with `422 too_many_workers` and you must send `worker_ids` in batches of up to 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are silently left out, not reported. One job is queued per worker and track: in DBS & Right To Work a worker enrolled for both tracks gets two jobs unless you send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) to check one track only; in Registration Monitoring the only track is `registration`.

The answer is `202` with `jobs` (`worker_id`, `track`, `job_id`) for every check that was queued and `refused` for those that were not, each with the reason (a worker may be refused for the reasons in `POST /workers/{id}/verify`, while the rest are queued). Poll each `job_id` on `GET /verify/jobs/{job}`. When nothing at all could be queued the call answers `422 verification_refused` with the list in `details.refused`; when there is no active worker to check it answers `422 no_active_workers`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same job ids) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing the checks again; without it every call queues new jobs. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to check, at most 200. Leave it out to check every active worker of the portal (refused with `too_many_workers` when there are more than 200). Ids that are not active workers of your account in this portal are left out without an error.

track.description: Check one track only: `registration` in Registration Monitoring; `dbs` or `rtw` in DBS & Right To Work. Left out, every track each worker is enrolled for is checked, so a worker enrolled for both DBS and right to work gets two jobs.

operations.summary: Show the progress of a verification job
operations.description:
Returns the state of a job created by `POST /workers/{id}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed`), how many workers it handled (`processed_count` of `total_workers`), how many checks worked (`success_count`) and failed (`failed_count`), how many workers changed status (`status_changes_found`), when it started and ended, and `error_message` when it failed. Poll it every few seconds, not faster than your rate limit allows; a job stays readable after it ends. `completed` means the job ran, not that every check succeeded: look at `failed_count` and at the worker's check history.

A job belongs to the portal that created it: a registration job is only visible in Registration Monitoring, a DBS or right to work job only in DBS & Right To Work, and a job of another client is `404 not_found` (so is a job of the other portal). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: The verification job id (integer) returned by `POST /workers/{worker}/verify` or `POST /verify/batch`.

operations.description:
Starts monitoring one professional registration. The worker is created active, with the monitoring start date you give (today when you give none), the check frequency you give (the account's default for registrations, `monthly` when it has none) and consent recorded as given at this moment. The call returns the worker with `201`. It does not link the worker to a Hub candidate: `candidate_ref` is null, and a `hb_candidate_id` in the body is ignored.

If the same regulator and registration number were removed from your account earlier, that worker is restored (same id, earlier checks and alerts kept) and updated with the values you send, instead of a second one being created.

Nothing is checked by this call and nothing is charged by it. The first check is made by the next monitoring run, or at once when you ask for it with `POST /workers/{id}/verify`. When the check completes the worker gets its status, expiry date and restrictions, an alert is raised for the first result and the `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification` webhook is sent. Every later status change raises an alert and sends `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`. Monitoring is part of the account's subscription (see `GET /billing/usage`): the worker counts towards the monthly bill while it is active, and checks stop when the free trial is over and Direct Debit is not set up.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second worker, and the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. Without the header a repeated call is refused anyway when the registration is already monitored (`422 validation_failed` on `registration_number`).

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `consent_given` when it is not true (the worker must have agreed to be monitored), `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account, `date_of_birth` when it is missing for an NMC registration, `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: The worker to monitor: who they are and the registration to check. Send JSON. `first_name`, `last_name`, `email`, `regulator`, `registration_number` and `consent_given` are required, and `date_of_birth` is required when `regulator` is `nmc`. A field that is not listed is ignored.

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters. Required.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, free text, at most 255 characters.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. Required when `regulator` is `nmc` (the NMC check needs it, otherwise `422` on this field); optional for the other regulators.

regulator.description: The regulator whose register is checked, as a lower case key. Required. One of: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc`, `gcc`.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. Required. The same regulator and number cannot be monitored twice for one account (`422` on this field); a number that was removed earlier is restored.

profession.description: The worker's profession in your own words, at most 255 characters.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person in your organisation responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters.

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Left out, it is today.

consent_given.description: Must be true: the worker has agreed to be monitored. The call is refused with `422` on this field otherwise. Hub records the moment you made the call as the time consent was given.

notes.description: Free text notes about the worker, at most 5000 characters.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. Left out, the account's default frequency for registrations applies (`monthly` when the account has none).

operations.description: Removes the worker from your account: it is no longer listed, checked, billed or reachable on `/workers/{id}` (the id answers `404 not_found` afterwards). The worker is soft deleted, so adding the same regulator and registration number again with `POST /workers` restores it with its earlier checks and alerts. Removing a worker stops its future checks and webhooks; nothing is sent about the removal and no refund or charge is made by this call. Repeating the call for a removed worker is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

operations.summary: List the evidence files of a registration
operations.description:
Lists the files captured by the checks of one worker, newest first by default, 25 to a page by default. Each check of a registration can capture a screenshot of the regulator's register page and a saved copy of the page; an NMC check can add sanction PDFs and a GDC check determination PDFs for conditions or a caution. The evidence is what lets you show an auditor what the register said on the day. A worker with no files yet (one that has never been checked, for example) gets an empty list.

The rows carry `download_url`, which points to `GET /evidence/{file}/download`; the files are never served from a public address and need your bearer token. `captured_from` and `captured_to` filter by the day the file was captured, and `sort` orders by `captured_at`, `id` or `file_size`. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. Read only: nothing is checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:evidence:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `captured_at`, `id`, `file_size`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-captured_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: captured_from
parameters.description: Only files captured whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `captured_to`.

parameters.name: captured_to
parameters.description: Only files captured whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `captured_from`.

operations.description:
Lists the professional registrations your account monitors, 25 to a page by default (`per_page` 1 to 100), sorted by last name unless `sort` says otherwise. Every worker of the account that has a regulator is listed, active or not (`is_active` filters them); workers that are monitored only for DBS or right to work belong to the DBS & Right To Work API and are not shown. The list is scoped to the client of the API key, and a worker of another client never appears.

`search` takes words that must each match the first name, last name, email, registration number or profession. `regulator` is one of the fourteen regulator keys, `status` is a worker status or `not_checked` for a registration that has never been checked, and `check_frequency` is the schedule. `candidate_ref` narrows the list to the worker linked to that Hub candidate (only workers that Hub staff linked have one); a `candidate_ref` that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`. A filter value that is not allowed (an unknown regulator or frequency) is `422 validation_failed` too.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:read`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `last_name`, `first_name`, `next_check_due_at`, `last_checked_at`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-last_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. Every word must match (anywhere in the text, ignoring case) at least one of the fields searched: first name, last name, email, registration number, profession.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only workers created whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only the worker linked to this Hub candidate: the `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. Only workers that Hub staff linked to a candidate have one. A value that is not one of your Hub candidates is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: regulator
parameters.description: Only registrations of this regulator, as a lower case key. One of: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc`, `gcc`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only workers whose last check found this status: `active`, `lapsed`, `suspended`, `conditions`, `caution`, `removed`, `erased`, `registered_no_licence`, `not_found`, `manual_review`, `invalid_pin` or `error`. `not_checked` returns the workers that have never been checked successfully. At most 50 characters; a value that is not a status returns an empty list.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: `true` returns only workers that are monitored, `false` only workers that are switched off. `1` and `0` also work.

parameters.name: check_frequency
parameters.description: Only workers checked at this frequency: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly` (or `daily`, which some workers carry but which cannot be set through the API).

operations.summary: Change the monitoring settings of a worker
operations.description:
Changes how often a worker is checked and whether monitoring is on. Send at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`); a body with none of them is `422 validation_failed`. In Registration Monitoring `check_frequency` is the schedule of the registration. In DBS & Right To Work `check_frequency` sets every track the worker is enrolled for, and `dbs_check_frequency` or `rtw_check_frequency` sets one track and wins over `check_frequency` for it; a track the worker is not enrolled for is left alone.

Side effects: a changed frequency reschedules the next check of the track while the worker is active, counted from the last check (or the start date when there has been none) for a registration and from now for DBS and right to work, so the new `next_check_due_at` is in the answer. Switching a worker off (`is_active` false) clears every next check date and stops scheduled checks; switching it on again reschedules each track from its frequency. Nothing is checked immediately, no email, alert or webhook is sent, and nothing is charged by this call, but an active worker counts towards the monthly bill (`GET /billing/usage`), so switching a worker off removes it from the bill from then on.

The answer holds `registration` (Registration Monitoring) or `dbs` and `rtw` (DBS & Right To Work, null for a track the worker is not enrolled for). A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

schema.description: The monitoring settings to change. Send at least one field; a field you leave out keeps its value.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. The next check is rescheduled from the last check (or from the start date when there has been none).

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`; send null to clear it.

is_active.description: Whether the worker is monitored. False stops scheduled checks and clears every next check date; true again reschedules each track from its frequency.

operations.summary: Change the monitoring settings of several workers
operations.description:
Applies the same settings as `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings` to up to 500 workers in one call: send `worker_ids` and at least one of `check_frequency`, `monitoring_start_date` and `is_active` (and, in DBS & Right To Work, `dbs_check_frequency` and `rtw_check_frequency`). Every id must be a worker of your account in the portal of the path: if any id is not, the call changes nothing and answers `422 workers_not_found`. Repeated ids are counted once. The side effects per worker are those of the single call (rescheduled next checks, switching off clears the next check dates), and nothing is checked, sent or charged by the call itself.

The answer is the number of workers changed (`updated_count`). Errors: `422 validation_failed` for an empty or oversized `worker_ids`, a value that is not allowed, or a body with no setting to change; `422 workers_not_found` when an id is unknown, belongs to another client or to the other portal. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write` or `dbs-rtw:workers:write`.

allOf.description: The monitoring settings to change. Send at least one field; a field you leave out keeps its value.

check_frequency.description: How often the registration is checked: `weekly`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `six_month`, `nine_month` or `yearly`. The next check is rescheduled from the last check (or from the start date when there has been none).

monitoring_start_date.description: The date monitoring starts, `YYYY-MM-DD`; send null to clear it.

is_active.description: Whether the worker is monitored. False stops scheduled checks and clears every next check date; true again reschedules each track from its frequency.

worker_ids.description: The ids of the workers to change, 1 to 500 (repeated ids count once). Every id must be a worker of your account in this portal, otherwise nothing is changed and the call is `422 workers_not_found`.

operations.description:
Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the registration itself (regulator and number). Send only the fields to change; `PUT` and `PATCH` behave the same and a field you leave out keeps its value. How often and whether the worker is checked is not changed here: use `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

Changing `regulator` or `registration_number` points the worker at a different registration; the next check reads the new one, the checks already made stay in the history and nothing is re-checked by this call. No check, email, alert, webhook or charge is triggered by an edit. The call returns the worker as it is now.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account by another worker, `date_of_birth` when it is missing or emptied for an NMC registration (the NMC check needs it), `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. It is required for an NMC registration and cannot be cleared there; for the other regulators send null to clear it.

profession.description: The worker's profession, free text, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

notes.description: Free text notes, at most 5000 characters; send null to clear them.

regulator.description: The regulator key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`. Changing it points the worker at a register of another regulator.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. The regulator and number pair must not already be monitored for your account by another worker.

operations.description:
Returns one worker with its ten latest checks (`recent_checks`, newest first) and its ten latest alerts (`recent_alerts`). Use it to see where a worker stands; the full check history is `GET /workers/{id}/verification`, the alerts are `GET /alerts?worker_id=`, the captured files are `GET /workers/{id}/evidence`. A worker that belongs to another client, or that is a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

operations.description:
Changes who the worker is: name, contact details, date of birth, profession, compliance officer, notes and the registration itself (regulator and number). Send only the fields to change; `PUT` and `PATCH` behave the same and a field you leave out keeps its value. How often and whether the worker is checked is not changed here: use `PATCH /workers/{id}/monitoring-settings`.

Changing `regulator` or `registration_number` points the worker at a different registration; the next check reads the new one, the checks already made stay in the history and nothing is re-checked by this call. No check, email, alert, webhook or charge is triggered by an edit. The call returns the worker as it is now.

Errors: `422 validation_failed` with `details` naming the field: `registration_number` when the regulator and number are already monitored for your account by another worker, `date_of_birth` when it is missing or emptied for an NMC registration (the NMC check needs it), `regulator` when it is not one of the fourteen keys, and the usual type and length errors. A worker of another client, or a DBS or right to work worker, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:workers:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

first_name.description: The worker's first name, at most 255 characters.

last_name.description: The worker's last name, at most 255 characters.

email.description: The worker's email address, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

phone.description: The worker's telephone number, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

date_of_birth.description: The worker's date of birth, `YYYY-MM-DD`, before today. It is required for an NMC registration and cannot be cleared there; for the other regulators send null to clear it.

profession.description: The worker's profession, free text, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

compliance_officer_name.description: The person responsible for the worker's compliance, at most 255 characters; send null to clear it.

notes.description: Free text notes, at most 5000 characters; send null to clear them.

regulator.description: The regulator key: `nmc`, `gmc`, `hcpc`, `gdc`, `goc`, `gphc`, `ahcs`, `swe`, `sssc`, `scw`, `niscc`, `psni`, `gosc` or `gcc`. Changing it points the worker at a register of another regulator.

registration_number.description: The registration number (PIN) the regulator issued, at most 255 characters. The regulator and number pair must not already be monitored for your account by another worker.

operations.summary: List the check history of a worker
operations.description:
Lists every check made for one worker on one track, newest first, 25 to a page by default. In Registration Monitoring the track is `registration` and each row is a registration check (`status`, `status_changed`, `previous_status`, `expiry_date`, ...). In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`), which is required for a worker enrolled for both tracks (`422 track_required`, and `422 invalid_track` for any other value); a DBS row has the Update Service `status` and `has_evidence_pdf`, a right to work row has `status` (`has_right` or `no_right`), `method`, `expiry_date` and `has_screenshot`. A check that failed to reach a result is in the history with `result` `error` and does not change the worker's status. `checked_from` and `checked_to` filter by the day of the check and `sort` orders by `checked_at` or `id`.

Read only: nothing is changed, checked, sent or billed. A worker of another client or of the other portal is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:read` or `dbs-rtw:verification:read`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `checked_at`, `id`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-checked_at`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: checked_from
parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `checked_to`.

parameters.name: checked_to
parameters.description: Only checks made whose date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `checked_from`.

parameters.name: track
parameters.description: Ignored: Registration Monitoring has one track, `registration`.

operations.description:
Asks for one worker to be checked now instead of waiting for the schedule: a registration against the regulator's register (Registration Monitoring), or the DBS certificate against the DBS Update Service or the right to work against the Home Office service or the passport image (DBS & Right To Work). The call creates a verification job and answers `202` with its `job_id` at once; the check runs in the background. Poll `GET /verify/jobs/{job}` until `status` is `completed` or `failed`, read the result on the worker (`GET /workers/{id}`) and in its history (`GET /workers/{id}/verification`), and the evidence on `GET /workers/{id}/evidence`.

Registration Monitoring has one track (`registration`) and ignores `track`. In DBS & Right To Work send `track` (`dbs` or `rtw`) when the worker is enrolled for both; for a worker enrolled for one track it is optional. A `track` that is not `dbs` or `rtw` is `422 invalid_track`, and omitting it for a worker enrolled for both is `422 track_required`.

The rules are the ones a person pressing Re-check in Hub meets, and a refusal is `422 verification_refused` with the reason in `message`: manual re-checks are not enabled for the account, the worker is not active, the worker is not enrolled for the track, the account may not run checks (the free trial has ended and Direct Debit is not set up, or the regulator's connector is switched off or has used its monthly allowance), or the regulator's connector is paused. When the check ends it can change the worker's status: a change raises an alert and the `registration-monitoring.worker.status_changed`, `dbs-rtw.dbs.status_changed` or `dbs-rtw.rtw.status_changed` webhook, and the first registration result sends `registration-monitoring.worker.initial_verification`. A manual check is not charged separately: monitoring is part of the account's subscription (`GET /billing/usage`). Where the verification engine is switched off the request is only recorded: the job stays `pending` and no regulator is called.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat of the same key and body for the same worker within 24 hours returns the first answer (the same `job_id`) with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of queueing a second check; without it every call queues a new job. Another client's worker, or one of the other portal, is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `registration-monitoring:verification:write` or `dbs-rtw:verification:write`.

parameters.name: worker
parameters.description: The worker id (integer).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description: Registration Monitoring has one track, so the body can be left out.

track.description: Ignored: Registration Monitoring has one track, `registration`. Accepted so one client can serve both monitoring portals.

operations.description: Returns what the account can spend on verifications: `money_pence` (the money balance, VAT is added when it pays), `auto_credits` (automated verification credits, used by verification-only accounts; null for a regular account), `manual_credits`, and `legacy_balance_pence` (the older pounds balance that Healthier Business staff credit, shown as pence; null when the account has none and is not verification-only). `GET /pricing` says in which order a charge is taken from them. The API cannot buy credits or top up: that is paid for in Hub. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the movements behind the balances, newest first: each row has its `ledger` (`money`, `auto_credits`, `manual_credits` or `legacy_balance`), a `description`, the `amount` (always positive: pence for `money` and `legacy_balance`, a count for the credit ledgers; `unit` says which), whether it added to the ledger (`is_credit`: a top-up or a refund) or spent from it, and the `candidate_name` when the movement was for a verification. Filters: `ledger` (one of the four; without it the money and the two credit ledgers are listed together, the older balance only when asked for), and `created_from` / `created_to` (UTC days).
