The list has a fixed order and cannot be sorted. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only movements recorded on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only movements recorded on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before `created_from`.

parameters.name: ledger
parameters.description: Only this ledger: `money`, `auto_credits`, `manual_credits` or `legacy_balance`. Without it the money and credit ledgers are listed together; the older balance is only listed when asked for.

operations.summary: Get the price of each request type
operations.description:
Returns what a verification costs this account, for `auto` and `manual`, by the same rules that charge it when you create one: `free`, `net_pence`, `vat_pence` and `gross_pence` (integer pence, `GBP`) and a `reason` (a `code` and a `message`) that says why it is free or charged. The account type is read from the account, never from the request.

Who pays for what. A regular account (one that uses other Hub services), automated (`auto`) verification: free, reason `included_with_other_services`; it works with a zero balance and takes nothing. A regular account, manual verification: charged, reason `manual_verification_charged`. A verification-only account (it uses only Training Verification), automated verification: charged, reason `verification_only_account`. A verification-only account, manual verification: charged, reason `verification_only_account`.

A charge is the account's own price for the request type, or Hub's standard price when the account has none (automated 5, manual 10, in pounds, net). VAT (`vat_rate_percent`) is added when the money balance pays; the older pounds balance pays the net price. `funding_order` is the order a charge is taken from your credits and balances: the first that covers it pays. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Returns the account the key belongs to: its `id` and `name`, its `client_type` (`regular` for an account that also uses other Hub services, `verification_only` for an account that only uses Training Verification; read from the account and never from the request), the `request_types` you can submit (`auto` and `manual`) each with whether it is `free`, its net, VAT and gross price in pence and a `reason` that says why it is free or charged, the `limits` of a submission (largest file in kilobytes, accepted file types, longest `client_reference`), the `default_notify_email` that result emails go to when you send no `notify_email`, and how the API pays (`payment`: from credits and balances only, never by card). Use it as a first call to check that the key reaches the account you expect. A client that does not use Training Verification gets `403 portal_unavailable` on this and every other call of the portal. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Cancels a verification that is still `pending`, that is, that has not started processing: it becomes `rejected` with the reason code `cancelled_by_client`, the result email is not sent, and a charge is refunded to where it came from (a credit back to its credit ledger, money to the money balance, the older balance restored), which shows as `charge.refunded` true and the `training-verification.rejected` and `training-verification.refunded` webhook events. A free request has nothing to refund. A verification in any other status is `409 not_cancellable` (an automated one starts within minutes; a manual one is passed to staff). If the refund itself could not be made, the cancellation still stands and Healthier Business staff complete the refund; `charge.refunded` stays false until then. Returns the verification. The key needs the scope `training-verification:write`.

credits.description: Refunds the charge of the verification to where it came from; nothing new is charged.

parameters.name: verification
parameters.description: The verification id (integer), from the `id` of `POST /verifications` or `GET /verifications`. Another client's verification, or an unknown one, is a 404.

operations.description: Streams the certificate file you submitted, exactly as stored (`application/pdf`, `image/jpeg` or `image/png`), as an attachment, never cached. Opening it is written to the verification's timeline internally. A certificate that was submitted in Hub before this API existed, or whose file is no longer held, is `410 certificate_unavailable` (`certificate_available` on the verification tells you beforehand). The certificate is personal data: store the copy you download only as long as you need it. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Nothing is changed or charged.

parameters.name: verification
parameters.description: The verification id (integer), from the `id` of `POST /verifications` or `GET /verifications`. Another client's verification, or an unknown one, is a 404.

operations.description:
Submits one training certificate for verification and answers `202 Accepted` with the verification (`status` `pending`): the check runs afterwards, and the result arrives by webhook (`training-verification.verified`, `.not_found`, `.rejected`, `.failed`) and in `GET /verifications/{verification}`. Send the candidate (`candidate_name`, `candidate_email`), the `agency_name_on_cert` and the certificate: a file in a `multipart/form-data` request (field `certificate`), or, in a JSON request, `certificate_base64` with `certificate_filename`. The types (PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG) and the size limit (`GET /profile`) are those of the Hub form; the API never fetches a URL. `request_type` is `auto` or `manual`. Optional: `notify_email` (the result email goes there; it defaults to the account's first verification notification address, and is required when the account has none), `candidate_ref` (links one of your Hub candidates) and `client_reference` (your own reference, at most 100 characters, returned and sent in every webhook). Optional `max_credits` (decimal) refuses a request that costs more than you expect: it is the most the verification may cost as its net price in pounds (the price in `GET /pricing`, VAT not counted; `0` allows only a free request). When the live price is higher the answer is `409 quote_changed` (`details` holds the current `credits_needed`, `net_pence`, `gross_pence` and `currency`) and nothing is stored or charged. Leave it out and the call behaves as before.

Payment. The call charges your credits and balances only, by the rules of `GET /pricing`, and never starts a card payment. A `regular` account's automated (`auto`) verification is free and works with a zero balance; manual verification is charged on every account, and a `verification_only` account is charged for both. A charge is taken once, from the first of `credit` (verification-only accounts), `legacy_balance` and `balance` that covers it. When none does the answer is `402 insufficient_credits` with `details.required` and `details.available`, and nothing is stored or charged. The charge is on the answer (`charge`). A free request touches no balance and writes no ledger entry.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (the Hub form's `submission_token`). A retry with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the original answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and never creates or charges twice; the same key with another body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. The result email still goes to `notify_email`. Certificates are personal data and are kept by Healthier Business to verify the request. The key needs the scope `training-verification:write`, which also grants `training-verification:read`.

credits.description: A free request (a regular account's `auto`) takes nothing. A charged request takes one verification credit (verification-only accounts), or its price from the older balance (net) or the money balance (net plus VAT), once. A shortfall is refused with `402 insufficient_credits`, nothing stored.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
`POST /verifications`: asks Hub to verify one training certificate. The certificate is a file upload (`multipart/form-data`,
field `certificate`) or, in a JSON body, base64 text (`certificate_base64` with `certificate_filename`). The types and the size
limit are those of the Hub form (`config/training-verification.php`). The form's `submission_token` is the `Idempotency-Key` header.

request_type.description: `auto` (Hub reads the certificate and matches it automatically) or `manual` (Healthier Business staff check it). What each costs: `GET /pricing`.

candidate_name.description: The candidate's name as it appears on the certificate. At most 255 characters.

agency_name_on_cert.description: The agency (training provider) named on the certificate. At most 255 characters.

notify_email.description: Where the result email goes. Optional: it defaults to the account's first verification notification address (`default_notify_email` in `GET /profile`); when the account has none, this field is required.

candidate_ref.description: Optional. Links the verification to one of your Hub candidates: their `candidate_ref` from the Hub core API. It must be one of your candidates, otherwise `422` on `candidate_ref`.

client_reference.description: Optional. Your own reference for this verification, at most 100 characters. Stored, returned on the verification and sent in every webhook for it. It is not required to be unique.

certificate.description: The certificate file, in a `multipart/form-data` request: a PDF, JPG or PNG up to the size limit in `GET /profile`. Send this or `certificate_base64`.

certificate_base64.description: The certificate as base64 text, in a JSON request (a `data:` prefix is accepted). Send this with `certificate_filename`, or `certificate` instead.

certificate_filename.description: The file name of the base64 certificate, with its extension (`.pdf`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg` or `.png`). Required with `certificate_base64`.

max_credits.description: The most this verification may cost, as its net price in pounds (the account's price for the request type in `GET /pricing`, VAT not counted; `0` allows only a free request). When the live price is higher the call answers `409 quote_changed` with the current price and stores and charges nothing. Optional.

operations.summary: List the events of a verification
operations.description: Returns the verification's timeline, oldest first, under public event names: `submitted`, `processing_started`, `sent_for_manual_review` (a manual request was passed to staff), `verified`, `not_found`, `failed`, `rejected`, `refunded` (with `amount_pence`), `retried` (the check was run again after a stall or by staff), `completion_email_sent` and `result_email_resent`. `not_found`, `failed` and `rejected` carry the public `reason_code`. Steps that are only internal (reading the certificate, matching, staff opening the file) are not listed. The list is short and fixed in order, so a `sort` is `422`; it is paged with `page` and `per_page` like every list. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

operations.description:
Lists the account's certificate verifications, newest first unless you sort, including those made in Hub. Each row is a verification as `GET /verifications/{verification}` returns it, except that `result.records` is null (read one verification for the courses found). Filters: `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `verified`, `not_found`, `rejected` or `failed`; repeat the parameter, `status[]=verified&status[]=failed`, for several), `request_type` (`auto` or `manual`), `candidate_ref` (must be one of your Hub candidates, otherwise `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`), `client_reference` (exact match on the reference you sent) and `created_from` / `created_to` (UTC days). `sort` accepts `created_at` (the default, latest first), `status` and `id`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

Use it to reconcile your own records, and the `training-verification.*` webhook events to hear about changes as they happen. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. The rows carry the candidate's name and email as you entered them: personal data.

operations.description: Streams the verification report as a PDF (`application/pdf`, an attachment, never cached): the page Hub keeps of the result (candidate, agency, dates and the courses found). It exists once the status is `verified`; before that, or for a `not_found`, `rejected` or `failed` verification, the answer is `409 report_not_available`. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. The report is generated from what is stored; nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: verification
parameters.description: The verification id (integer), from the `id` of `POST /verifications` or `GET /verifications`. Another client's verification, or an unknown one, is a 404.

operations.description:
Returns one verification in full: your request, its `status` (`pending`, `processing`, `verified`, `not_found`, `rejected` or `failed`), the `result` once the status is final, the `charge` and the times. Status mapping: Hub's `Completed` (a TDTA certificate confirmed against practical training bookings), `Verified` (set by staff) and `Sent` (the automatic check matched the candidate and the result email was sent) are all `verified`; `Pending` is `pending`; `Processing` is `processing` (a manual request stays in it until staff decide); `Not Found`, `Rejected` and `Failed` are `not_found`, `rejected` and `failed`. `result.matched` is true only for `verified`; `result.provider` names the agency whose training was found and `result.records` lists the courses found (title, `completed_on`, `expires_on` as UK dates, and `type` `e-learning` or `practical`): the same facts the result email shows, read when you ask, so a later renewal appears. For `not_found`, `rejected` and `failed`, `result.reason` holds a stable `code` (`file_unreadable`, `agency_not_found`, `candidate_not_found`, `ambiguous_candidate`, `ambiguous_agency`, `no_courses`, `tdta_not_found`, `tdta_not_passed`, `system_error`, `staff_rejected`, `cancelled_by_client` or `other`) and a fixed sentence, never staff or engine comments. `{verification}` is the verification id; another client's verification, or one that does not exist, is `404 not_found`.

Poll it only for one verification you are waiting on; for the whole account use `GET /verifications` or, better, the webhook events. The key needs the scope `training-verification:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: verification
parameters.description: The verification id (integer), from the `id` of `POST /verifications` or `GET /verifications`. Another client's verification, or an unknown one, is a 404.

operations.description:
Returns the public link that you give to candidates so that they can book a Virtual BLS Training session themselves on your account (the page where the candidate chooses a course, a date and a time and pays by card). `booking_url` is null when the account has no such link. A booking made through that page is a candidate booking: it is not made through this API, and it does not send webhook events to your endpoints because it belongs to no client account.

To book on behalf of a candidate through the API instead, use `GET /timeslots`, `POST /timeslots/hold` and `POST /bookings`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:account:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Cancels a paid booking that has not started. The booking changes to `cancelled`, the trainer, the trainer's calendar entry and the Zoom meeting are released, the candidate is emailed, and the webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.cancelled` is sent to your endpoints (with `status` `cancelled`, sent before any refund is made).

Refunds. When the session is more than 120 hours (five days) away the booking is refund eligible (`refund_eligible` is `true`) and is refunded automatically: a booking paid with a credit gets the credit back as a deposit in `GET /credits/transactions`, a booking paid from the balance gets the money back onto the balance, and a booking paid by card is refunded to the card. A booking paid by invoice has nothing to refund. When the refund is made the booking changes on to `refunded`, so the response can show `booking_status` `refunded` rather than `cancelled`. A refund that fails does not fail this call: the booking stays `cancelled` with `refund_eligible` `true` and is refunded by hand. Inside the 120 hours nothing is refunded and `refund_eligible` is `false`. A cancelled booking cannot be reinstated; make a new booking.

Errors. `409 conflict` when the booking cannot be cancelled: it is not paid yet (a `pending` booking for which a candidate has not paid cannot be cancelled here), it is already cancelled or refunded, or its session has already started. A booking of another account is `404 not_found`. This call does not take an `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat after the first succeeded answers `409 conflict`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Downloads the booking's certificate as a PDF file (the response is the file, not JSON; the file name is `bls_cert_{booking id}.pdf`). The certificate exists once the candidate has attended the session (`attendance` `attended`) and the training kit has been returned; until then this call answers `409 conflict`. `certificate_available` on the booking tells you in advance, and the webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.certificate_available` is sent when the certificate is announced after the candidate has also finished the e-learning modules.

A booking of another account is `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Books the slot you are holding for a candidate. This is the third step of a booking, after `GET /timeslots` and `POST /timeslots/hold`. Send the `hold_hash` of a live hold of your account, the `candidate_ref` of a Hub candidate of your account, the address the training kit is posted to, how the booking is paid for, and the agency contact. The attendee's first name, last name, email address, phone number and job role are not sent: they are taken from the Hub candidate (the job role is the candidate's first role). The booking is made exactly as the Bookings page of Hub makes it, for the course and the date and time of the hold, and the hold is used up.

What `pay_option` does. With `credits` one booking credit of the held course is taken from the account, with `balance` the price in pence is taken from the money balance (at your own rate if the account has one, otherwise the list price), and with `invoice` (or its older spelling `inv`) the booking is charged to the account by invoice at your own rate or the list price. In these three cases the booking is created `booked` with `pay_status` `completed` at once, and the response is the finished booking. With `candidate_pays` the candidate pays by card: the booking is created `pending`, the candidate is emailed a payment link, and the response carries the same link as `payment_url`. The booking becomes `booked` when the candidate pays. The link stops taking payment three days before the session, and an unpaid booking of this kind is never abandoned after an hour (which is what happens to an unpaid pending booking made on the Bookings page), but it is cancelled automatically when the session is five days away or less. Paying by card as the agency is not available through the API.

Side effects. A booking made with credits, balance or invoice sends the booking confirmation email and text message, exactly as the Bookings page does. The webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.created` is sent to your endpoints for every booking, and `virtual-bls-training.booking.confirmed` is sent when the booking is confirmed: at once for credits, balance and invoice, and after payment for `candidate_pays`. A trainer is assigned afterwards by the platform, the Zoom meeting details appear on the booking once the meeting exists (`virtual` is null until then), the training kit is sent to `address`, `city` and `postcode`, and the candidate's e-learning account is provisioned afterwards by a background job. The booking is not linked to the Hub candidate record itself: it matches the candidate by their HB Portal candidate id or email address.

Errors. `422 validation_failed` names the field in `details`: `hold_hash` when the hold does not exist, belongs to another account or has expired (hold the slot again); `candidate_ref` when it is not a candidate of your account or the candidate has no first name, no email address or no phone number, or a name the booking rules refuse (letters and spaces only), in which case fix the candidate with `PATCH /api/v2/hub/candidates/{candidate_ref}`; `pay_option`, `address`, `city`, `postcode`, `agency_contact_name` or `agency_contact_email` when missing or invalid; and `booking_fields.field_<id>` when an answer to a booking question is missing or not one of the allowed options. `422 booking_rejected` means the booking rules refused it, most often `That way of paying is not available for this booking.`: the account has no credit for the course, the balance is below the price, or invoicing is not open to the account or its credit limit is too low. Check `GET /credits` and choose another `pay_option`. When the hold's course can no longer be found the answer is also `422 booking_rejected`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and books nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

credits.description: Charged by this call, before it answers, when pay_option is credits (one credit of the held course) or balance (the price in pence from the money balance). Nothing is taken from either wallet for invoice or candidate_pays. A way of paying the account cannot cover is refused with 422 booking_rejected, not 402.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
The booking made with `POST /bookings`: a held slot booked for a Hub candidate. The attendee's first name, last name, email
address, phone number and job role are not part of the body: they are read from the Hub candidate named by `candidate_ref`
(the job role is the candidate's first role). The postal address is where the training kit is sent and is kept on the
booking. The key's scope is the permission.

hold_hash.description:
The hold to book: the `hold_hash` returned by `POST /timeslots/hold`. Required, at most 64 characters. The
hold must belong to your account and must not have expired (holds last 30 minutes), otherwise the call is
`422 validation_failed` on `hold_hash`. The course, date and time of the booking are those of the hold, and the
hold is used up by the booking.

candidate_ref.description:
The candidate the booking is for: their `candidate_ref` (a uuid) from the Hub core API, `GET /api/v2/hub/candidates`.
Required. It must be a candidate of your account that has a first name, an email address and a phone number,
and whose name contains only letters and spaces; otherwise the call is `422 validation_failed` on
`candidate_ref`. Their name, email address, phone number and first role are copied onto the booking.

address.description:
The street address the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 500 characters. It is kept on the booking
and is not part of the Hub candidate.

city.description: The town or city the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 255 characters.

postcode.description: The postcode the training kit is posted to. Required, at most 20 characters.

pay_option.description:
How the booking is paid for. Required. `credits` takes one booking credit of the course, `balance` takes the
price from the money balance, `invoice` (also accepted as `inv`) charges the account by invoice; all three
confirm the booking at once. `candidate_pays` leaves the booking `pending` and emails the candidate a card
payment link, which is also returned as `payment_url`. A way of paying the account cannot cover (no credit, a
balance below the price, invoicing not open to the account) is `422 booking_rejected`; any other value is
`422 validation_failed`.

agency_contact_name.description: The name of the person at your agency who is the contact for this booking. Required, at most 255 characters.

agency_contact_email.description: The email address of that agency contact. Required, a valid email address, at most 255 characters.

agency_email.description:
An email address at your agency that is kept on the booking as the agency email; some booking emails, such as
late kit notices, are copied to it. Optional, at most 255 characters. When it is left out, the account's
notification email address (`notify_email` in `GET /profile`) is used.

booking_fields.description:
Your answers to the booking questions of the booking form, as an object whose keys are `field_` followed by the
question id (for example `field_3`). Optional unless a question is required: a required question that is not
answered, or an answer that is not one of the question's allowed options, is `422 validation_failed` on
`booking_fields.field_<id>`. A question you leave out is stored as `N/A`. A list answer (a checkbox question)
is sent as an array of strings. The API has no call that lists the questions.

additionalProperties.description: The answer to one booking question: a string, or an array of strings for a checkbox question.

schema.title: VblsStoreBookingBody

operations.description:
Lists the Virtual BLS Training bookings of the account, newest session first by default. Each row carries the `candidate_ref` of the Hub candidate the booking belongs to (null when your account has no Hub candidate that matches the booking), the name on the booking, the course, the session start and end in UTC, the booking and payment status, the way it was paid, the price, attendance, the Zoom details and what you can still do with it (`can_reschedule`, `can_cancel`, `certificate_available`). The candidate's email address, phone number and job role are not returned: read them from the Hub candidate. Bookings that were abandoned (a pending booking that was never paid and was cleaned up) are never listed.

Filter by `status` (one or several of `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled`, `refunded`), `course_id`, `candidate_ref`, session date with `start_date_from` and `start_date_to`, booking date with `created_from` and `created_to`, `upcoming` and `past`, and `search`. Sort by `start_date`, `created_at` or `status` (prefix with `-` for descending). The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). A `candidate_ref` that is not a candidate of your account is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`, not an empty list. A `status` value that is not one of the known statuses is ignored.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `start_date`, `created_at`, `status`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-start_date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Free text, at most 100 characters. A booking matches when the text is part of the first name, the last name or the email address on the booking. The text is not split into words, so a full name such as `Jo Smith` matches nothing; search for one name.

parameters.name: start_date_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `start_date` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `start_date_to`.

parameters.name: start_date_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `start_date` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `start_date_from`.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only bookings with this booking status: `pending`, `booked`, `rescheduled`, `cancelled` or `refunded`. Send the parameter several times (`status[]=booked&status[]=rescheduled`) to match any of them. A value that is not a booking status is ignored, not an error.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: Only bookings for this course: an `id` from `GET /courses`.

parameters.name: candidate_ref
parameters.description: Only bookings of this candidate: their `candidate_ref` uuid from the Hub core API. A booking matches when its HB Portal candidate id or its email address is that of the Hub candidate. A uuid that is not a candidate of your account is `422 validation_failed` on `candidate_ref`.

parameters.name: upcoming
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only bookings whose session has not started yet.

parameters.name: past
parameters.description: Send `true` to return only bookings whose session has already started.

operations.description:
Moves a paid booking to another free timeslot of the same course. Send the new `date` and `time` in UK local time; the slot must be one that `GET /timeslots` lists as free (a slot has to be at least five days ahead and is not held, so you do not hold it first). The booking changes to `rescheduled`, keeps its price and way of paying, and the session start and end change. The trainer is released and a new one is assigned afterwards by the platform, the Zoom meeting is moved, the old calendar entry of the trainer is cancelled, and the candidate is emailed the new time. The webhook event `virtual-bls-training.booking.rescheduled` is sent to your endpoints. Nothing is charged by a reschedule made outside the late-change window.

The late-change window. Within 120 hours (five days) before the session a reschedule needs a flat fee to be paid first, which the platform sets (its default is 20 pounds). Until it is paid this call answers `402 payment_required` with a `payment_url` in the body: the candidate pays the fee by card on that signed page, and you then call this endpoint again, which then succeeds. This is a fee for the change; it does not take credits or balance. Outside the window there is no fee.

Errors. `422 booking_rejected` when the booking cannot be rescheduled: it is not paid yet (`pending`), it is cancelled or refunded, its session has already started, or the new slot is not free. The message says which. `422 validation_failed` when `date` or `time` is missing or malformed. A booking of another account is `404 not_found`. This call does not take an `Idempotency-Key`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:write`.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

schema.description:
The new slot for `POST /bookings/{booking}/reschedule`: a date and a start time in UK local time. The slot must be one that
`GET /timeslots` lists as free for the booking's course and at least five days ahead. No hold is needed.

date.description:
The new date of the session, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. Required. It must be a date on which the
time is free for the booking's course, otherwise the call is `422 booking_rejected`.

time.description:
The new start time, `HH:MM` in 24 hour UK local time (not UTC), exactly as `GET /timeslots` lists it.
Required.

schema.title: VblsRescheduleBookingBody

operations.description:
Returns one booking in full: everything `GET /bookings` returns for a row, plus the trainer (`trainer`, null until a trainer has been assigned) and `refund_eligible`, which is set when the booking is cancelled and null before. Use it to read the current state after a webhook event, to find the Zoom link and password, or to check whether the booking can still be rescheduled, cancelled or has a certificate.

A booking of another account, a booking that does not exist and an abandoned booking are all `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:bookings:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: booking
parameters.description: The booking id (integer).

operations.description:
Lists the Virtual BLS Training courses that can be booked: each course with its list price, the price your account pays under its own agreement and the length of the session. Only active courses are listed, in name order by default. The list is short and fixed, so one page holds every course.

`cost_inc_vat_pence` is the list price including VAT, in pence. `client_rate_pence` is your account's own rate in pence, or 0 when the account has none. The own rate is charged only when a booking is paid by invoice (`invoice`) or from the money balance (`balance`); a booking paid with a credit or by the candidate is charged at the list price. Take the course `id` from here for `GET /timeslots` and `POST /timeslots/hold`.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `course_name`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-course_name`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

operations.summary: Get the booking credits and balance
operations.description:
Returns what the account can pay for bookings with. `booking_credits` lists, per course, how many whole booking credits are left (one credit pays for one place on that course); a course with no credits left is not listed, so an empty list means that no course has credits. `booking_balance_pence` is the pay-as-you-go money balance in pence, and `currency` is always `GBP`. Credits are whole credits, not money.

Use this before you book with `pay_option` `credits` or `balance`: a booking that chooses a way of paying the account cannot cover is refused with `422 booking_rejected`. Credits and balance are bought and topped up in Hub, not through the API. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Lists the movements of the account's wallets, newest first by default: the booking balance (money, in pence) and one credit wallet per course (whole credits). Each row says whether it was a `deposit` or a `withdraw`, which wallet it touched, the amount (always positive; `type` tells added from taken out), whether it is confirmed, a description and, when the movement paid for a booking, the `booking_id`. A booking paid with a credit or from the balance takes one `withdraw` at the moment the booking is made, and a refund puts the credit or the money back as a `deposit`.

Filter by `wallet` (`booking_balance` or a course id such as `12`), by `type`, and by date with `created_from` and `created_to` (a date such as `2026-10-01`; the range runs from the start of the first day to the end of the last day in UTC). Sort by `id` or `created_at` (prefix with `-` for descending). A wallet value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page, not an error. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:credits:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Only movements of this wallet: `booking_balance` for the money balance, or a course id (for example `12`) for that course's credits. At most 100 characters. A value that matches none of the account's wallets returns an empty page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only movements of this type: `deposit` (money or credits added) or `withdraw` (money or credits taken out).

operations.description:
Returns the Virtual BLS Training account the API key belongs to: the Hub client id, the account name, the contact name and email address held for it, the address that receives booking notifications, and whether the account is active. Use it once after you connect, to confirm that the key points at the account you expect.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:account:read`, and the client must have a Virtual BLS Training account; without one every call of this portal answers `403 portal_unavailable`. Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

Reserves one free timeslot for 30 minutes so that nobody else can book it while you complete the booking. This is the second step: pass the returned `hold_hash` to `POST /bookings` before `expires_at`. The `date` and `time` you send are UK local time and must be a slot that `GET /timeslots` lists as free. The course must be active.

An account may hold one slot at a time. A second hold while one is still live is refused with `409 conflict`, and the error body carries the live hold in a top-level `hold` field (with its `hold_hash`), so you can either book it or release it with `DELETE /timeslots/hold/{hash}` and hold another. A slot that is not free, or a course that is not available, is `422 booking_rejected`. A hold that is not booked simply expires after 30 minutes and no longer blocks the slot. Nothing is charged, sent or emailed, and no webhook event is fired by a hold.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the original hold with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:holds:write`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A unique value you choose (a uuid is good, at most 255 characters) for this operation. Within 24 hours the same key with the same body returns the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and does nothing twice; the same key with a different body is `409 idempotency_conflict`.

schema.description:
The slot to hold with `POST /timeslots/hold`: a course, a date and a start time. `date` and `time` are UK local time, and the
slot must be one that `GET /timeslots` lists as free. The hold lasts 30 minutes and an account holds one slot at a time.

course_id.description:
The course to hold a slot for: an `id` from `GET /courses`. Required. An id that does not exist is
`422 validation_failed` on `course_id`, and a course that is not active is `422 booking_rejected`.

date.description:
The date of the slot, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. Required. It must be a date on which
`GET /timeslots` lists the time as free, otherwise the call is `422 booking_rejected`.

time.description:
The start time of the slot, `HH:MM` in 24 hour UK local time (not UTC), exactly as `GET /timeslots` lists
it (slots start every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 22:00). Required.

schema.title: VblsHoldTimeslotBody

operations.description:
Lists the start times that are free for one course, so that you can choose one to hold. This is the first step of a booking. Each row is a `date` and a `time` in UK local time (not UTC) and the course. Slots start every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 22:00 UK time. The first bookable day is five days from today, and the search looks `months_ahead` months beyond that (2 when you leave it out, up to 12). A slot is free when at least one trainer is free for the whole session and the slot is not already promised to another booking or held by another client.

Send `course_id` (required): an id from `GET /courses`; an unknown course is `422 validation_failed` on `course_id`. Send `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to see only one day. The list is paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25) and can be sorted by `date` or `time`. The list is a snapshot: a slot you see can be taken before you hold it, in which case `POST /timeslots/hold` answers `422 booking_rejected`. An empty list means that nothing is free in the window.

The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:catalogue:read`. Read only: nothing is changed, held, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `date`, `time`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-date`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: course_id
parameters.description: The course to list free slots for: an `id` from `GET /courses`. Required. An id that does not exist is `422 validation_failed` on `course_id`.

parameters.name: months_ahead
parameters.description: How many months ahead of the first bookable day (five days from today) to search, 1 to 12. When omitted the search covers 2 months. A value outside 1 to 12 is a `422`.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Only slots on this date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, as a UK local date. A date outside the searched window returns an empty list, not an error.

operations.description:
Releases a hold that you made with `POST /timeslots/hold`, so that the slot becomes free again at once. Use it when the candidate changes their mind before you book, or to replace a hold with another slot (an account may hold one slot at a time). Only a hold of your own account can be released; the hash of a hold that does not exist, has expired and been removed, belongs to another account or has already been booked is `404 not_found`. A booking that was made from the hold is not affected, and nothing is charged or sent.

The answer is `{ "data": { "hold_hash": "...", "released": true } }`. The key needs the scope `virtual-bls-training:holds:write`.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: The hold token returned when the place or timeslot was held.

operations.summary: List the deliveries of an endpoint
operations.description:
Lists the endpoint's deliveries, one row per event sent to it, newest first unless you sort: the event (`event_type`, `event_id`), the `status`, how many attempts have been made (`attempt`), the HTTP status your server returned (`response_code`, null when it did not answer) and when it was delivered. The `status` is `pending` (queued, no attempt yet), `retrying` (an attempt failed and another is scheduled), `delivered` (your server answered with a 2xx status) or `failed` (the last attempt failed, or the endpoint was off). Use the list to find failed deliveries to redeliver and to see why an endpoint is failing; the error text and the beginning of your response are shown on the Developer page, not in this list.

Filters: `status` (one of the four values above), `event_type` (an exact event name, `webhook.test` included) and `created_from` / `created_to` (when the event was queued; each bound is a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `id` (the default, newest first), `created_at` and `delivered_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25). Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`.

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read` (or `account:webhooks:own`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `created_at`, `delivered_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only deliveries with this status: `pending`, `delivered` or `failed`.

parameters.name: event_type
parameters.description: Only deliveries of this event, for example `online-training.course.completed`.

operations.description:
Sends the same event again to the same endpoint as a fresh series of attempts: same body, same `event_id`, same delivery id (`X-Hub-Delivery-Id`), new `X-Hub-Timestamp` and a new signature made with the endpoint's current secret. Because the `event_id` is unchanged, a receiver that ignores event ids it has already handled stays correct. Use it after you fixed your receiver, for a delivery that `failed`; it works on a delivery in any status, including `delivered` (the event is then simply sent a second time).

The answer only says the delivery was queued again (`{ "message": ... }`); the attempt counter goes back to 0, the status to `pending`, and the usual schedule applies (up to 5 attempts, 25 failed deliveries in a row switch the endpoint off). If the endpoint is switched off or has been deleted by then, the delivery fails at once with that message; switch the endpoint on first. A delivery that belongs to another client's endpoint, or to a different endpoint than `{webhook}`, answers `404 not_found`. Each call queues another series; there is no `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

parameters.name: delivery
parameters.description: The delivery id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries`.

operations.description:
Registers an address to receive the events you choose, from any portal, signed with one secret per endpoint. Typical sequence: `GET /webhooks/events` to pick names, this call, `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/test` to check your receiver, then verify `X-Hub-Signature` on every delivery (see the `webhooks` section for the algorithm and code samples).

The answer holds the `signing_secret` (`whsec_` and 48 characters): store it now, it is shown only once, here and when you rotate it. Everything else about the endpoint can be read again later. Send `name` (up to 100 characters), `url` and `events` (at least one); `is_active` (default true) and `timeout_seconds` (5 to 30, default 10) are optional. The address must be a full `https` URL of up to 2048 characters, with no username or password, that resolves to a public server: addresses on private networks, `http` and credentials in the URL are refused with `422` on `url`. Hub checks the address again before every delivery and does not follow redirects, so give the final address (a `3xx` counts as a failed delivery). Only events listed by `GET /webhooks/events` are accepted (`422` on `events.N` otherwise), and only events of a portal the calling key can read: a key with no scope for a portal, a wildcard key included, cannot subscribe to that portal's events (`422` on `events.N`).

Events of an area that needs manual approval (by default Occupational Health and DBS & Right To Work) are refused with `403 webhook_events_not_approved` until your client holds approval for that area: the body lists the `areas` and the offending `events`. Request approval in the Hub under API access; `GET /account/api-access` shows where you stand. Once approved, events of the area are sent; if staff later withdraw the approval, events of that area are no longer sent and the endpoint is kept.

`source` (`api`, the default, or `zapier`) says which tool made the endpoint; the Developer page shows it. `external_ref` (up to 191 characters) is your own reference for the endpoint, unique within the client, which makes the call idempotent: when an endpoint with the same `external_ref` already exists, no second endpoint is made and the call answers `200` with the existing endpoint, without a `signing_secret` (a secret is shown only when an endpoint is first created). A key that holds only `account:webhooks:own` and repeats an `external_ref` that belongs to an endpoint another key created gets `409 conflict` and nothing about that endpoint. A deleted endpoint gives its `external_ref` back.

Caps: a key may have at most 200 active endpoints that it created, and a client at most 500 active endpoints in all (the limits are set by Hub); beyond that the call answers `422` with a message on `name`. Switched-off endpoints do not count, and switching one back on is refused the same way when the cap is full.

From now on every matching event of the client is sent to the address, whatever portal it comes from; you can register several endpoints and an event goes to each one that picked it. Without an `external_ref` the call is not idempotent and does not take `Idempotency-Key`: repeating it creates a second endpoint with its own secret, so send an `external_ref` or list your endpoints before you retry after a lost answer. The answer is the endpoint plus `signing_secret` and `notice`, not wrapped in `data`.

With the scope `account:webhooks:own` instead of `account:webhooks:write` the key can create endpoints and afterwards read, change and delete only the endpoints it created itself; every other call on an endpoint another key created answers `404 not_found`. The endpoint remembers the key that created it, so an endpoint created by a key that is later regenerated or deleted can then be managed only by keys with `account:webhooks:write`.

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

schema.description: A new webhook endpoint.

name.description: A name to recognise the endpoint by, up to 100 characters.

url.description: The https address Hub sends events to, up to 2048 characters. It must be a full `https` URL to a public server: `http`, a username or password in the URL, and addresses on private networks are refused with `422` on `url`. Redirects are not followed.

events.description: The events to receive, each `{portal}.{event}` from `GET /api/v2/webhooks/events`; at least one. On an update this replaces the whole list. Each event must belong to a portal the calling key can read (a scope for that portal, or `*`); otherwise `422` on `events.N`.

is_active.description: False to create the endpoint switched off (or to switch it off on an update); true to switch it on, which on an update also resets the failure count. Default true when creating.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Hub waits for your server's answer, 5 to 30 seconds. Default 10; null on an update returns to the default.

source.description: On creation only: which tool makes the endpoint, `api` (the default) or `zapier`. Shown on the Developer page. Ignored on an update.

external_ref.description: On creation only: your own reference for the endpoint, up to 191 characters, unique within your client. Sending one that already exists does not create a second endpoint: the call answers `200` with the existing endpoint and no `signing_secret`. A key with only `account:webhooks:own` that repeats a reference held by another key's endpoint gets `409 conflict`. Ignored on an update.

operations.description:
Deletes the endpoint. No new event is sent to it from that moment, and deliveries that were still waiting for a retry fail with the message that the endpoint was switched off or removed (nothing more is sent to the address). The delivery history is no longer reachable through the API, and the signing secret stops being valid. A deleted endpoint cannot be brought back: create a new one, which gets a new secret. Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`, and deleting twice answers `404 not_found` the second time, so a retry after a lost answer is safe to treat as done.

To stop events without losing the endpoint and its history, use `PUT /webhooks/{webhook}` with `is_active: false` instead. The answer is `{ "message": "Webhook deleted." }`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

operations.description:
Lists the client's webhook endpoints, whoever created them (this API, the Developer page, or an import from an old portal API, which shows `imported: true`). A key with only the scope `account:webhooks:own` sees just the endpoints that key created itself; a key with `account:webhooks:read` or `account:webhooks:write` sees all of them. Newest first unless you sort. Each row shows the address, the events it receives, whether it is on, the timeout, the outcome of the last delivery (`last_delivered_at`, `last_response_code`) and `consecutive_failures`, so you can spot an endpoint that is failing before Hub switches it off. The signing secret is never included; only its first characters (`secret_prefix`).

Filters: `is_active` (`true` or `false`), `search` (part of the name or the address, at most 100 characters) and `created_from` / `created_to` (when the endpoint was created; each bound is a whole UTC day). `sort` accepts `id` (the default, newest first), `name` and `created_at`; prefix with `-` for descending. Paged with `page` and `per_page` (1 to 100, default 25).

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read` (or `account:webhooks:own`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The field to sort by, one only: `id`, `name`, `created_at`. Prefix with `-` for descending (`-id`). Without `sort` the list has a fixed order that is stable between pages. Any other value is a 422.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Matches the endpoint name or URL.

parameters.name: created_from
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or after this date: the start of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-01`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be after the matching `created_to`.

parameters.name: created_to
parameters.description: Only rows whose `created` date is on or before this date: the end of that day in UTC. Any date (`2026-10-31`) or ISO 8601 time. Must not be before the matching `created_from`.

parameters.name: is_active
parameters.description: `true` returns only active endpoints, `false` only switched-off ones. One of: `true`, `false`, `1`, `0`.

operations.description:
Creates a new signing secret (`whsec_` and 48 characters) for the endpoint and returns it once, in `signing_secret`. The old secret stops being valid at once: every delivery from now on is signed with the new one, including deliveries that were already queued and are waiting for a retry, because the signature is made when each attempt is sent. A receiver that still holds only the old secret will therefore reject them. Change the secret in your verifier first, or at the same moment, and keep the old one only until the in-flight retries (up to about 80 minutes) are done if you want to accept both for a short time. Rotate when a secret may have leaked, when someone who knew it leaves, or on a schedule.

The call is not idempotent: every call makes a new secret and invalidates the previous one, so do not retry it blindly after a lost answer (read the endpoint's `secret_prefix`, or just rotate again). The answer is the endpoint plus `signing_secret` and `notice`, not wrapped in `data`. Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

operations.description:
Returns one endpoint with its events, status, timeout and the outcome of its last delivery. `{webhook}` is the endpoint `id`. Another client's endpoint, a deleted endpoint and an id that does not exist all answer `404 not_found`, and so does an endpoint created by another key when the calling key holds only `account:webhooks:own`. The answer is the endpoint object itself, not wrapped in `data` (the webhook endpoints are the one place where a single resource is returned unwrapped). The signing secret is never returned here; use `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/rotate-secret` if you have lost it.

The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read` (or `account:webhooks:own`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged.

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

operations.description:
Queues one `webhook.test` event to this endpoint, so you can check your address, your firewall and your signature verification before real events arrive. The event has the standard envelope (`event_id`, `event_type` `webhook.test`, `occurred_at`) and a `data` of `message` ("HB Compliance Hub webhook test event") and `endpoint_id`. It is delivered whether or not the endpoint subscribed to it, only to this endpoint, with the same headers, signature, timeout and retry schedule as a real event, and it appears in the delivery list (`event_type` `webhook.test`).

The answer is immediate and only says the event was queued: it holds the `delivery_id`. Follow the outcome (the status, the HTTP status your server returned and the attempts) in `GET /webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries`. An endpoint that is switched off (by you, or by Hub after repeated failures) answers `422` with the code `webhook_inactive`; switch it on first. Another client's endpoint answers `404 not_found`. Each call queues a new event; there is no `Idempotency-Key`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

operations.description:
Changes the fields you send (`name`, `url`, `events`, `is_active`, `timeout_seconds`); fields you leave out keep their value. The rules are those of creating an endpoint, so a new `url` is checked the same way and `events` must name events from `GET /webhooks/events`. `events` replaces the whole list: send every event you still want, not only the new one. Events are also limited to portals the calling key can read (`422` on `events.N`); an endpoint that already holds an event the key could not now subscribe to keeps working until its `events` are changed. Send `timeout_seconds: null` to go back to the default of 10 seconds.

Adding events of an area that needs approval you do not hold is refused with `403 webhook_events_not_approved` (see Create a webhook endpoint); events the endpoint already held can stay in the list.

Switch an endpoint that Hub turned off after 25 failed deliveries in a row back on with `is_active: true`; doing so also resets `consecutive_failures` to 0. Fix the receiver first: deliveries that failed while it was off are not sent again on their own (use `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries/{delivery}/redeliver` for the ones you need). Turning an endpoint off (`is_active: false`) stops new events at once. The signing secret does not change; use `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/rotate-secret` for that. Another client's endpoint, or one that was deleted, answers `404 not_found`.

The same body repeated gives the same result, so a retry is safe. The answer is the updated endpoint, not wrapped in `data`. The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:write` (or `account:webhooks:own`).

parameters.name: webhook
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id (integer), from `GET /api/v2/webhooks`.

schema.description: The fields to change; fields left out keep their value.

name.description: A name to recognise the endpoint by, up to 100 characters.

url.description: The https address Hub sends events to, up to 2048 characters. It must be a full `https` URL to a public server: `http`, a username or password in the URL, and addresses on private networks are refused with `422` on `url`. Redirects are not followed.

events.description: The events to receive, each `{portal}.{event}` from `GET /api/v2/webhooks/events`; at least one. On an update this replaces the whole list.

is_active.description: False to create the endpoint switched off (or to switch it off on an update); true to switch it on, which on an update also resets the failure count. Default true when creating.

timeout_seconds.description: How long Hub waits for your server's answer, 5 to 30 seconds. Default 10; null on an update returns to the default.

operations.summary: List the events an endpoint can receive
operations.description:
Lists every webhook event Hub can send, grouped by portal (`key`, `label` and the `events` of the portal, each with its `event` name and a one-line `label`). Use the `event` names, such as `online-training.course.completed`, in the `events` list of an endpoint; any other name is refused with `422` on `events.N`. Each event is documented in full, with when it fires, its payload and an example, in the `webhooks` section of this specification. The test event `webhook.test` is not in the list: it is sent only by `POST /webhooks/{webhook}/test`, to the endpoint you test, and needs no subscription.

The list is short and fixed, so it is always one page that holds every group (`total` is the number of groups). The key needs the scope `account:webhooks:read` (or `account:webhooks:own`). Read only: nothing is changed, sent or charged. Rate limit: the key's hourly limit, as for every authenticated call.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to return, starting at 1. A page beyond the last returns an empty `data` with the real `total`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 100. Default 25. A value outside the range is a 422, never clamped.
